releases.title: LuminoCity Expands Its B2B Entertainment Business, Showcasing Immersive Experience Solutions at IAAPA Expo 2026
releases.body:
Bringing customized immersive light shows, animatronic dinosaur attractions, and end-to-end entertainment solutions to venues nationwide.

NEW YORK, Oct. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LuminoCity Festival (LuminoCity Inc.), an immersive entertainment company specializing in large-scale light shows, animatronic attractions, and themed entertainment, is expanding its business-to-business (B2B) offerings for zoos, botanical gardens, parks, and entertainment destinations. The company will present its capabilities at IAAPA Expo 2026, November 17–20 in Orlando, Florida.

Founded in 2018, LuminoCity has welcomed millions of visitors nationwide across 33 festivals in 16 locations throughout eight U.S. states. Its signature Holiday Lights and Dino Safari experiences feature immersive light displays, handcrafted Chinese lantern installations, life-sized animatronic dinosaurs, and interactive attractions that combine traditional artistry with modern technology and storytelling.

Through its "Powered by LuminoCity" partnership model, the company develops customized light festivals, illuminated attractions, and themed entertainment experiences tailored to each venue's landscape, audience, and goals. Services span concept development, creative design, fabrication, installation, technical operations, and marketing support, helping partners transform existing spaces into memorable destinations and introduce new seasonal attractions.

A recent example is "Illumi-Nature" at Brevard Zoo in Melbourne, Florida, presented in the Spring of 2026. The nighttime experience transformed approximately ten acres of zoo grounds with illuminated lantern displays inspired by animals, flowers, and mythical creatures, including pathways typically closed to visitors. LuminoCity will next launch a new project with Jacksonville Zoo and Botanical Gardens in early 2027, and is engaged with other like-minded collaborative partners for 2027 and beyond.

"Our vision is to become North America's most trusted partner for immersive, story-driven family experiences," said Xiaoyi Chen, CEO and Founder of LuminoCity. "We want to help venues transform places into destinations, spark imagination across generations, and bring communities together."

At IAAPA Expo 2026, LuminoCity invites attractions industry professionals to visit Booth S5400 to learn more about its customized immersive experiences and explore potential venue partnerships.

About LuminoCity Festival

LuminoCity is a dynamic light-art brand taking the creative journey from concept through design, manufacturing, and presentation. Our diverse, mission-driven team is inspired by the storied tradition of Chinese lantern making, drawing on its rich cultural heritage to create contemporary art that transforms imaginative ideas into stunning works of light and color. Our annual festivals include LuminoCity's Holiday Lights and Dino Safari, with exciting new themes to come.

Contact: press@luminocityus.com

releases.title: Music IP Holdings Launches "Click-Through" License Portal for AI Technology Companies
releases.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn., Oct. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Music IP Holdings, Inc. (MIH) today launched a "Click-Through License Portal" that lets AI technology companies license its patented technologies online in minutes. MIH is a leading AI innovation licensing and technology development company setting the standard for authorized AI generation involving existing and new content.

The first-of-its-kind, custom-designed "Click-Through License Portal" allows MIH to quickly and efficiently provide cost-effective patent portfolio licenses to select companies so they can obtain the "freedom to operate" within and across AI markets. The new portal is designed for both technology and content companies that need to license the MIH AI derivatives workflow, Super Fan, Stems and other related patents in the portfolio: https://app.musiciprights.com/company-info

Today's portal, offered to smaller companies through the MIH Strategic Innovation Partner (SIP) program, is separate from the licensing agreements with large content and technology companies that MIH began announcing in August.

"A great deal of work has gone into this process by our technology, legal and licensing teams. It represents a critical step in MIH's evolution in 2026. We are laser-focused on protecting content owners and accelerating licenses for AI companies, all while enabling standards and value in the marketplace," said Daniel Drolet, CEO of MIH.

MIH owns a patent portfolio built for the age of generative AI. The portfolio includes more than 28 patent families and more than 90 issued, allowed and pending assets that together claim the workflow by which AI generation services turn prompts of all types into finished outputs. That workflow runs from intake and interpretation of the request, through checks against rights holders' content rules, generation, and post-generation review and marking, to controlled delivery under authorization and payment.

"Copyright asks whether something was copied; the MIH patents ask how it was made," Drolet said. "The MIH portfolio covers those answers across all three major claim categories – methods, systems and software – so rights attach whether or not an output copies anything, and whether or not the output itself can be copyrighted."

The MIH protections are directed to content in general rather than a single medium, and are being commercialized across music, voice, motion pictures, video, imagery, animation, publishing, and character and franchise IP, as well as name, image and likeness (NIL).

The comprehensive portfolio protects both existing content and new AI-generated content while providing AI generation companies with a clear, licensed pathway to drive revenue and accelerate market growth.  www.musiciprights.com

KNOXVILLE, Tenn., Oct. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The end of the year is a time for reflection, so Regal's film team selected movies for November's Deep Cuts series that deserve a second look from moviegoers in a theatrical environment. Over time, these movies have developed a devoted following away from the big screen, and Regal wants to give these titles a one-day cinematic revival to enjoy as the filmmakers intended.

"Some of the most memorable moviegoing experiences come from films that dared to be different, even if audiences didn't fully embrace them during their original theatrical runs," said Brooks LeBoeuf, Senior Vice President of US Content at Regal. "With the Deep Cuts series, our film team has curated a collection of bold, unconventional and often overlooked films that have earned passionate followings. It's an opportunity to rediscover these stories, appreciate the creative risks behind them, and experience them the way they deserve to be seen."

Following its New York launch, PremierXTM plans to expand through a broader international rollout across North America, Asia and Europe, with future editions planned as part of a growing network of recurring live entertainment properties and flagship cultural events.

releases.title: New Jerry Garcia Music Arts Center Planned for the San Francisco Bay Area
releases.body:
Facility to Celebrate Grateful Dead Co-Founder's Musical Roots, Fine Art, and Conservation Legacy

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Jerry Garcia's family, in partnership with archival media management platform Starchive and project coordinator Christopher McCutcheon, today announced plans for the establishment of the Jerry Garcia Music Arts Center in the San Francisco Bay Area through Jerry Garcia Music Arts.

Conceived as far more than a conventional museum, the envisioned institution is designed as an active, living cultural center, preservation space, and creative hub. Dedicated to preserving and advancing the multifaceted legacy of the Grateful Dead co-founder, the facility will showcase Garcia's expansive musical catalog, fine art, community ethos, and enduring impact spanning the 1960s counterculture through today.

For several years, Jerry Garcia's family and Jerry Garcia Music Arts have explored meaningful avenues to share the rich catalog of historical and artistic materials carefully preserved within Starchive. Following the announcement of the Eyes of the World immersive experience project this past August, widespread enthusiasm and community interest served as the catalyst to formalize plans for this dedicated, permanent archival home in the Bay Area.

Reflecting Jerry Garcia's spirit of family and community, all Garcia family heirs are warmly welcomed to participate and share their personal family content, archival materials, and special mementos to be preserved and celebrated within the collection.

The center will feature a community-oriented, fan-accessible research library and physical archive housing rare memorabilia and historical artifacts, complemented by a modern digital preservation hub. To cultivate ongoing public participation, the center will also review and accept fan-donated materials.

Beyond Garcia's visual art and recordings, exhibitions will trace the diverse musical traditions that shaped his artistic journey-including Americana, blues, rock, gospel, jazz, country, folk, and world music. Galleries will also highlight landmark technological innovations pioneered by Garcia and his collaborators, notably historical innovations in live concert sound design.

"My father is recognized as one of the most culturally influential artists in history," said Keelin Garcia, co-founder of Jerry Garcia Music Arts. "It is a great honor to work with Christopher McCutcheon and the Starchive team of professional archivists in stewarding the preservation of his many artistic contributions for future generations."

Comprehensive plans for the facility encompass a state-of-the-art performance center and screening room for live music and film presentations, alongside special exhibition galleries dedicated to Garcia's fine art and instruments. The center will also host an Artist-in-Residence program supporting emerging and established creators in the recording and visual arts, accompanied by interactive environmental exhibits spotlighting Garcia's dedication to conservation-specifically his advocacy for coral reefs and rainforest preservation-supported by integrated charitable initiatives benefiting ocean preservation, music education, and the arts.

"Music and art naturally build community," said Manasha Garcia, Jerry's wife and co-founder of Jerry Garcia Music Arts. "In welcoming fan contributions and building an accessible archive, we honor the vibrant community that grew around my husband's commitment to creative freedom, live sound innovation, and planetary stewardship."

Additional announcements regarding architectural design, programming, and scheduled developments will follow as the project progresses.

About Jerry Garcia Music Arts

Jerry Garcia Music Arts supports and curates the creative works, recordings, and visual art of Jerry Garcia, continuing his mission of artistic integrity, community connection, and philanthropy. For more information, visit jerrygarciamusicarts.com.

About Starchive

Starchive is an archival media management platform built for artists, creators, and cultural estates to organize, protect, and share their media collections with future generations. Learn more at starchive.io.

releases.title: Kim Sledge Allen of Sister Sledge Calls on the Music Industry to Demand Congress Fund the American Center for Cures
releases.body:
Ahead of the Nov. 3 midterms, Kim Sledge Allen invites Taylor Swift, Lionel Richie, Barbra Streisand and artists everywhere to take #TheCuresPledge, unite a divided country and demand immediate action to cure disease

CHICAGO, Oct. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kim Sledge Allen of Sister Sledge, the group behind the 1979 anthem "We Are Family," today called on her brothers and sisters in music and the arts to join a national movement to cure disease. In a personal audio message, Sledge Allen asked artists and faith leaders, including Taylor Swift, Lionel Richie, Barbra Streisand, Cher, Barry Manilow, Celine Dion, Tyler Perry, The Weeknd, Pastor Jamal Bryant, Pastor John Hannah, and Jesse Duplantis, to take The Cures Pledge and urge every member of Congress and the White House to fund the American Center for Cures immediately.

"This is a time of a new movement, a movement for healing," said Sledge Allen. "I am asking my brothers and sisters in the music industry and the arts to come together, support this movement and speak to our politicians, our families, our churches and our communities. It's time for these diseases to be wiped out. We have the science, we have the minds, we have the heart, we have the hope, we have the faith, and we certainly have love for one another. We are family, and we're unity strong."

Sledge Allen also lends her voice to "Unity Strong," the American Center for Cures' song, featured on the campaign's website.

"The American Center for Cures is the opportunity for the music industry to lead the path forward to preventing and curing disease," said Lou Weisbach, co-founder of the American Center for Cures. "It's 'We Are the World' on steroids: a fully funded, business-like, accountable and urgent mission that brings together, for the first time in American history, every element needed to prevent and cure disease, including the great talents of our researchers and AI. But it can only happen if the American people stand up together and remind our leaders that members of Congress and the president work for us. The days leading up to Nov. 3 are a defining moment to heal America, physically and politically."

Founded in 1999 by Weisbach and Richard Boxer, M.D., the American Center for Cures is a bipartisan initiative calling on Congress to fund a national mission to prevent and cure cancer, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, diabetes, heart disease, ALS and other major diseases. With the midterm elections less than two weeks away, the organization is asking Americans to make curing disease the No. 1 bipartisan issue of this election.

The need is urgent. Alzheimer's, diabetes, heart disease and cancer cost the nation more than $1.1 trillion a year, according to the most recent estimates from the Alzheimer's Impact Movement, the American Diabetes Association, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the National Cancer Institute. The American Center for Cures' $750 billion plan, funded through U.S. Treasury bonds over six years, would cost less than the nation now spends on these four diseases in a single year.

Once funded by Congress, the American Center for Cures would launch 16 separate private-sector efforts. Fourteen would each be charged with preventing and/or curing a single disease, with a $36 billion budget. Two additional units would receive $108 billion each, one to fund all other diseases, including orphan diseases, and one to fund artificial intelligence efforts. The remaining $30 billion would be held as a reserve fund. Each effort would be led by proven business leaders working alongside leading scientists and physicians, with clear goals and accountability for results.

Sledge Allen and the American Center for Cures are asking artists, fans and families to take The Cures Pledge before Nov. 3: record a 10-second video saying who they're waiting on a cure for, ask three people by name to do the same and post it with #TheCuresPledge. Then send it to their U.S. representative, their U.S. senators and the candidates on their ballot. Every video joins the campaign's wall, where a famous name and a family member get the same space.

"Speak to your senators, speak to your congressmen, speak to your communities, speak to one another," Sledge Allen said. "We are a human family. It's time to be one in hope and in healing."

To hear Kim Sledge Allen's message, listen to "Unity Strong" and take the pledge, visit thecurespledge.org.

About the American Center for Cures

The American Center for Cures is a bipartisan initiative founded in 1999 by Lou Weisbach and Richard Boxer, M.D., to prevent and cure the major diseases of our time, including cancer, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, diabetes, heart disease, ALS, MS and mental illness. The American Center for Cures is a fiscally sponsored project of The Giving Back Fund, a 501(c)(3) public charity. Donations are tax deductible to the extent allowed by law. For more information, visit thecurespledge.org.

releases.body:
New mural installation by artist A'Darrius Hanible celebrates the country music star as part of the Congress of Country Music's growing public art initiative

PHILADELPHIA, Miss., Oct. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Country music star Lainey Wilson joined GRAMMY Award-winning artist Marty Stuart and community leaders Tuesday for the unveiling of "Wildflowers and Wild Horses," a new mural honoring Wilson in downtown Philadelphia, Mississippi.

"Lainey Wilson is not only a dear friend, but someone who understands the meaning of home," said Marty Stuart. "She knows that no matter how far life takes you or how high your dreams carry you, nothing can replace the people and places that shaped who you are. Lainey came here for this mural unveiling and her fundraiser performances for the Congress of Country Music on nothing more than a hug and a handshake. No contract, no formalities, just friendship, trust and a shared love for where we come from. That tells you everything you need to know about who Lainey Wilson is, and I am so thankful for her support of the Congress of Country Music."

Created by artist A'Darrius Hanible, the mural takes its name and inspiration from Wilson's hit song and celebrates an artist whose distinctive sound, storytelling and authenticity have helped shape a new generation of country music.

The unveiling is part of Marty Stuart's Congress of Country Music's ongoing public art initiative, which brings country music's history and cultural influence to life through murals honoring some of the genre's most recognizable artists.

Wilson attended the ceremony and addressed community members and fans gathered to celebrate the new installation.

"This mural is absolutely beautiful, and I'm so grateful the warm welcome I've received here," said Lainey Wilson. "I brought some of my Mississippi friends along for a little picking and grinning, and that's exactly what I want tonight to be about. A chance to step away from the craziness of everyday life, come together and celebrate the heart of country music. At the end of the day, country music is about storytelling, and there's nothing better than sharing those stories with good people."

The mural was made possible through the support of Aalwese Properties, Hill Real Estate, lafedericks.com, Brent and Annette Federick, and the Riviera Motor Hotel, whose contributions reflect the community's continued investment in downtown Philadelphia's growing arts and cultural landscape.

"Wildflowers and Wild Horses" joins a growing collection of murals throughout downtown Philadelphia honoring influential country music artists and songwriters. The initiative builds on the Congress of Country Music's mission to preserve the genre's heritage while creating new opportunities for residents and visitors to experience its enduring influence.

About Marty Stuart's Congress of Country Music

Marty Stuart's Congress of Country Music is the spiritual home of country music, committed to touching lives by sharing experiences through exhibits, education and performances that inspire dreams for generations. The Congress aspires to touch lives through a real diversity of offerings in an authentic place unlike any other. Unique live performances, exhibits which honor both legends and newcomers and substantial educational offerings reach audiences across the state and country. Major performing artists are regularly featured alongside a solid season of events, integrated with revolving exhibits in collaboration with the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum. Our educational offerings will touch all ages and can be accredited and recognized for their influence.

releases.title: TYGER AND UNIVERSAL MUSIC GROUP ANNOUNCE STRATEGIC LICENSING AGREEMENT FOR IMMERSIVE MUSIC EXPERIENCES ACROSS GAMING
releases.body:
UMG becomes the first-major music company to license TYGER's groundbreaking interactive gaming-focused music service, powering new ways for artists, songwriters and fans to connect and experience music through gaming

TYGER uses AI to power adaptive gaming soundtracks that bring the music fans know and love into real-time gameplay

SAN DIEGO and SANTA MONICA, Calif., Oct. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TYGER, the adaptive music platform built for gaming, and Universal Music Group (UMG), the world leader in music-based entertainment, today announced the first major-music licensing agreement that connects artists and songwriters from UMG's global roster to TYGER's gaming-focused music service.

Under the agreement, select licensed recordings from UMG's global recorded music and publishing catalogs will soon be available through TYGER's paid, on-demand subscription service, for personal immersive listening experiences during active gameplay. Additionally, some UMG recordings will also be available on TYGER's free, ad-supported streaming service.

Unlike traditional music services, TYGER is built specifically for interactive entertainment. Through a single subscription, players can enjoy their favorite music alongside supported games, with licensed tracks adapting in real-time to live gameplay, enabled through TYGER's patented technology. Because TYGER allows users to play music alongside existing games in this way, it creates a direct route for artists, songwriters and rights holders to reach gaming audiences, while giving players greater control over the music accompanying their gameplay.

Nick Venti, CEO and co-founder of TYGER, said, "Gaming is where the next generation spends its time, discovers culture and connects with friends, but music has never had a native way to reach those audiences. This agreement with Universal Music Group is an important milestone for TYGER and validates our vision for the future of music in and around interactive and digital experiences. Together, we're creating new opportunities for players, developers, artists, songwriters and rights holders alike."

Michael Nash, Chief Digital Officer & EVP at UMG, said, "At UMG, we have a well-established track record of exploring and developing new creative and commercial opportunities that enable our artists, songwriters and labels to better connect with music fans. We believe that music has a more integral role to play in gaming and through this innovative new licensing agreement with TYGER, our artists and their music will now be able to soundtrack personalized gameplay experiences and connect with millions of gamers and fans around the world."

The Universal Music Group relationship represents the latest milestone in TYGER's growth. TYGER is currently live with a library of more than 400,000 songs, primarily from independent artists. Following the addition of UMG content, TYGER plans to relaunch later this year with an updated ad-supported tier and subscription offering, as it continues to pioneer a new category for licensed music in gaming, bringing artists, labels, developers, fans and players together through a platform designed specifically for dynamic interactive entertainment experiences.

About TYGER

TYGER is the adaptive music platform for the gaming generation, bringing licensed music and interactive entertainment through proprietary adaptive technology and direct music licensing. Built to work across PC, console and mobile, TYGER enables users to play premium music alongside gameplay without requiring game studio integration, creating dynamic listening experiences that respond in real time to player actions and gameplay events.

The platform is currently available in closed beta across more than 20 gaming titles whose combined monthly audiences exceed 540 million players and is supported by a growing catalogue of licensed music from the world's leading rights holders. TYGER's patented adaptive engine is creating a new category for licensed music in gaming, connecting artists, songwriters and composers, labels, developers and players through a platform purpose-built for the next generation of entertainment.

About Universal Music Group

At Universal Music Group, we exist to shape culture through the power of artistry. UMG is the world leader in music-based entertainment, with a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content. Featuring the most comprehensive catalogue of recordings and songs across every musical genre, UMG identifies and develops artists and produces and distributes the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music in the world. Committed to artistry, innovation, and entrepreneurship, UMG fosters the development of services, platforms, and business models in order to broaden artistic and commercial opportunities for our artists and create new experiences for fans. For more information, visit www.universalmusic.com.

Universal Music Publishing Group (UMPG), the global publishing division of Universal Music Group, represents a world-class catalogue of songs inclusive of every genre. Headquartered in Los Angeles, UMPG has 48 offices in 41 countries. The company represents some of the world's most important songwriters and catalogs. UMPG is also a global leader in Classical & Screen, Christian/Gospel and Production Music. The company is the publisher of choices for film and TV studios, providing creative, sync licensing and administration services for companies including Universal Pictures, Warner Bros. Pictures, Lionsgate, MGM, Paramount, Disney Europe (and other territories), Viacom, Amazon, HBO, DreamWorks, DreamWorks Animation, Legendary Pictures, Mar Vista Entertainment, NBC and Sesame Workshop, among many others. For more information, visit https://www.umusicpub.com/.

releases.title: A Bronx Miracle, 55 Years Later: "The Sight Unseen" Premieres on MNN Lifestyle
releases.body:
"The Sight Unseen," a hybrid documentary-drama exploring a reported 1971 Bronx phenomenon involving a glowing Christian cross, makes its New York City television debut on MNN Lifestyle, bringing faith, family memories, and local history to audiences.

NEW YORK, Oct. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- "The Sight Unseen" will make its first television broadcast for the general public on Manhattan Neighborhood Network (MNN) Lifestyle on Sunday, October 25, 2026, at 7 p.m. ET, followed by an encore presentation on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at 9 p.m. ET.

Presented by Harlem Film House and produced by Perspexsion, this hybrid documentary-drama examines a reported 1971 Bronx phenomenon involving a glowing Christian cross through the lenses of religion, faith, spirituality, eyewitness testimony, and historical documentation. Its New York City television debut reflects the film's direct connection to the region's religious history, community heritage, and cultural memory.

Writer and director Shawn Antoine II first learned of the story in 2016, when his great-aunt described it during a hospital visit. His mother, Sharon Wilson-Antoine, was six-years-old when the cross reportedly appeared. Years later, at the Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture, he discovered a photograph of his mother, grandmother, and aunt published in The Amsterdam News, as part of Melvin Tapley's reporting on the phenomenon. Those family memories and archival discoveries became the basis for "The Sight Unseen."

More than 300 backers across the United States made "The Sight Unseen" possible for the New York City based production, raising $25,000 in one month. Local businesses donated food and space, while the production employed more than 60 Harlem community members as cast and crew, turning the family's account into a film.

releases.title: The Vilcek Foundation Announces the 2026 New American Perspectives Program at the Hawaiʻi International Film Festival (HIFF)
releases.body:
Presented in partnership with HIFF, the program spotlights five immigrant filmmakers through screenings and special events, including a master class with Academy Award® winner Ke Huy Quan

HONOLULU, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Vilcek Foundation, in partnership with the Hawaiʻi International Film Festival (HIFF), presents the New American Perspectives (NAP) program at the 46th edition of the festival, running on O'ahu from October 21–November 5, 2026.

NAP spotlights immigrant filmmakers, celebrating the powerful impact of diversity in contemporary cinema in the United States through public film screenings, Q&A sessions with filmmakers and actors, and a panel discussion. This year's NAP program will also feature a book talk and master class by Academy Award®-winning actor Ke Huy Quan.

A mainstay festival program for the past two decades, NAP welcomes a cohort of five foreign-born artists this year. The distinguished 2026 group includes featured filmmaker Quan (b. Vietnam) and four guest filmmakers: Henry Ian Cusick (b. Peru), Liz Sargent (b. South Korea), Alex Tarrant (b. New Zealand), and Michelle Zhou (b. China). This program represents the U.S. premiere of new films from Cusick and Tarrant. The program will also mark the debut of feature-length films by Sargent and Zhou.

"From stories of wartime bravery to period pieces set during cinema's Golden Age, this year's New American Perspectives program celebrates the humanity at the heart of filmmaking and showcases the importance of diverse voices in the craft," Vilcek Foundation President Rick Kinsel says. "The Vilcek Foundation is proud to continue our longstanding partnership with the Hawaiʻi International Film Festival and spotlight the ingenuity of storytellers from around the globe."

The 2026 NAP program is buoyed by two featured events. First, NAP's quartet of guest filmmakers take the stage for a panel discussion exploring both their creative journeys and how immigrant and Indigenous perspectives can challenge conventional narratives and democratize the film industry.

Second, Academy Award®-winning actor Quan hosts a book talk for his debut work, Never Say Die: A Memoir. Reflecting on his journey from childhood stardom to behind the camera and back again, Quan discusses his life, career, and the lessons from over four decades in film. A HIFF career achievement honoree, Quan will also lead a master class discussion following a screening of his classic film Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom.

NAP guest filmmakers will participate in Q&A sessions following select screenings. Filmmakers Henry Ian Cusick and Alex Tarrant will also participate in HIFF's Guest Filmmaker Program, which brings artists from around the globe into Hawaiʻi's K-12 classrooms.

"These five films show the power and depth of American storytelling today — and are informed by the remarkable journeys of the filmmakers themselves," Jean H. Lee, executive director of the Hawaiʻi International Film Festival, says. "We are grateful to the Vilcek Foundation for bringing us work that will inspire the next generation of filmmakers here in Hawaiʻi to tell their own rich and varied stories as well."

More information on the NAP program and participating filmmakers can be found below. Tickets to the NAP and HIFF46 can be purchased at hiff.org.

FEATURED EVENTS

New American Perspectives: In Conversation

Oct 26 | 6:00 p.m. HST | Honolulu Civil Beat, 3650 Waialae Ave, Suite 200, Honolulu, HI 96816

NAP guest filmmakers Henry Ian Cusick, Liz Sargent, Alex Tarrant, and Michelle Zhou unite for a discussion about their careers and the importance of diversity across the filmmaking landscape. This panel discussion is supported in part by Honolulu Civil Beat and will be held in its offices.

Never Say Die: Book Talk with Ke Huy Quan

Nov 1 | 11:30 a.m. HST | da Shop: books + curiosities, 3565 Harding Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Join Academy Award®-winning actor, HIFF career achievement honoree, and NAP featured filmmaker Ke Huy Quan for an intimate conversation celebrating his new book Never Say Die: A Memoir. Book signing to follow.

Born in Vietnam, Quan spent a year in a refugee camp before arriving as a refugee in the United States in 1979. Shortly after, he earned breakout roles in Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom and The Goonies before stepping away from acting to work behind the scenes in film production and stunt choreography. His acclaimed return performance in Everything Everywhere All at Once earned him an Academy Award, Golden Globe, Critics Choice Award, and Screen Actors Guild Award for Best Supporting Actor. Quan remains the only Vietnamese actor to win an Oscar.

Special Presentation and Master Class: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom

Nov 1 | 2:00 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Ke Huy Quan made his cinematic debut as the precocious Short Round in Steven Spielberg's 1984 classic Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom. Notorious for its gruesome imagery and outdated Orientalism, the prequel to Raiders of the Lost Ark remains a rollicking blockbuster. Join Quan for a film screening and master class on filmmaking following.

Los Vampires

Oct 26 | 7:45 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Oct 27 | 4:30 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Henry Ian Cusick stars in this meta-horror set in 1930s Hollywood. Carlos Villarías (Cusick) is hired to play Dracula in the Spanish-language production, filming overnight on the same soundstages as the English-language movie featuring Bela Lugosi. Tensions mount as a string of murders on the darkened soundstage begins to blur the line between performance and possession. Los Vampires is in Spanish and English with English subtitles. The October 26 presentation marks the film's U.S. premiere and will be followed by a Q&A with Cusick.

Cusick (b. Peru) is an actor, director, and filmmaker known for his work across screen and stage. Born in Peru, raised in Trinidad and Scotland, and now based in Hawaiʻi, Cusick trained at the Royal Scottish Academy of Music and Drama and began his career as a classical theatre actor. He earned a Primetime Emmy nomination for his turn as Desmond Hume on the serial mystery Lost. His extensive television work includes starring roles in The 100, Scandal, The Passage, and MacGyver. Cusick's short film, Dress, won Best Short Film at the Peace on Earth Film Festival and at HIFF33.

Take Me Home

Oct 24 | 6:00 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Oct 25 | 2:15 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Rooted in the real-life experiences of writer and director Liz Sargent and star Anna Sargent, Take Me Home follows Anna, a Korean American adoptee caring for her aging parents in a Florida suburb. When a devastating heat wave disrupts their fragile routine, Anna, her sister Emily, and their father Bob must confront an uncertain future. This intimate drama explores disability, family, and resilience with compassion and hope. The October 25 screening of Sargent's first feature-length film will be followed by a Q&A with the filmmaker.

Sargent (b. South Korea) is a Korean American adoptee whose award-winning filmmaking examines themes including adoption and family relationships. A writer and director with a background in choreography, she brings a unique visual and emotional sensibility to her storytelling, shaped by her experiences as the middle child of 11 siblings and her intersectional identity. Take Me Home premiered in the U.S. competition section of the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, where Sargent received the Waldo Salt Screenwriting Award. The film debuted globally at the Berlin International Film Festival, where it was presented as part of the Perspectives Competition.

Sgt. Haane

Oct 23 | 6:30 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Oct 30 | 3:15 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

On April 19, 1943, 28th Māori Battalion soldier Haane Manahi led a daring assault on the fortress of Takrouna in Tunisia, helping change the course of the North African campaign during World War II. Though recommended for the Victoria Cross, the honor was never awarded. Starring Alex Tarrant as Manahi, this powerful film directed by Tearepa Kahi explores courage, sacrifice, and the enduring legacy of a Māori hero whose amazing story continues to inspire generations. Sgt. Haane is in Te Reo Māori with English subtitles. A Q&A with Tarrant will follow the premiere screening.

Tarrant is an Auckland-born actor of Māori, Samoan, and Niuean descent. A graduate of New Zealandʻs national drama school, Te Kura Toi Whakaari O Aotearoa, Tarrant made his international feature debut in Night Raiders. One of the Pacific's most recognizable actors, Tarrant is best known for his lead role as Kai Holman in NCIS: Hawaiʻi, as Valandil in The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, and for television roles across New Zealand and Australia.

Oct 28 | 3:30 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Seeking to appease her seemingly perfect middle-class Chinese family, Lei brings a man home on New Year's Eve to pretend to be her boyfriend. The unexpected appearance of her real girlfriend shatters this carefully constructed facade, and Lei finds herself caught between familial obligation, cultural expectations, and the desire to live authentically. Big Little Things is in Mandarin and Cantonese with English subtitles. HIFF represents Big Little Things' U.S. premiere, as well as Michelle Zhou's first feature-length film. A Q&A with the filmmaker will follow the first screening.

Zhou (b. China) is a Los Angeles-based writer and director whose work explores intimate relationships and shifting power dynamics. Zhou's short film, Fish Eye, won Best Short Film at the 46th USA Film Festival and her screenplay Under the Snow was a Sundance Screenwriters Lab semi-finalist. Her debut feature, Big Little Things, premiered in the Orizzonti section of the 83rd Venice International Film Festival. It won the WIP (Work-in-Progress) Activator Market Potential Award at the 62nd Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival and was presented at the 2025 Far East Film Festival as part of Udine's Focus Asia section.

BROOKLYN, N.Y., Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- In a powerful celebration of creativity, determination, and the limitless possibilities of the human spirit, 36-year-old Brooklyn native Amanda Ortiz born with Down Syndrome is making her musical debut with the release of Dear Amanda, an original album featuring songs written by Ortiz, with contributions from legendary American singer and songwriter Stephanie Mills.
releases.title: BROOKLYN SONGWRITER AMANDA ORTIZ BORN WITH DOWN SYNDROME RELEASES DEBUT ALBUM DEAR AMANDA
releases.body:
36-year-old songwriter brings her musical dreams to life with contributions from Grammy Award Winning Singer Stephanie Mills

BROOKLYN, N.Y., Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- In a powerful celebration of creativity, determination, and the limitless possibilities of the human spirit, 36-year-old Brooklyn native Amanda Ortiz born with Down Syndrome is making her musical debut with the release of Dear Amanda, an original album featuring songs written by Ortiz, with contributions from legendary American singer and songwriter Stephanie Mills. 

"Amanda is just a wonderful spirit and it's just amazing that she wrote these beautiful songs. I was on board with this project immediately. I'm raising a child with special needs. My son is 25 now, but I never bought into his disabilities. I think these children are very special," said Grammy Award Winning Singer Stephanie Mills.

In celebration of Down Syndrome Awareness Month, Dear Amanda is a testament to the power of perseverance and the audacity to follow your dreams. "Have faith in yourself, be brave and have the confidence to achieve your life long dreams," says Amanda Ortiz who wrote the songs after completing online courses at the College of Adaptive Arts in California.

Born with down syndrome, Amanda has always been interested in performing largely in part to her grandmother's love of jazz music. Her music is deeply personal and rooted in family influence. Writing and performing is something her grandmother instilled in her early on as a way to help Amanda reconnect with her Hispanic-Italian heritage. 

"She loves learning new things. Ever since she took this song writing class, she exploded," said Amanda's mom Linda Mandracchia. "This is beyond anything I would have expected. I didn't know anything like this would happen. Amanda just said she wants to be in the music business so this is all a surprise to me."

Amanda writes across a wide range of styles and themes, including jazz, Latin, pop, soul, blues, and country, with songs centered on love, grief, nature, joy, seasons , color, music, and dance—all expressed in her own voice.

The album was executive produced by musical composer Ira Antelis, best known for producing music for commercials, records, theater, movies, etc. Antelis has worked with such artists as Marc Anthony, Patti La Belle Christina Aguilera and B.B. King. 

"I think Amanda is an inspiration. The whole idea of people pursuing their dreams is why I was inspired to help bring this project to life," said Ira Antelis.

At a time when conversations surrounding inclusion and representation are more important than ever, Ortiz is helping redefine what is possible for artists with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

releases.body:
Creator-First Streaming Platform Opens Founding Memberships Ahead of November 16 Premiere of Its First Original Series, House of Ink.

NEW YORK, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Optix Network, a new premium streaming platform dedicated to original entertainment, independent storytelling and creator-focused opportunities, will officially launch November 1, 2026, introducing a fresh entertainment destination for audiences and content creators.

Designed to bring compelling stories and diverse programming to viewers, the platform will feature a growing catalog of original series, feature films and documentaries, with content from independent producers and established studios. Accessible across web, mobile and major connected TV platforms, Optix aims to deliver an entertainment experience that connects audiences with the stories and personalities they love.

"Our vision for The Optix Network extends far beyond launching another streaming service," said an Optix Network spokesperson. "We want to connect audiences with compelling entertainment while creating meaningful opportunities for independent storytellers to share their work, earn from their creativity and build lasting careers."

The network will introduce its first original series, House of Ink, premiering November 16, 2026, marking the beginning of an expanding slate of original programming. The unscripted series brings together familiar personalities Ceaser Emanuel, Sky Days, Spyder, Krystal Morales and Bux, navigating evolving businesses, relationships, personal challenges and new beginnings. Offering audiences an intimate look at ambition, reinvention and life beyond the spotlight, the series marks a new chapter for its cast.

House of Ink is the first of several planned original productions, complementing a broader entertainment library spanning scripted and unscripted series, independent films, feature films and documentary programming.

A NEW MODEL FOR INDEPENDENT CREATORS

Beyond its entertainment offerings, The Optix Network is developing a creator-focused distribution model designed to provide independent filmmakers, producers and production companies with additional opportunities to monetize their work.

Through a combination of licensing arrangements, performance-based royalties and potential profit-sharing opportunities, the platform aims to create new revenue streams for content partners while supporting the long-term growth of independent productions.

By connecting established entertainment personalities with emerging creative voices, Optix seeks to build a sustainable platform where compelling stories can reach broader audiences and creators can continue generating value from their work.

FOUNDING MEMBERSHIPS NOW AVAILABLE

Ahead of its November 1 launch, The Optix Network is introducing founding memberships, allowing early subscribers to secure introductory pricing and access exclusive content and experiences.

For an initial $1 payment, viewers can register as founding members, with monthly subscription billing scheduled to begin at launch. Founding subscribers will also receive early access to the House of Ink Season 1 trailer.

The network will offer three subscription tiers:

  • Ad-Supported — $4.99/month: Access to the Optix content library with advertising and streaming on one device.
  • Ad-Free — $6.99/month: An uninterrupted viewing experience across two devices, with regularly updated programming.
  • VIP — $13.99/month: Includes Ad-Free benefits, streaming on three devices, early access to select episodes, exclusive behind-the-scenes content, virtual cast Q&As, and opportunities for priority or discounted access to select premiere events. Additional founding-member benefits include a digital VIP badge and recognition on the network's Founders Wall. Limited to 5,000 Memberships.

Founding members are expected to retain their introductory monthly subscription rates under the terms of the founding membership offer.

The Optix Network launches November 1, 2026, with House of Ink premiering November 16.

Founding memberships are available at www.TheOptixNetwork.com 

View Sizzle Reel Here 

ABOUT THE OPTIX NETWORK

OPTIX Network is an independent streaming entertainment platform delivering original series, films, documentaries and independently produced programming across every major device. Combining premium entertainment with a creator-first model built on monthly royalties, licensing fees and profit-sharing, OPTIX connects audiences with compelling stories while giving independent creators new avenues to reach viewers and build lasting careers. The OPTIX app is available across major streaming devices and smart TVs — iOS, Android, Roku, Fire TV, Apple TV, Google TV, Samsung and more — or stream at www.theoptixnetwork.com.

releases.title: ELEC825 TELEVISION PROGRAM 'OUR INFRASTRUCTURE MATTERS' CELEBRATES FIRST-EVER NEW YORK EMMY AWARD NOMINATION
releases.body:
"NJ Roads Are Not Boring" Recognized in Public Affairs – Single Program Category

SPRINGFIELD, N.J., Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Our Infrastructure Matters, an internet and television program dedicated to showcasing the people, projects and industries that build and maintain our critical infrastructure, celebrated a major milestone with its first-ever New York Emmy Award nomination.

The program's featured segment, "Method to the Madness: NJ Roads Are Not Boring," was nominated in the Public Affairs – Single Program category, recognizing the television series' commitment to telling compelling stories about infrastructure and the skilled union workforce behind it.

The nomination was celebrated at the New York Emmy Awards ceremony held on October 10, 2026. While the program did not take home the award, earning a nomination alongside some of the region's leading television productions represents a significant achievement for the series and its production team.

"Receiving our first New York Emmy nomination is an incredible honor and a testament to the hard work and creativity of everyone involved in producing Our Infrastructure Matters," said Executive Producer Michael Makarski. "Our mission has always been to shine a spotlight on the skilled men and women who build, maintain and modernize the infrastructure we depend on every day. This recognition reinforces the importance of telling their stories."

The nominated segment, "NJ Roads Are Not Boring," takes viewers behind the scenes of New Jersey's transportation infrastructure, highlighting the engineering, innovation and skilled labor required to build and maintain the state's complex roadway network.

Through engaging storytelling and firsthand perspectives, the segment demonstrates that the roads millions of residents travel each day are anything but ordinary — representing the expertise, dedication and craftsmanship of the professionals responsible for keeping New Jersey moving.

"This nomination is particularly meaningful because infrastructure is something most people take for granted," added ELEC825 Director Mark Longo. "The goal of the program is to bring these projects to life, showcase the extraordinary work happening across New Jersey and give viewers a greater appreciation for the union workforce that quietly makes it all possible."

Presented by the New York Chapter of the National Academy of Television Arts & Sciences (NATAS), the New York Emmy Awards recognize excellence in television and digital media production throughout the region.

The historic nomination marks an exciting new chapter for Our Infrastructure Matters, reinforcing the program's commitment to educating the public about infrastructure investment, workforce development and the vital contributions of organized labor.

About Our Infrastructure Matters

Our Infrastructure Matters is a television and web program dedicated to highlighting the people, projects and investments that strengthen New Jersey's infrastructure. Through original feature stories, the program showcases the skilled Operating Engineer union workforce, innovative technologies and critical infrastructure projects that support the region's economy and quality of life.

Our Infrastructure Matters airs Saturdays & Sundays on News12 NJ+ and can be found online at https://www.youtube.com/@OurInfrastructureMatters or on https://tristateinfrastructurenews.com.

releases.body:
"LIVE FROM YEONNAM : HYUKOH" Brings Together Artists, Grassroots Venues and Local Communities in Seoul

  • Held on October 11 in Seoul's Yeonnam-dong neighborhood, featuring live performances, a block party and a music flea market
  • Brought together grassroots music venues, artists and local creatives as part of Marshall's global KEEP LIVE MUSIC ALIVE campaign
  • Drew an estimated peak attendance of approximately 1,350 visitors, bringing Marshall's MADE OF LOUD brand philosophy to the local live music scene

SEOUL, South Korea, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Marshall successfully concluded "LIVE FROM YEONNAM : HYUKOH," held on October 11 at Channel 1969 and the nearby Dongjin Market parking area in Seoul's Yeonnam-dong neighborhood. The event featured live performances by HYUKOH and other artists, alongside a music flea market and block party, highlighting the local venues and communities that contribute to live music culture.

"LIVE FROM YEONNAM : HYUKOH" was held as part of Marshall's global KEEP LIVE MUSIC ALIVE (KLMA) campaign. The initiative supports grassroots music venues and local music communities where emerging artists and new music cultures take shape, helping create an environment in which live music can continue to thrive. Through the event, Marshall brought together artists, venue operators, local creatives and audiences to share in the experience of live music.

Channel 1969, one of the event's main venues, is a grassroots live music venue that has worked with Marshall since the early stages of its local music initiatives in Korea. The venue hosted live performances by OYSTERS, SAILORHONEYMOON, Tiger Disco and HYUKOH. Meanwhile, the nearby Dongjin Market parking area hosted a music flea market and block party, with performances from Channel 1969 livestreamed to the outdoor space so visitors could enjoy the music both inside and outside the venue.

According to on-site attendance estimates, the event attracted up to approximately 1,350 visitors. Around 150 audience members attended the live performances at Channel 1969, while attendance at the Dongjin Market area increased after 6 p.m., reaching its highest level between 8 p.m. and 9 p.m. The event demonstrated how live music experiences can extend beyond a single venue to engage a wider range of local spaces and communities.

The event also marked the first local activation in Korea to bring Marshall's MADE OF LOUD brand philosophy to life following its introduction earlier this year. MADE OF LOUD reflects Marshall's longstanding connection to live music, artists, venues and music communities. Through this platform, Marshall is reinforcing its commitment to music culture and the people behind it, extending its role beyond consumer audio products.

"Marshall has stood alongside artists, music venues and music lovers for more than 60 years," said Issei Iimura, Head of Marketing, Korea, at Marshall. "Guided by the philosophy of MADE OF LOUD, we will continue to spotlight and support the people and places where live music begins and grows."

Following the Yeonnam-dong event, Marshall plans to expand its LIVE FROM series to other locations, music genres and online and offline communities. The series will form part of Marshall's continued KEEP LIVE MUSIC ALIVE activities, through which the brand aims to strengthen its collaboration with grassroots venues, artists and local music communities across Korea.

ABOUT MARSHALL GROUP

Marshall Group is the audio, tech and design powerhouse uniting musicians and music lovers through genre-breaking innovation. Marshall is uniquely positioned with over 60 years of rock 'n' roll attitude on stage, at home and on the go. Our iconic products are brought to life by a dedicated team of 800 passionate employees and sold in over 90 markets worldwide.

ABOUT MARSHALL AMPLIFY 

Marshall Amplify is Marshall's initiative to support grassroots music. Through the initiative, Marshall commits an amount equal to 1% of member purchases on marshall.com, starting with grassroots music venues. Learn more at marshall.com/amplify.

For more details contact your local press agency or visit press.marshall.com.

releases.title: Ballard and GeoPura put clean energy center stage in a hydrogen-powered summer of music and sport
releases.body:
Hydrogen power units supplied critical energy to everything from concerts and festivals to major golf tournaments

VANCOUVER, BC, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This year, GeoPura, a UK-based hydrogen power provider, recently acquired by Ballard Power Systems (NASDAQ: BLDP) (TSX: BLDP), made hydrogen integral to live entertainment. 

Powered by Ballard fuel cells, Hydrogen Power Units (HPU) deliver reliable electricity while cutting harmful air pollution near stages, production areas and crowds, protecting the health of artists, crews and attendees and improving air quality for surrounding communities. 

The Energy-as-a-Service offering combines equipment, hydrogen supply, transport, on-site storage and operational support, thereby giving organisers a fully managed power solution that meets production standards, while supporting a cleaner, healthier event environment. 

Having powered the HYDRO stage at Boomtown in 2025, GeoPura's HPU2 systems supplied the 20,000-capacity stage throughout the build and live festival in 2026, supporting the sound, lighting and visual production behind performances from Skrillex, Four Tet and Groove Armada. At Edinburgh Summer Sessions, HPUs were used to supply main-stage power and site infrastructure, embedding hydrogen into the delivery of a major concert series. These projects built on previous deployments at American Express presents BST Hyde Park, LIDO Festival and the Isle of Wight Festival. 

In sport, the Solheim Cup in the Netherlands (GeoPura's first continental European golf deployment) received critical power – without CO₂, nitrogen oxides or particulate emissions at the point of use – from hydrogen, which also powered infrastructure at the Genesis Scottish Open.  

This was the summer that saw even more repeat deployments, larger festival commitments and further integration into event power planning. Alongside GeoPura's established work in film, television and live broadcasting, GeoPura provided the combined business with an operating model for expansion into the US, Canada, Europe and wider international markets. 

Andrew Cunningham, President of Ballard, said: "This summer, hydrogen powered the performances, production and infrastructure that major events depended on. Organisers are incorporating it into their plans, returning for subsequent seasons and increasing the scale of their deployments. 

"Boomtown's move from HYDRO to HYDRO XL captures that progress. We're seeing the same shift in film and television, where customers need reliable power on location and want to reduce diesel use, noise and air pollution - clean power has become a requirement across these industries.

"Our ambition is for clean power to become the default across these industries. With Ballard's fuel cell expertise and international reach alongside our hydrogen supply and operational capabilities, we can expand this approach to more customers and markets." 

Marty Neese, Chief Executive Officer of Ballard, said: "GeoPura is already delivering power to customers, supplying the hydrogen and managing the service. Combining these capabilities with Ballard's technology and global reach broadens our offering and creates opportunities to capture value across equipment, fuel and operations. 

"The US and Canada offer exciting potential, from festivals and major sporting events, to film and television production. We can build on our UK experience to develop a complete service for these markets, while selectively expanding across Europe and North America. The same capabilities also serve construction, infrastructure and other customers facing grid constraints, alongside our established business in heavy-duty mobility." 

The combined business aims to make managed hydrogen power a mainstream choice across more sectors and markets. Its growing operations in events and screen production provide a base for international expansion, alongside longer-duration applications in construction, grid support and critical power, where customers need dependable electricity beyond the capacity of existing connections. 

About Ballard

Ballard Power Systems (NASDAQ: BLDP; TSX: BLDP) is a global leader in zero-emission hydrogen energy solutions and an integrated Energy-as-a-Service (EaaS) provider. Together, with its wholly owned subsidiary, GeoPura Ltd., Ballard delivers turnkey, vertically integrated hydrogen ecosystem solutions spanning hydrogen production, logistics, refuelling, zero-emission fuel cell engines, and stationary Hydrogen Power Units.

Ballard powers critical off-grid, stationary applications - including construction, events, film sets, healthcare, defense, temporary power infrastructure, and supplies fuel cell engines for heavy-duty mobility applications such as bus, rail, and marine. With an EaaS model, combined with cutting-edge technology across the hydrogen value chain, Ballard decarbonizes mission-critical operations worldwide. NEW YORK, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The  fourth annual Ukrainian Cultural Festival (UCF), presented by Razom for Ukraine, runs through Nov. 6  at venues across New York City, with 18 extraordinary events. The festival began Oct. 18 at Carnegie Hall with the U.S. premiere of Oleh Bezborodko's Steel, Violet, Rage—the first four-hands piano concerto by a Ukrainian composer. 

From Oct. 22–26, UCF presents a dedicated Cinema weekend at DCTV's Firehouse Cinema and QUAD Cinema:

  • Narrative & Documentary Screenings: Gar O'Rourke's Sanatorium (Ireland's 98th Academy Awards entry), Nice Ladies, Scream of My Blood: A Gogol Bordello Story, Silent Flood, Honeymoon, To the Victory!, and Cuba & Alaska.
  • Short Film Programs & Workshops: Docudays UA short films, Linoleum Fest animation, an XR immersive technology discussion, and an animation masterclass with Sashko Danylenko. Most screenings feature live filmmaker Q&As.

On Oct. 26, Teatro LATEA hosts scenes and discussion from The Reckoning, a London-born documentary-theater piece by DASH Arts based on war witness testimonies gathered by The Reckoning Project, ahead of its 2027 North American tour. A screening of Richard Nelson's More Beauty Than Sorrow, the final installment in his Lesia Ukrainka series, shows at The Public Theater, Nov. 4. 

UCF's literary programming (Oct. 28 – Nov. 1) highlights Ukrainian writers and translators:

  • Oct. 28: "Poet as Witness" featuring soldier-poets Yaryna Chornohuz and Lesyk Panasiuk, and translator Amelia Glaser, at Poets House.
  • Oct. 30: A panel on modernist playwright Lesia Ukrainka at the NYPL. Stage Directors Virlana Tkacz and Rory Pelsue lead the conversation.
  • Nov. 1: "Ukrainian Poetry Outburst" at Ukrainian National Home, featuring Gogol Bordello frontman Eugene Hütz and master bandurist Julian Kytasty.

UCF concludes Nov. 6 at Zankel Hall with a performance uniting the Chamber Girls' Choir of the M.V. Lysenko Kyiv State Lyceum and the Westchester Children's Chorus.

Razom for Ukraine is a leading U.S.-based nonprofit organization working to build a secure, democratic, and prosperous Ukraine. Founded in 2014, Razom ("together" in Ukrainian) supports urgent needs in Ukraine while investing in long-term solutions across health, civil society, advocacy, and culture. As Ukraine's future has global implications, Razom strengthens trauma care systems, supports local leaders and communities, and connects Ukraine to the world.

BCME shines a national spotlight on the educators, school leaders, families and community partners working to ensure students have meaningful opportunities to participate in music. releases.title: 28 Years of Championing Music Education: NAMM Foundation Opens 2027 Best Communities for Music Education Applications
releases.body:
CARLSBAD, Calif., Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The NAMM Foundation opens applications for the 2027 Best Communities for Music Education (BCME) Award, marking the program's 28th consecutive year of recognizing school districts and individual schools across the nation that prioritize music education as an essential part of a well-rounded education.

BCME shines a national spotlight on the educators, school leaders, families and community partners working to ensure students have meaningful opportunities to participate in music. By celebrating communities that make music education a priority, the program demonstrates the value of sustained investment in music learning and inspires other schools and districts to strengthen their own programs.

New for 2027, eligible BCME applicants will also have the opportunity to apply for the Dinah Gretsch Impact Award, which will provide awards of up to $5,000 each to as many as 10 schools and districts demonstrating financial need and a commitment to strengthening and sustaining music education.

Applications for the 2027 BCME program are open October 20, 2026, through January 5, 2027, at nammfoundation.org/bcme.

Recognizing Communities That Put Music First

Across the country, BCME honorees demonstrate how sustained investment in music education creates meaningful opportunities for students. Their work reflects a shared commitment among educators, administrators, families and community leaders to make music an integral part of the school experience.

From established programs with decades of recognition to first-time honorees expanding access and participation, these communities illustrate the many ways music education enriches students' lives.

Dinah Gretsch Impact Award: Extending the Impact of Music Education

While BCME recognizes communities for prioritizing music education, the Dinah Gretsch Impact Award offers an additional opportunity to support eligible schools and districts that demonstrate financial need and are committed to strengthening their programs.

In 2027, up to 10 recipients will receive awards of up to $5,000 each to help sustain and expand music education opportunities. Title I schools, districts with Title I schools, and non-public schools demonstrating financial need are eligible to apply through the BCME application process.

The award honors Dinah Gretsch and her enduring commitment to music education, access and the belief that music can create opportunity and connection for every student.

28 Years of Raising the Bar for Music Education

For nearly three decades, the Best Communities for Music Education program has provided national recognition for schools and districts that make music education a priority.

BCME honorees demonstrate their commitment through investment in music programs, access and participation, quality instruction, community engagement and sustained support. Their achievements show how schools and communities can work together to make music an enduring part of students' educational experiences.

By recognizing these communities, The NAMM Foundation celebrates what is working, elevates the importance of music education nationwide and encourages more school districts to invest in opportunities that help students learn, grow and thrive through music.

2027 BCME Key Dates

  • October 20, 2026: Applications open



  • January 5, 2027: Application deadline



  • Spring 2027: BCME honorees and Dinah Gretsch Impact Award recipients announced

School districts and individual schools nationwide are encouraged to apply and share how they are creating meaningful opportunities for students to learn, perform, create and connect through music.

Apply and learn more: Best Communities for Music Education

About The NAMM Foundation

The NAMM Foundation is a 501(c)3 public charity established in 2006, born from the National Association of Music Merchant's (NAMM) decades-long commitment to giving back. Since its founding, the Foundation has invested over $20 million to expand access to music making and music education for people of all ages.

SINGAPORE, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- JJ Lin, Tia Ray and Lil Ghost brought their distinctive sounds to the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix on October 9, 2026, energizing the evening's entertainment in Singapore with performances that brought music and motorsport together for a global audience. The appearances were part of Tencent Music Entertainment Group (TME)'s efforts to bring leading artists from the Chinese-language music scene to international stages.

Chinese R&B diva and acclaimed singer-songwriter Tia Ray performed signature tracks including "Love Herby" and "Beautiful Day", blending Eastern influences with international musical elements to highlight the distinctive sound and global outlook of Chinese R&B. She had recently headlined a solo show at the Grammy Museum, making her the first Chinese female singer to do so. Visionary singer-songwriter Lil Ghost performed material from his new album "KUI", staging the world live premiere of his track "Wild Card", backed by a full-band lineup and performing songs including "Saturday Night". His commanding stage presence energized the crowd. Together, the two artists showcased contemporary Chinese-language music through their distinct styles, drawing interest from music fans and motorsport enthusiasts around the world.

 

Asian pop superstar JJ Lin closed out the night on the main stage. After nearly six months of preparation, he brought together a 100-member international team for a 20-song show featuring three stage outfits and large-scale pyrotechnics. The set included the live debut of his new English-language single "RISE WITHOUT A SOUND". JJ also shared that he embedded secret snippets from his upcoming 2027 album within this performance, which he described as a miniature sequel to JJ20 Tour. A long-time Formula 1 enthusiast, JJ fulfilled his dream by performing at the race in his home country of Singapore, bringing his passions for music and motorsport together in one night.

The three artists enriched the event's entertainment lineup with a rich tapestry of Chinese‑language musical styles and live performances. Their appearances drew a positive response from both the artists and their fans. The participating artists expressed their excitement at taking the stage and how honored they felt to perform, with JJ describing it as a dream stage. Tia Ray's and Lil Ghost's sets generated widespread attention and discussion on Chinese social media, with many fans voicing their intent to travel to Singapore the following year to catch the shows and soak in the iconic Formula 1 race-weekend atmosphere. The enthusiastic fan reaction underscores music's potential to bridge artists, fans and major sporting events.

By combining motorsport with live entertainment, the Singapore Grand Prix gives audiences from different countries and regions an opportunity to discover a wide range of music. The collaboration gave artists from the Chinese-language music scene more opportunities to engage with international audiences. Leveraging the artists' reach and fan base, it has also stoked greater interest among Chinese music fans for the race and attending the event on-site.

Moving forward, TME will deepen its partnerships with the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix and other global collaborators, building on each artist's unique artistic identity across varied performance settings. These efforts will unlock more opportunities for Chinese-language artists to showcase their creations, exchange creative insights and forge bonds with global fans, while supporting partners to tap into China's music-loving audiences.
