releases.title: Experience Kissimmee Launches Film Kissimmee
releases.body:
The new Kissimmee Film Commission will promote diverse filming locations, support productions and drive tourism-related economic impact.

KISSIMMEE, Fla., Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Experience Kissimmee announces the launch of Film Kissimmee, the official film commission for Osceola County. The commission is created to attract film, television, commercial and digital media productions, showcase the destination's diverse filming locations and expand opportunities for the local tourism economy.

Film Kissimmee will serve as a central resource for production companies, location managers and digital content creators seeking filming opportunities in Central Florida. The initiative connects industry professionals with a wide range of filming locations, local expertise and production resources to help bring stories to life in Osceola County.

"This initiative reflects the hard work of a team that saw an opportunity and took meaningful steps to bring it to life," said DT Minich, President and CEO of Experience Kissimmee. "Film Kissimmee creates a direct connection between our community and an industry that can drive visitation, support local businesses and introduce new audiences to everything Osceola County has to offer."

Nick Floyd, Experience Kissimmee's Manager of Video Production and the new Director of the Kissimmee Film Commission, will lead Film Kissimmee and oversee efforts to position Osceola County as a premier destination for film, television and commercial productions.

"Just as Osceola County is an excellent place to spend your vacation, we truly believe it is a diverse location for film and television production. And Film Kissimmee is us exploring that intersection between the two," said Floyd. "I'm beyond excited to kick off this new initiative, not just as an opportunity to showcase so many of our incredible partners, but to welcome fresh perspectives on our destination from filmmakers and producers."

One of Film Kissimmee's greatest strengths is the remarkable variety of filming environments available throughout Osceola County. Within a short distance, filmmakers can access a diverse collection of landscapes and settings that capture many sides of Florida, including natural waterways, cypress-lined wetlands, historic downtown streets, ranchlands, hospitality properties and modern innovation centers. Adding to this versatility is Kissimmee's expansive collection of vacation homes, offering filmmakers unique and production-ready settings ranging from luxurious estates and themed properties to contemporary residences and resort-style retreats, each providing distinctive backdrops for film, television and commercial productions.

To support the initiative's launch, Experience Kissimmee partnered with a professional location scout with more than 20 years of experience. The scout identified and documented more than 100 potential filming locations across Osceola County. These locations are being added to an online directory powered by Reel-Scout, an industry-leading location management platform that allows filmmakers to search available properties, review photography and access production-related information.

Beyond attracting film and television projects, Film Kissimmee is expected to create meaningful economic opportunities for local businesses. Production crews often require accommodations, dining, transportation, equipment rentals, supplies and a variety of support services while filming on location.

Those expenditures can generate additional business for hospitality operators and local service providers while supporting Experience Kissimmee's broader mission of driving tourism-related economic impact throughout Osceola County.

Looking ahead, Film Kissimmee plans to continue expanding its location database, developing educational resources for local partners and coordinating familiarization tours for producers and location managers across the United States. These tours will provide industry professionals with firsthand access to Osceola County's filming assets while fostering relationships with local businesses and property owners.

For more information about Film Kissimmee, visit filmkissimmee.com.

About Experience Kissimmee:

Experience Kissimmee, the official tourism authority for Osceola County, Florida, is dedicated to creating economic opportunities by driving tourism to the region. With a vision to be a trailblazer in destination marketing, Experience Kissimmee promotes Central Florida's diverse tourism experiences to the world. By attracting leisure travelers, meetings and conventions and sports events, the destination welcomes more than 10 million visitors annually, generating more than $11 billion in economic impact and supporting more than 41,000 local jobs. Experience Kissimmee helps position the region as a premier global destination. For more information, visit www.experiencekissimmee.com. 

About Kissimmee

Located at the heart of Florida, Kissimmee is 25 minutes from Orlando International Airport (MCO), close to world-famous theme parks and attractions, offers a variety of shopping and dining locations and provides access to natural spaces and outdoor adventures. Also known as the Vacation Home Capital of the World®, Kissimmee has approximately 50,000 options of accommodations, including sprawling hotels and resorts and more than 30,000 vacation homes ranging from two-bedroom condos to 15-bedroom mansions.

releases.title: CPKC Holiday Train begins 182-stop journey of music and giving Nov. 19
releases.body:
CALGARY, AB, Oct. 13, 2026 /CNW/ -- Canadian Pacific Kansas City (CPKC) today announced the 2026 CPKC Holiday Train program will kick off Nov. 19 in Montreal, beginning a 32-day journey in support of local food banks through music, celebration and giving, with stops in 182 communities across Canada and the United States.

"Our railroaders take great pride in bringing the Holiday Train through hundreds of communities across our network to support people facing food insecurity," said CPKC President and CEO Keith Creel. "This year, we are going farther south than we ever have before, visiting 10 communities in Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Missouri for the first time.

"Through the generosity of the thousands of families and fans who come out to see the Holiday Train and support local food banks, whether for the first time or as part of a long-running holiday tradition, we can spread the joy of the season and support the giving spirit of the holidays," Creel added.   

Holiday Train Highlights

  • 182 live music shows in six provinces and 13 U.S. states. The Holiday Train will visit 10 communities for the first time, with new stops in Missouri (Blue Springs), Mississippi (Meridian, Jackson), Louisiana (Vicksburg, Monroe, Ruston, DeQuincy, Leesville, Zwolle) and Texas (Port Arthur).
  • Performers include American Authors, Magic!, Maris, Chase Rice, Madeline Edwards, Allen Stone, Jamie Fine, Shawnee Kish, Rafaëlle Roy, Tyler Shaw, Sam Roberts Band, and Owen Riegling.
  • Since 1999, more than $28.3 million and over 5.6 million pounds of food for community food banks have been collected in Canada and the U.S.

For 28 years, the CPKC Holiday Train has brought communities together to support neighbours facing food insecurity. Today, millions of people across Canada and the U.S. continue to rely on food banks for assistance, making community support more important than ever. CPKC encourages attendees to bring a cash donation or non-perishable food item, with all contributions staying in the local community to help families in need.

"There's nothing quite like the magic of the CPKC Holiday Train arriving in Edmonton, bringing our community together for great music and a great cause, and ultimately helping our neighbours in need," said Marjorie Bencz, executive director of Edmonton's Food Bank, where the Holiday Train will stop Dec. 13. "As the train lights up the night, every donation of food and funds helps us give food to our neighbours. We are so grateful for the warmth and generosity of Edmontonians who bundle up, show up, and make a real difference. Thank you, CPKC Holiday Train, for visiting and helping our community." 

For the musicians taking part, the CPKC Holiday Train represents more than a performance. It is a chance to connect with communities, share holiday cheer and support families experiencing food insecurity.

"The CPKC Holiday Train is one of the most special events of the holiday season! Not only are the lights and music spectacular, but it brings people together to give back to their communities and support friends, family, neighbours and those in need," said Zac Barnett of American Authors. "We feel so fortunate to take part in the celebration that makes such a meaningful impact."

"We are so grateful to be invited back on the CPKC Holiday Train," said Nasri Atweh of Magic!. "Not only do we get to see so many beautiful parts of the world, but we get to see all the smiling faces every time they open up the train doors and give everybody that came out there in the cold a little bit of warmth and some holiday cheer. It's always been my favorite time of year."

Follow the 2026 CPKC Holiday Train journey using #CPKCHolidayTrain and join the conversation online. For the latest tour updates, event information and announcements, visit CPKC's official social media channels on X, Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn. Be aware of fake accounts impersonating CPKC or the CPKC Holiday Train, and rely on CPKC's verified channels for trusted information.

CPKC reminds all music and rail fans to keep safety top of mind and stay 15 metres or 50 feet back from the tracks when taking photos/videos or viewing the Holiday Train. Never take a picture or video standing on the track or the ballast rock and always stand back from the locomotive and rail cars.

About CPKC

With its global headquarters in Calgary, Alta., Canada, CPKC is the first and only single-line transnational railway linking Canada, the United States and México, with unrivaled access to major ports from Vancouver to Atlantic Canada to the Gulf Coast to Lázaro Cárdenas, México. Stretching approximately 20,000 route miles and employing approximately 20,000 railroaders, CPKC provides North American customers unparalleled rail service and network reach to key markets across the continent. CPKC is growing with its customers, offering a suite of freight transportation services, logistics solutions and supply chain expertise. Visit cpkcr.com to learn more about the rail advantages of CPKC.

releases.title: MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM SEED FREEDOM ZERO Hits North American Theaters in February 2027; Teaser Trailer, Teaser Visual, and More Unveiled at New York Comic Con 2026
releases.body:
IRVINE, Calif., Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- At New York Comic Con 2026, Bandai Namco Filmworks Inc. took a trip down memory lane and provided insight into the upcoming installment of the GUNDAM SEED franchise during the "GUNDAM Showcase 2026 @ NYC - Feat. SEED FREEDOM ZERO" panel with the Japanese production staff and English voice casts of MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM SEED. Gundam series Executive Producer Naohiro Ogata and MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM SEED FREEDOM ZERO Planning Producer Kaori Shida were joined on stage by Matt Hill, Sam Vincent, and Matthew Erickson, the English voices of Kira Yamato, Athrun Zala, and Shinn Asuka. Those in the audience were the first to see a brand new teaser trailer for MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM SEED FREEDOM ZERO, announced to hit theaters across North America in February 2027.

Watch the teaser trailer: https://youtu.be/FEeahlHaGyk 

Assets are available here.

Executive Producer Naohiro Ogata took the stage first to briefly discuss the worldwide growth and fanbase of the Gundam series. Ogata commented on the many ways Gundam is being delivered to fans around the world, inviting fans to "enjoy Gundam life," with the new productions and events coming up to celebrate the upcoming 50th Anniversary of Gundam.

Next, Matt Hill, Sam Vincent, and Matthew Erickson greeted Gundam fans with a reenactment of a scene from the MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM SEED series. When asked to take a look at Gundam SEED Gunpla kits, Matt Hill mentioned becoming a fan of the toys later on, saying, "This is one of the coolest things I've ever seen."

Sam Vincent added, "I remember seeing the Justice Gundam and saying, 'That's me!' And these take me back."

Matthew Erickson is a self-proclaimed "Gunpla nerd," and went on to say that he spends a lot of time building and painting them.

The lights went down after the talk, and fans got a first look at an all-new teaser trailer for MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM SEED FREEDOM ZERO. The room filled with cheering Gundam fans excited about the film, set to premiere in North America in February 2027. Planning Producer Kaori Shida dove deeper into the plot of the film, explaining that the story is set between DESTINY and FREEDOM.

GUNDAM SEED FREEDOM ZERO was written by the late Chiaki Morosawa, and Shida mentioned that the script was created to dive deeper into the characters' feelings when FREEDOM was in production.

A new teaser visual was revealed, placing Shinn Asuka at the forefront, with Kira Yamato and Athrun Zala appearing behind him. Kaori Shida described the importance of the visual, saying that the focus on the red is a testament to Shinn's concept color. She expressed that this offers fans a look into what Shinn is feeling after the events of DESTINY.

All-new SEED FREEDOM ZERO products were unveiled. Four new Gunpla, including the Infinite Justice Gundam and Booster Unit, Murasame Kai, Gouf Ignited Custom, and Infinite Justice Gundam (SEED FREEDOM ZERO Vers.), were revealed along with figures of Shinn Asuka, Lunamaria Hawke, Leonard Valway, and Lacus Clyne.

Additionally, it was announced that Matt Hill, Sam Vincent, and Matthew Erickson will be back to reprise their roles in the English dub of MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM SEED FREEDOM ZERO. Each expressed their excitement in returning to the beloved characters.

Matthew Erickson said, "I am overwhelmed, you know? I feel amazing and I'm so thankful to all of the fans." Matt Hill agreed, also thanking the fans for making their return possible, and explaining that, "When a show ends, you think you may not get to do this again." Sam Vincent cheered, yelling, "It's an honor!"

releases.title: First Entertainment Credit Union and Nymbus Named 2026 Credit Union Times Luminaries Finalists
releases.body:
First Entertainment recognized for technology innovation with CineFi; Nymbus for consulting excellence

JACKSONVILLE, Fla., Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- First Entertainment Credit Union and Nymbus have both been named finalists in the 2026 Credit Union Times Luminaries Awards, which honor standout leadership and innovation across the credit union industry. First Entertainment is a finalist in the Innovation in Technology: Technology Project/Rollout category for launching CineFi, the first fully digital credit union built exclusively for entertainment industry professionals, in partnership with Nymbus. Nymbus is a finalist in the Consulting Excellence: Organizations category for helping credit unions turn growth strategy into live digital brands.

Since 1967, First Entertainment has served the people behind film, television and music. The credit union saw an opportunity in Atlanta, where the entertainment industry has grown rapidly but many of the professionals who power it still bank with institutions that weren't built around their work. Through CineFi, First Entertainment is bringing financial services designed for the industry to Atlanta's growing creative workforce. Nymbus delivered the technology, market strategy, and execution to bring the brand live, and co-developed tools that help members manage variable, freelance, and project-based income, along with a prospect portal that offers financial education before a person opens an account.

CineFi runs as a sidecar brand on the cloud-native Nymbus Banking Platform, parallel to First Entertainment's existing systems, so the credit union entered a new market with no branches, no disruption to current operations and no core replacement. Since launch, CineFi has acquired over 1,700 members with over $61M in deposits.

"Our members build careers project by project, and CineFi gives them a credit union designed around how they actually earn," said Stephen Owen, CEO of First Entertainment Credit Union. "Nymbus helped us move from idea to a live brand in a new market without disrupting the members we already serve. Sharing this recognition with them makes it even more meaningful."

CineFi is one of several brands Nymbus has taken from strategy to launch through vertical banking, a growth model that helps institutions go deeper into specific communities with purpose-built digital brands. Through Nymbus Labs, the company provides market research, segmentation, brand development and go-to-market execution, then supports each brand live on its own platform.

Nymbus is also preparing its clients for AI-ready banking. In April 2026, the company launched one of the first Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers purpose-built for core banking, giving AI a single, standardized and auditable connection to core functions with role-based access controls, PII masking and full audit logging, so institutions decide which tools are enabled and where human review is required.

"Being named finalists alongside First Entertainment reflects what we set out to prove: credit unions can grow by going deeper into the communities they know best," said Jeffery Kendall, chairman and CEO of Nymbus. "CineFi shows that the right platform and strategy, delivered together, can produce measurable results in weeks. We congratulate First Entertainment on this well-deserved recognition."

The CU Times Luminaries Awards winners will be announced Nov. 5 at the Luminaries Awards gala in Orlando, Fla.

About Nymbus

Nymbus delivers a cloud-based, highly extensible, full-stack banking platform, empowering community banks and credit unions to accelerate their growth and market positioning. Founded in 2015, Nymbus modernizes legacy core systems that support both brick-and-mortar operations and digital-first institutions, and facilitates the launch of vertical banking strategies or subsidiary brands with a sidecar Core alternative.

The Nymbus Banking Platform solution delivers the technology, people, and processes to scale as your financial institution grows. For more information, visit nymbus.com.

About CineFi

Launched in 2026 by First Entertainment Credit Union, CineFi is the first fully digital credit union created for film industry professionals and aspiring talent in Atlanta, Ga. With more than 50 years of entertainment industry expertise, CineFi delivers a future-ready banking experience designed to simplify financial management for those who live and breathe the craft. Offering premium financial products, competitive rates, and tailored financial education, CineFi empowers filmmakers—above and below the line—to achieve long-term success. Beyond banking, CineFi is committed to strengthening the entertainment and creative community by supporting industry nonprofits, schools, organizations, festivals, and events that advance the art and business of filmmaking. Visit www.cinefi.com.

releases.title: Introducing FinalFinal: A New Music Collaboration Platform Built for How Creators Work Today
releases.body:
The new platform brings communication, file management, feedback, and project organization into one secure, seamless workspace

SAN DIEGO, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FinalFinal, a next-generation music collaboration platform built for producers, artists, and creative teams who require a safer, smarter, and more seamless way to create together, today announces its official launch with its web platform. With the introduction of its web experience and a fully integrated mobile app coming in early November, FinalFinal sets a new standard for how music is shared, managed, and brought to life.

Built with the modern music creator in mind, FinalFinal is more than a file-sharing tool. It's a powerful, secure workspace that supports every step of the collaborative process. With real-time version control, time-stamped edits, encrypted storage, and intuitive sharing features, FinalFinal is the first platform to fully prioritize both creative flow and content protection.

At the heart of FinalFinal is its Chat UX–driven interface, allowing collaborators to communicate, share files, manage feedback, and track progress in real time, all within a single unified environment. The result is a more connected creative process, with conversations, files, feedback, and project activity all living in one place.

"Music has become more integrated than ever, but the way artists and producers collaborate is still fragmented," said Angel "AROCK" Castillo, Founder & CEO of FinalFinal. "Creative teams and artists have long had to piece together file-sharing platforms, messages, and email threads just to finish one song. FinalFinal brings those moving parts together in one place, giving creators a more seamless way to stay connected from the first idea to the final track."

The FinalFinal platform is strategically built to streamline the entire lifecycle of music creation. Unlike competitors, it combines:

  • Chat-Based Collaboration (Chat UX): Real-time conversations directly tied to files, versions, and project milestones - keeping all context in one place.
  • Integrated Project Management: Track sessions, assign responsibilities, monitor progress, and manage deliverables without leaving the platform.
  • Simple, Intuitive Interface: Designed for creatives, making it easy to onboard and use immediately.
  • Cross-Device Accessibility: A web experience available at launch, with a mobile app coming in early November to enable seamless collaboration across mobile and desktop from anywhere in the world.

The approach transforms FinalFinal from a tool into a workflow engine, giving creators clarity, speed, and control across every project. The platform includes core features such as:

  • Real-Time Version Control: Track every change, take, and edit with full visibility into contributor activity.
  • Time-Stamped Sessions: Automatically document creative progress and protect intellectual property.
  • Secure Cloud-Based Storage: Industry-grade encryption ensures assets remain protected at all times.
  • Smart Sharing & Permissions: Granular control over who can access, edit, or distribute files.
  • Unified Collaboration Environment: Replace scattered tools with a single, cohesive workspace.

"FinalFinal addresses the pain points everyday creators face – lost files, overwritten versions, and disconnected communication," Castillo added. "The platform puts creative control back in the hands of artists while giving teams the infrastructure to move faster and more confidently. Whether you're working in Los Angeles, London, or your bedroom studio, FinalFinal makes collaboration feel immediate, connected, and effortless."

Creators can sign up for a complimentary account at finalfinal.pro to gain early access to the platform. The FinalFinal mobile app is will be available beginning in early November.

For more information about FinalFinal, visit finalfinal.pro and follow @FinalFinal.pro on Instagram and @FinalFinal_Pro on YouTube.

About FinalFinal

FinalFinal is a music technology company founded by artists, engineers, and producers committed to redefining collaboration. Built for the fast-paced, always-on nature of modern music creation, FinalFinal delivers a secure, intelligent, and seamless environment where creativity can thrive without compromise.

HOLLYWOOD, Calif., Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fender Musical Instruments Corporation (FMIC) today announced the next evolution of American Professional, its flagship series of electric guitars and basses. Built around some of the most recognizable shapes in music - including the Stratocaster®, Stratocaster® HSS, Telecaster®, Hotshot™ Telecaster®, Jazzmaster®, Jaguar®, Precision Bass®, Precision Bass® V, Jazz Bass® and Jazz Bass® V - the refreshed series brings new player-focused design and performance upgrades to instruments that continue to shape how music is played and performed today.
releases.title: FENDER UNVEILS NEXT EVOLUTION OF ITS FLAGSHIP AMERICAN PROFESSIONAL SERIES
releases.body:
A Centerpiece of The One. For All., the Refreshed Series Brings Player-Driven Innovation to the Stratocaster, Telecaster, Jazzmaster, Jaguar, Precision Bass and Jazz Bass

HOLLYWOOD, Calif., Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fender Musical Instruments Corporation (FMIC) today announced the next evolution of American Professional, its flagship series of electric guitars and basses. Built around some of the most recognizable shapes in music - including the Stratocaster®, Stratocaster® HSS, Telecaster®, Hotshot™ Telecaster®, Jazzmaster®, Jaguar®, Precision Bass®, Precision Bass® V, Jazz Bass® and Jazz Bass® V - the refreshed series brings new player-focused design and performance upgrades to instruments that continue to shape how music is played and performed today.

Fender was built on original ideas - instruments designed from scratch that changed what music could sound like. Eight decades later, that commitment to original design, innovation and craftsmanship continues to shape how Fender builds, with American Professional representing the latest expression of that philosophy.

These are not interchangeable instruments. For generations, Fender's most iconic designs have carried distinct identities - shaped by their sound, feel and the artists who make them their own. From Strat players to Tele devotees, each has its own personality and fiercely loyal following across generations and creative communities.

The refreshed American Professional series honors that identity while continuing to evolve for the way musicians play today. Every update is rooted in the people who build the instruments, the experimentation behind their development and the player insight that helps Fender determine what to preserve, what to refine and what to rethink.

"You don't evolve an instrument like the Strat or Tele by changing things just to make them new," said Justin Norvell, Fender Chief Product Officer, Guitars and Basses. "We balance modern, useful improvements with the familiarity of what has made them iconic. In the same spirit as Leo Fender, we create tools for musicians by listening to what they need. We start with the players—how they're playing today, what they're asking for and where there's an opportunity to make the experience better. We put that insight in the hands of the designers, engineers and builders who know these instruments inside and out. American Professional is the result of that process: continuing to invest in original design, experimentation and craftsmanship while being thoughtful about what makes these instruments iconic in the first place."

Built For Today's Players

Handcrafted in Corona, California, the refreshed American Professional series lineup includes the Stratocaster®, Stratocaster® HSS, Telecaster®, Hotshot™ Telecaster®, Jazzmaster®, Jaguar®, Precision Bass®, Precision Bass® V, Jazz Bass® and Jazz Bass® V and introduces updates across the range designed to refine how these guitars and basses feel in the hand, respond under the fingers and hold up night after night, while preserving the character and identity that define each instrument.

Highlights of the new American Professional series include:

  • New V-Mod III pickups: Custom-voiced for balanced output, string to string note clarity, and a unique touch sensitivity. New V-Mod III single-coils in the Stratocaster, Telecaster, Jaguar and Jazzmaster, a redesigned V-Mod III Humbucking bridge pickup in the Stratocaster HSS for more push out of the bridge position, new Jazz Bass V-Mod III pickups and a new V-Mod III split-coil in the Precision Bass.
  • Redesigned bridges: Built for improved resonance and sustain, enhanced comfort, and solid stability. ClassicGear Radial bent steel saddles sit comfortably under the palm on the Stratocaster, the Telecaster runs a top-load or string-through bridge with ClassicGear™ compensated brass bullet saddles, the Jaguar and Jazzmaster pair a ClassicGear™ J-Bridge™ with a Panorama® tremolo for the full range of expressive vibrato, and both basses get a redesigned HiMass™ Modern Bridge for added resonance and sustain.
  • Advanced electronics: ClassicGear™ Precision™ Potentiometers offer improved taper and ideal tension while Push-Push tone controls on every guitar put extra voices one click away.
  • Necks that feel played in: A Deep "C" on the guitars, a Medium "C" on the Precision Bass and a Slim "C" on the Jazz Bass, every one with rolled edges that let the fretting hand move freely across the fingerboard.
  • Left-handed models coming Spring 2027: Fender will expand the American Professional Series with left-handed versions of the Stratocaster, Telecaster, Precision Bass and Jazz Bass.

"There are incredibly talented designers, engineers and builders behind every one of these instruments," said Edward "Bud" Cole, CEO of Fender. "They listen to players, test ideas and work through the details to make meaningful improvements for players. The American Professional series reflects that combination of player insight, experimentation and craftsmanship as we continue to push ourselves to make great instruments even better."

The One. For All.

American Professional serves as a centerpiece of The One. For All., Fender's broader campaign celebrating the artists, music and communities that continue to shape what Fender's iconic instruments become. Featuring Dinosaur Jr., Mike Kinsella of American Football, They Are Gutting a Body of Water, Lindsey Jordan of Snail Mail, Steve Gunn, Marc Ribot's Ceramic Dog, and Thurston Moore Group, the campaign brings together artists across generations and genres whose distinct sounds and creative approaches reflect the many possibilities within Fender's most recognizable designs.

Last month, Fender and Dinosaur Jr. brought that idea to life with The One. For New York., a series of intimate performances across New York City celebrating the artists, neighborhoods and communities that continue to shape music today. Go behind the scenes and watch the full film of The One. For New York. on Wednesday October 14th exclusively on Fender.com. 

"New York was the first place we came where we had any fans or acceptance. We just kind of gravitated towards New York," said J Mascis. "Starting a band I decided I wanted a Fender…I went to buy a Strat but they had a Jaguar for $200 and Jazzmaster for $300. The neck felt better on the Jazzmaster, it was worn in like a baseball bat so I just went for the Jazzmaster."

The One. For New York. is the first of several city-focused chapters of The One. For All., with The One. For London., The One. For Tokyo., The One. For Shanghai., and The One. For Sydney. planned for later this year and 2027. Each will celebrate the artists, venues and communities that make a city's music culture its own — and the people who continue to shape what comes next.

An Icon Is Only An Icon If People Keep Making It Their Own

At a time when music is created and shared in more ways than ever, the connection between a musician and their instrument remains deeply personal. Technology has opened up new paths into creativity, giving more people the ability to write, record and produce on their own terms, while a renewed appreciation for analog experiences is bringing the physical process of making something back into focus. For musicians, that can mean picking up an instrument, feeling its response and developing a sound through the hands-on process of playing.

That physical connection has long been at the heart of Fender's most recognizable instruments. From stages and studios to bedrooms and rehearsal spaces, they continue to be picked up by musicians developing their sound and finding new ways to express themselves.

The new American Professional series builds on that enduring relevance, bringing player-driven innovation to Fender's most iconic electric guitars and basses for the way musicians create today. The series reflects Fender's continued investment in evolving its original designs while preserving the character, feel and identity that have made them enduring favorites.

High-resolution lifestyle and product images can be found HERE.

For additional information on new Fender products and to find a retail partner near you, visit www.fender.com. Join the conversation on social media by following @Fender on all social platforms.

releases.body:
The R&B singer and songwriter continues his latest run of releases with "GOYARD," arriving October 16, featuring a new music video directed by PhillyFlyBoy.

ATLANTA, Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- R&B singer and songwriter Sammie continues his latest musical run with the release of his new single, "GOYARD," arriving Friday, October 16, 2026. Following the releases of "Old Alone" and "AYO," Sammie keeps the music coming with a new record accompanied by an official music video directed by PhillyFlyBoy, who also directed the videos for "Old Alone" and "AYO."

With a career spanning more than two decades, Sammie continues to evolve as an artist while maintaining his connection with R&B audiences. His latest releases demonstrate his ongoing commitment to creating new music and giving listeners fresh material to experience. Following "Old Alone" and the success of "AYO," "GOYARD" represents the next installment in this series of releases.

Sammie first captured national attention in 1998 after appearing on the television talent competition Showtime at the Apollo. In 2000, he released his debut album, From the Bottom to the Top, which achieved Gold certification from the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). The album established him as one of the young R&B voices to watch and laid the foundation for a career that has continued to evolve across multiple stages of the music industry.

After taking time to focus on his education, Sammie continued his recording career with his self-titled sophomore album in 2006. His subsequent projects include Indigo, Coming of Age, Everlasting, and Such Is Life. Through his evolving catalog, Sammie has demonstrated his longevity in R&B, continuing to release music and connect with listeners across generations.

Throughout his career, Sammie has also maintained a strong presence on the live performance circuit, sharing the stage with other established R&B artists and participating in major touring productions. In 2017, he joined Tank on the Savage Tour. In 2019, Sammie continued his touring activity with The Everlasting Tour. Sammie was also featured in The Millennium Tour in 2020, 2021, and 2024, performing alongside a lineup of celebrated R&B and Hip-Hop artists. He also toured with Eric Bellinger on the Vibes on Vibes Tour, adding another chapter to his live performance history and collaborative work within the genre. These appearances helped keep him connected with audiences across multiple generations and reinforced his place within the contemporary R&B landscape.

For "GOYARD," Sammie continues his creative partnership with PhillyFlyBoy, following their collaborations on the music videos for "Old Alone" and "AYO." The director returns to bring the new single to life visually, giving fans another opportunity to experience the collaboration between the singer and filmmaker. With "Old Alone" and "AYO" preceding the upcoming release, Sammie continues to build his current body of work one single at a time. "GOYARD" carries that progression forward, pairing his R&B artistry with a familiar creative collaborator and giving fans another release to experience. Their continued partnership connects the releases while allowing "GOYARD" to establish its own identity. "GOYARD" will be released by Star Camp Entertainment in partnership with Santi Music, and distributed by Vydia, a gamma company.

Throughout his career, Sammie has maintained a connection with the fans who have supported him through different stages of his musical journey. As he shares "GOYARD," he is expressing his appreciation for that continued support and inviting listeners to be part of the conversation surrounding his latest music.

"First and foremost, I want to thank my fans for the love and support you've shown me throughout my career. You've been with me through so many chapters of my musical journey, and I never take that for granted. I'm excited to share 'GOYARD' with you, and I'm really looking forward to hearing your feedback. Your continued support means everything to me, and I can't wait for you all to hear and see what we've been working on." — Sammie

Fans can follow Sammie on Instagram at @sammiealways for updates on "GOYARD" and its accompanying music video. "GOYARD" arrives Friday, October 16, 2026.

ABOUT SAMMIE

Sammie is an American R&B singer and songwriter whose career began in childhood. His accomplishments include a Gold-certified debut album, charting singles, songwriting contributions, and a diverse catalog of studio albums and independent releases. With a career spanning more than two decades, he continues to create music, perform live, and connect with R&B audiences worldwide.

ABOUT STAR CAMP ENTERTAINMENT AND SANTI MUSIC

Star Camp Entertainment is an independent record label owned by Sammie and working in partnership with Santi Music owned by his manager, Melinda Santiago. Their releases are distributed by Vydia, a gamma company.

COBOURG, ON, Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Celtic folk duo Lo & the High Road have released their sophomore album, 'Standing Stones,' a 14-track record that trades some of the whimsy of their debut for something noticeably darker, both musically and lyrically.

Written by Lauren Halász and Colin McMahon, the album reaches into Greek mythology and real historical darkness, with "The Weaver" reimagining Arachne's myth as a sea shanty, "God of the River" drawing on Book 21 of the Iliad to explore humanity's relationship with nature, and lead single "Salem" pulling directly from the Salem Witch Trials, pushing further into indie rock territory than anything else in the duo's catalogue. Still, pockets of light remain: "Canaries" reworks a bright Renaissance lute tune, and the duo's take on "Wild Mountain Thyme" honours one of the best loved folk melodies from Scotland and Ireland.

The title track began as Colin's idea for a song about community and platonic love, inspired by the Bronze Age monuments themselves, ancient structures whose original purpose remain unknown even to historians. "I have this idea that the earth remembers, even if people do not," Halász says, a thought that shapes the song's bridge and its bonfire gathering, built to feel flung back in time with help from guest musicians Saskia Tomkins on nyckelharpa, a Swedish keyed violin dating back over 600 years, and Steáfán Hannigan on uilleann pipes, Irish flute and whistle.

Based in Cobourg, Ontario, Lo & the High Road has built one of Canadian folk's most devoted followings, drawing coverage from Cashbox Canada, Tinnitist, Celtic Life International and Record World International across the singles leading up to this release.

Their 2023 debut, 'Jackalope Tales (& other stories),' has surpassed 2.8 million Spotify streams, and the band has amassed more than 200,000 social media followers worldwide, many of whom turn to their music for tabletop role playing soundtracks, woodland weddings and Renaissance faires.

A successful 2026 tour carried the duo, joined live by Dave Finneran, Christine Dando and Jordan Baldwin, from Toronto to Halifax, including stops at Port Hope's Cultivate Festival and Kingston's Ironwood Fantasy Fair, and 'Standing Stones' arrives ready to carry that momentum even further into the far ranging, myth-soaked world they've spent two albums building.

FORT ERIE, ON, Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fort Erie, Ontario blues and roots rocker René Huard has released his new single "Tail Waggin'," out now and giving fans their first taste of his forthcoming album 'Gently Used', arriving November 5, 2026.

The song traces back to an old bit of guitar-world folklore. René Huard explains: "Based on an anecdotal urban legend, jazz guitarist Wes Montgomery replied to a journalist's question, 'Do you find time to practice guitar while you're touring?' Wes quipped, 'I just open the guitar case every once and a while, and toss a chunk steak in.' Ding-a-ling-a-ling, went the Pavlovian songwriter bell in my brain. Life on the road, wearisome, tedious, sometimes perilous! Didn't B.B. King run into a burning building to save Lucille? Guitar man's best friend, sharp teeth and strings that bend."

"Tail Waggin'" leads into 'Gently Used', an eleven-track collection written and performed by René Huard on vocals, guitar and harmonica, produced by longtime collaborator Rick Taylor, who also contributes guitar and vocals.

On the road, and recording studio, Huard is backed by the Project band, featuring Rick Taylor on guitar and vocals, Jeff Muir on bass and Peter Griffin on drums, with special guest contributions to the record from: Chris Airyes and Thomas Nelson on vocals, Alistair Robertson on saxophone and Ed Roth on keys.

Huard's musical roots run four decades deep from his early days fronting the Meteors, who opened for blues heavyweights James Cotton, Long John Baldry and the Downchild Blues Band, and appeared at the first-ever Ottawa Blues Festival. He's also known to Canadian audiences as the former host of the television series Antique Hunter and Antique Style.

His previous album, 'Blues Calling', produced by Jack de Keyzer, climbed into the Top 20 on the Roots Music Report and held the number eleven spot for several months. Its lead single, "Hard Times," found its way to Holger Petersen's CBC Blues Radio Show, along with U.S. and international podcasts and campus radio playlists.

With 'Gently Used', René Huard adds another chapter to a career built on the road, in the clubs, and among the musicians who shaped him, proof that four decades in, the songs are still coming, and the guitar case is staying open for more than just steak.

MONTREAL, Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nearly four decades after they first plugged in together in Montreal, A Different Brand of Noise are releasing their second album, Far More Than Conversation, out now on all major streaming platforms, led by the single "Who Dares."

Guitarist Robert Ranaldi and bassist Ken Ashdown had already built careers before the band existed, Ranaldi through Secret Act and Man and Things, Ashdown through This "Blue Piano" and Ulysses Underwood. Both toured Canada and the UK, found campus and alternative radio success, and opened for major alternative rock acts. A chance meeting on a Montreal street reignited their friendship, and with drummer Gonzo, they quickly formed a power trio.

Writing and rehearsing quickly, they built a loyal following through packed Montreal shows. A demo recorded on an analog four-track in late 1987 surfaced as the bootleg Up, Tight, becoming a favourite on Montreal campus and alternative radio. After about a year and a half, university and steady paycheques won out, and the group quietly disbanded, leaving behind 10 songs that would not receive an official release for decades.

Ranaldi relocated to New York, Ashdown settled in Roberts Creek, BC, and Gonzo remained in Montreal. During the pandemic, Ashdown called his former bandmates, leading them to re-record their old material remotely. Relearning songs from rehearsal cassettes, teaching themselves audio production and Logic Pro, they traded files for three years until 19 songs were complete. The first 10 became the band's debut, Blurry, released in 2025.

Far More Than Conversation carries that identity into nine songs the band describes as being about sex, drugs and incipient societal collapse. "Who Dares" tackles income inequality and consumerism. "Do the Poor" grew from an overheard conversation among wealthy teenagers and closes with members of the Sunshine Coast Children's Choir. "Designs" traces back to a mushroom-fuelled afternoon, "She's the One" honours Ranaldi's childhood sweetheart, while "Pleasure Signs," "Falling Down Again II" and "Time Will Tell" salute the band's musical influences and enduring optimism. Touring remains on hold while the reunited trio balance music with careers in labour relations and behavioural neuroscience.

releases.body:
Spotify I YouTube I Website I Bandcamp I Facebook I Instagram I TikTok

BOSTON, Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- D-Tension & The Secrets have released their self-titled debut album, D-Tension & The Secrets, a nine-song set led by the single "Hate To See You Go." The record spans rock, alt rock, punk and power pop without settling into any one lane.

The band exists because of an unlikely pivot. D-Tension built his name internationally as a hip hop artist, touring with the late DMX, Ja Rule and the late Biz Markie, before a pandemic lockdown and a Fender Jazzmaster won in what he calls a shady Instagram contest pushed him toward rock and roll.

A producer known for work with Slug of Atmosphere, Blackalicious and Mr. Lif, D-Tension had grown up surrounded by rock records despite never playing guitar. YouTube lessons closed the gap quickly. By Christmas 2020 he was recording his own material, released the following year as Secret Rock & Roll Project, featuring Craig Silverman of Agnostic Front, Frank Pino of the Andrew W.K. band and Brian Viglione of Dresden Dolls and Violent Femmes. "Lockdown had its advantages," he says. "All I did that year was play guitar."

D-Tension, who is on the autism spectrum, has long described music as his superpower, carrying that confidence into his shift from rapper to rocker.

Once the world reopened, The Secrets formed in his hometown of Lowell, Massachusetts. A second album, Tales From The Pub, followed on Red on Red Records as the band entered the Rock & Roll Rumble, proving this was never a rap-rock project but one built on melody, hooks, harmony and storytelling.

Their new album is the first recorded fully as a band. Opener "Hate To See You Go" channels Boston's Irish punk tradition with echoes of Dropkick Murphys, Rancid and Flogging Molly, while "Banned," "Crime Spree" and "Violated" move through psychobilly, dark humour and hard rock. D-Tension calls it "your favorite hour of rock and roll radio."

"Hate To See You Go" honours friends D-Tension lost, including soul singer Lesley, who died during the pandemic before they could make a record together, as well as a beloved cat and a childhood friend. Rather than write an elegy, he turned grief into an Irish punk drinking song celebrating lives well lived.

D-Tension was inducted into the New England Music Hall of Fame in 2024 and has won two Boston Music Awards, a New England Music Award and a New England Urban Music Award.

NEW YORK, Oct. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Generative AI has made music fast, and the race in AI music is now about speed and volume. Pat Villaceran, founder of CITY JAM, says that race leaves one input untouched: original sound from human creators. Drawing that sound out of artists is both an art and a science. It is the craft behind INDUSTRY.AIFF, which takes a label's signed-but-unfinished artists to catalog-ready work and carries them through launch.

"When you stack up the progress around AI, it's all about speed, and about getting human creators back on track. That is an art and a science of its own," said Villaceran. "There are blueprints in it. Anyone can copy a blueprint: the roadmap, the pipeline, the scheduling and the workflows. But you cannot force the sound to come out if it has to be an original sound. The creativity is in how you bring out and evoke insights from musicians and creatives, and that is what CREATOR LABS and INDUSTRY.AIFF do. How you do that is the expertise we have at CITY JAM."

In tech terms, the blueprint is the easy part. A release plan can be written down and handed to anyone. Software can run it. The sound, Villaceran says, cannot.

The figures show how fast supply has moved. Luminate's 2025 Year-End Music Report counted 106,000 tracks a day reaching streaming services in 2025, up 7% on 99,000 a day in 2024. In 2025, 120.5 million of 253 million audio tracks had ten streams or fewer. That is almost half.

A growing share of that supply is not made by people. On Deezer, fully AI-generated tracks reached almost 75,000 a day in April 2026, roughly 44% of daily uploads, and passed 50% of new uploads at the June 2026 peak. Yet AI tracks are 1 to 3% of streams on Deezer, and up to 85% of those streams were fraudulent in 2025. On Deezer, the flood is in uploads, not listening.

The CISAC and PMP Strategy study projects that generative AI "could put 24% of Music creators' revenues at risk in 2028." That is a projection.

The US Copyright Office is now asking what that volume costs. Its inquiry into music streaming fraud names, in its Federal Register notice, "the dilution of the royalty revenue pool" as the primary harm, and asks which industry practices may be "inadvertently contributing to streaming fraud." Initial comments are due November 23, 2026, and replies December 21, 2026.

Detection and enforcement sit with regulators and the streaming services. CITY JAM's work sits earlier, in the stretch between signing an artist and a finished record. The royalty pool is diluted by volume without an audience. Fully finished, genuine releases are what the pool is for, and those still depend on an artist finding a sound of their own.

So if speed is no longer the hard part, what is music for? Villaceran's answer is the artist's own sound. It has to be drawn out of the musician. Then the speed AI brings can serve an original sound instead of replacing it.

INDUSTRY.AIFF does this for record labels and artist services companies. It works with their signed artists from unfinished work to catalog-ready releases, and stays with them through launch.

INDUSTRY.AIFF sits within the AI-era accelerator and incubator model for music that Villaceran launched on October 9, 2026, starting with record labels. Artists get the kind of support a startup accelerator gives founders. Education and professional development sit alongside community and live jam sessions. Collaborations and commercial opportunities come with it, and so does technology.

About CITY JAM

CITY JAM is holistic, end-to-end infrastructure for the music industry, built for everyone from independent musicians to record labels and artist services companies. It runs INDUSTRY.AIFF and CREATOR LABS with a global network of experts and producers, including CITY JAM New York. Pat Villaceran founded and leads CITY JAM. She also founded the innovation agency The MooVe, and has built innovation programs for companies and founders in Asia Pacific and the United States as well as in the United Kingdom and Europe. CITY JAM brings that record to music. INDUSTRY.AIFF is CITY JAM's program for record labels and artist services companies, and the name of its weekday letter for music label CEOs. CREATOR LABS is a holistic support system for independent musicians. It is a separate offering and is not part of INDUSTRY.AIFF. CITY JAM is a brand of HINABI PRIVE, INC. For updates, follow CITY JAM on LinkedIn.

releases.body:
Following its TIFF and VIFF premieres, the documentary heads to theatres across Canada

VANCOUVER, BC, Oct. 9, 2026 /CNW/ -- Network Media Group Inc. and Network Entertainment Inc. (TSXV: NTE) (OTC: NETWF) ("Network" or the "Company") are pleased to announce that Man In Motion: The Rick Hansen Story was honoured with gala premieres at the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) and the Vancouver International Film Festival (VIFF).

The film premiered at TIFF on September 11, where it received an honourable mention for Best Canadian Feature Film, followed by a hometown screening at VIFF on October 3 at the Vancouver Playhouse.

Adrian Buitenhuis directed the film, which was produced by Derik Murray and Ryan Reynolds, in association with Ryan Reynolds' Maximum Effort.

"We were thrilled to share the film with audiences at both TIFF and VIFF and were incredibly gratified by the response," said Derik Murray, Founder and CEO of Network Entertainment. "These festivals were the ideal venues to showcase the film and motivate potential global distribution opportunities."

The film draws on rare archival footage, original interviews and Rick Hansen's personal audio recordings to reveal the story behind one of the most remarkable athletic achievements in history. Rick Hansen, paralyzed from the waist down after a car accident, wheeled around the world to raise money and awareness for spinal cord research. The Man In Motion World Tour began in Vancouver on March 21, 1985, when Hansen was 27, and took him and his small team more than 40,000 kilometres through 34 countries over 26 months.

The Tour raised more than $26 million for spinal cord injury research and accessibility initiatives, helping to change perceptions of people with disabilities and build momentum for a more accessible and inclusive world.

The Rick Hansen Foundation, established in 1988 following the Tour, has continued this work, raising more than $435 million and advancing initiatives focused on improving accessibility and removing barriers for people with disabilities.

About the Rick Hansen Foundation

A legacy of Rick Hansen's Man In Motion World Tour more than 40 years ago, the Rick Hansen Foundation (RHF) is a registered charity that exists to remove those barriers and accelerate a global movement toward an accessible, inclusive and healthy world. We bring people and organizations together to turn innovative ideas into real-world solutions. Together, we're continuing Rick's dream of a world without barriers for everyone, everywhere. Visit www.RickHansen.com to learn more.

About Network Entertainment

Network Media Group is the parent company of Network Entertainment Inc.

Network Entertainment is a creatively driven production company that creates, finances, and produces award-winning film, television and digital content for audiences around the world. For more than two decades, Network has built a reputation for telling the stories of extraordinary and iconic international figures.

Network has earned international recognition for productions including Facing Ali, which was shortlisted for an Academy Award for Best Feature Documentary; SIDNEY, which premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival, was produced in partnership with Oprah Winfrey and was released globally on Apple TV+, earning a Critics' Choice Documentary Award for Best Biographical Documentary and a Black Reel Award for Outstanding Documentary Feature; and Sly Lives! (aka The Burden of Black Genius), a Peabody Award-winning and Emmy Award-nominated feature documentary, directed by Academy Award winner Ahmir "Questlove" Thompson. The film debuted at the 2025 Sundance Film Festival and premiered shortly after on Hulu/Disney+. Also, BRATS, a feature documentary directed by Brat Pack member Andrew McCarthy in partnership with NEON and ABC News Studios, had its world premiere at the 2024 Tribeca Film Festival, went straight to #1 on Hulu upon its release, and won the 2025 ASCAP Award in the Top Streaming Film category; and Man In Motion: The Rick Hansen Story, produced in partnership with Ryan Reynolds and his team at Maximum Effort, chronicled one man's extraordinary journey to break barriers and inspire global change. The film premiered at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival, where it received an honourable mention for Best Canadian Feature Film, followed by its hometown premiere at the Vancouver International Film Festival in October 2026.

Upcoming productions include a feature documentary on Jimi Hendrix, directed by acclaimed filmmaker Bao Nguyen in collaboration with Janie Hendrix and Experience Hendrix; and Bernie Taupin, directed by Matthew Miele.

For additional information on Network Entertainment Inc., visit www.networkentertainment.ca.

releases.title: A Piece of New England Music History Is Up for Grabs: Beloved JJ Hapgood Hits the Market
releases.body:
From Grateful Dead and Bob Marley Memorabilia to Its Starring Role in Baby Boom, This Legendary Peru, Vermont Gathering Place is Ready for Its Next Chapter

PERU, Vt., Oct. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Some places are restaurants. Some are general stores. And then there are places that become part of the cultural fabric of a community.

For decades, JJ Hapgood has been that kind of place.

Tucked into the heart of Peru, Vermont, the beloved destination has become known for its unmistakable music vibe, eclectic collection of rock-and-roll and jam-band memorabilia, and the sense that walking through its doors means stepping into a living piece of Vermont history.

Now, after years of building Hapgoods into a destination for locals and visitors alike, owners Leslie and Michael French say they are ready to hand the keys to a new owner.

And they aren't necessarily looking for someone to simply preserve what exists.

They are looking for someone who sees what could come next.

"We've had so much joy with Hapgoods," the Frenches say, while acknowledging that there is still enormous potential for the property, business and community surrounding it. They are already in serious conversations with a couple of prospective buyers interested in taking the space in a new direction, including more live music and events.

But nothing has been signed—and that means the door remains open.

Where the Walls Tell a Musical Story

Part of what makes Hapgoods unusual is that the experience begins long before the first bite or beverage.

The space itself is a tribute to music history.

Visitors encounter an extraordinary collection of concert posters and memorabilia representing some of the most influential artists and bands of the past several decades.

Among the pieces are a 1978 Bob Marley Greek Theatre Berkeley poster, described as a signed and accompanied by a certificate of authenticity; a Creedence Clearwater Revival Fillmore Auditorium concert poster, CGC graded 9.8; and a 1978 David Bowie Oakland Coliseum concert poster, PAE graded Mint "95."

And that's only part of the collection.

Phish, the Grateful Dead, Jerry Garcia, Trey Anastasio—classic rock, reggae and other legendary musical acts are woven throughout the space, creating an atmosphere that feels less like a traditional commercial property and more like a physical love letter to live music.

For music fans traveling through Vermont, the memorabilia alone can make Hapgoods worth a stop.

For entrepreneurs, the collection—and the community that has grown around it—offers something harder to replicate: identity.

A Hollywood Connection

Hapgoods also occupies a distinctive place in pop-culture history.

The Peru location was featured in the filming of Baby Boom, the 1987 film starring Diane Keaton, adding another layer to a property already steeped in Vermont and American cultural history.

That combination—music, film, community and place—is difficult to manufacture.

It has developed organically over time.

And that may be one of the most intriguing aspects of the opportunity now emerging in Peru.

A Vermont Institution Looking for Its Next Chapter

For Leslie and Michael French, the decision to sell is clearly bittersweet.

Hapgoods has brought them years of memories, relationships and experiences. But they also believe the space has more to give.

One of the prospective buyers currently in discussions with the Frenches is exploring a future with expanded live music and events, potentially building upon the energy that has already made Hapgoods a destination.

Nothing is finalized.

Which means, for the right entrepreneur, hospitality operator, music enthusiast, investor or creative visionary, there is still an opportunity to enter the conversation.

The question isn't simply what happens to a building in Peru.

It's what happens to a place that has already developed a following.

More Than a Real Estate Transaction

Across the Northeast, destinations like this have become increasingly difficult to create from scratch.

A new owner isn't starting with four walls and a business plan. They're stepping into a story that already includes generations of customers, travelers, musicians, moviegoers, collectors and music fans.

The next chapter could preserve the character that made Hapgoods special.

Or it could expand upon it.

Perhaps that's the most interesting part of the story.

JJ Hapgood is for sale—and the next owner could be the person who decides what the soundtrack sounds like. The Frenches are currently in serious discussions with a couple of prospective buyers but no sale has been finalized. Interested parties who want to explore the opportunity can still throw their hat in the ring.

The Rare Impact Fund Benefit: A Night of Radiance & Reflection, which will support youth mental health organizations, will take place on October 14 in Los Angeles

LOS ANGELES, Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Rare Impact Fund today announced the special musical guests set to take the stage at its fourth annual Benefit on October 14 at The Hollywood Palladium in Los Angeles. Artist Leon Bridges and artist and songwriter Bella Kay will perform at the event, hosted by Selena Gomez and emceed by Emmy and Tony Award-winning actor and comedian Sean Hayes. The Rare Impact Fund also announced this year's inaugural host committee and Rare level sponsors in support of the Fund's mission to mobilize $100 million for organizations that increase access to youth mental health services and education around the world.

Since launching in 2020, the Rare Impact Fund has raised over $30 million and supports 30 nonprofit partners across five continents, reaching 3.5 million young people annually. Last year's Benefit raised more than $2 million from over 20 sponsors and guests and was hosted by Jimmy Kimmel with performances from alternative pop band The Marias and Grammy-winning singer Laufey.

"I'm deeply grateful to every one of our amazing sponsors and to the extraordinarily talented Leon Bridges and Bella Kay for supporting our fourth annual Rare Impact Fund," said Selena Gomez, Founder and Creator of Rare Beauty and the Rare Impact Fund. "Shining a light on youth mental health is something we cannot do alone, and having their support not only inspires me, but directly touches the lives of millions of young people around the world."

The 2026 host committee brings together leaders, advocates and friends of the Rare Impact Fund who champion its mission of supporting youth mental health, including Brieane Olson, Chief Executive Officer at Pacsun; Johnese Spisso, Chief Executive Officer, UCLA Hospital System; Anne Wintroub, Head of Social Impact and Engagement at lululemon; Cindy Citrone, Founder and Chief Executive Officer at Citrone 33; Courtney Ciciora, Horejsi Charitable Foundation; Raquelle Stevens, author and producer; Becky G, singer, songwriter, and activist; benny blanco, Grammy Award–nominated producer, artist, actor and New York Times bestselling author; Matty Matheson, NYTimes Best-selling author and producer; Jay Shetty, a #1 New York Times Bestselling Author, Award winning host of On Purpose, and a purpose driven entrepreneur; and Radhi Devlukia, author, host of A Really Good Cry podcast and co-founder of Juni.

"Mental health advocacy is crucial and taking part in an event that creates real, tangible access to help for young people is an absolute privilege. Selena is setting a standard for how artists can use their platforms to drive real change, and I'm deeply honored to be a part of it," said artist Leon Bridges.  

"I'm honored to share the stage at Selena's Rare Impact Fund Benefit this year," shared artist and songwriter Bella Kay. "Music has always been an outlet for making sense of my own mental health and vulnerabilities so being part of an evening dedicated to expanding youth mental health support hits very close to home."

Thank you to this year's Rare level Sponsors who are supporting this year's Rare Impact Fund Benefit, including Rare Beauty, Afterpay, Batch & Box, lululemon, Pacsun, UCLA Health, and Ulta Beauty. releases.title: MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM SEED FREEDOM ZERO Coming to North American Theaters in February 2027, Announced at New York Comic Con 2026
releases.body:
IRVINE, Calif., Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Bandai Namco Filmworks Inc. today announced that MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM SEED FREEDOM ZERO, the newest film in the GUNDAM SEED series and a prequel to MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM SEED FREEDOM, is scheduled to open in North American theaters in February 2027. Matthew Erickson, Matt Hill and Sam Vincent will voice Shinn Asuka, Kira Yamato and Athrun Zala, respectively, in the English-language version.
 

The North American theatrical release window and English voice cast were announced during the GUNDAM Showcase 2026 @ NYC panel at New York Comic Con 2026, held at the Jacob K. Javits Convention Center in New York. A recording of the panel is available on the Popverse YouTube channel.

The film is a prequel to MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM SEED FREEDOM, which earned more than 5 billion yen and drew 3 million admissions to become the highest-grossing theatrical release in Gundam history. The teaser visual centers on Shinn Asuka, one of the main characters of MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM SEED DESTINY. Its screenplay was written during the production of SEED FREEDOM by series composition writer Chiaki Morosawa, Shigeru Morita and director Mitsuo Fukuda.

  • North American theatrical release scheduled for February 2027.
  • English voice cast announced: Matthew Erickson as Shinn Asuka, Matt Hill as Kira Yamato and Sam Vincent as Athrun Zala.
  • Teaser visual and new trailer released, together with comments from the Japanese cast and director Mitsuo Fukuda.
  • The MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM SEED Series Grand Prix 2026 fan vote opens Oct. 8, 2026 (PDT).

Watch the teaser here: https://youtu.be/FEeahlHaGyk

Assets are available here.

Story
After the collapse of the Destiny Plan proposed by Dullindal, which would have decided people's fates based on genetics, Cagalli, the chief representative of the Orb United Emirates, has been working to bring about a peaceful new order by establishing a global peace monitoring agency called COMPS (Pronounced Compass).

C.E.74. The great war is over, but Shinn has yet to decide what course he should follow. Then a mobile suit which has survived many past battlefields is transferred from ZAFT to COMPS's temporary base on Onogoro Island. That night, however, the Strike Freedom Gundam is stolen by persons unknown.

To stop the situation from escalating, to recover the stolen machine, and for the sake of everything they must protect, Shinn and his comrades once again throw themselves into battle...

Characters
Joining Shinn Asuka are Lunamaria Hawke, his academy classmate, and Agnes Giebenrath, who made her debut in GUNDAM SEED FREEDOM. Leonard Valway, who makes his first appearance in an animated work in this title, also joins the story.

Kira Yamato, Athrun Zala and Yzak Jule also return.

Shinn Asuka
Shinn joined ZAFT after losing his family during the invasion of Orb. He was used by Dullindal to oppose Kira and his comrades, but they were reconciled after the war. Shinn decided to join COMPS to seek a world without war, and is now training in Orb alongside the Archangel.

Lunamaria Hawke
A ZAFT pilot who was Shinn's academy classmate, and fought alongside him aboard the Minerva. Lunamaria is a reliable person with a strong personality. After the previous war, she decided to join COMPS along with Shinn. She still continues to watch over him closely as they train aboard the Archangel.

Agnes Giebenrath
A ZAFT pilot who was Shinn's classmate and Lunamaria's friend during their academy days. Known as the "Moonlight Valkyrie," Agnes plays a public relations role for the military. She visits Orb on a mission to transport the Strike Freedom and Infinite Justice.

Leonard Valway
One of the "Reds" who ranked in the top ten at military academy, Leonard is known as the "Raging Lion." He accompanies Agnes to Orb on a mission to transport the Strike Freedom and Infinite Justice.

Kira Yamato
Caught up in a war, Kira fought for the Earth Alliance Forces, but then became an independent force fighting alongside Lacus to end the conflict. He rejected the Destiny Plan and helped defeat Dullindal, but is now wondering what he should do to help a world which is still in chaos.

Athrun Zala
As a ZAFT soldier, Athrun found himself enemies with his childhood friend Kira, but came to realize the emptiness of hatred and chose to fight by Kira's side. After the war, he remained with the Orb forces. He also supports Cagalli with activities such as intelligence gathering as part of Terminal.

Yzak Jule
A ZAFT pilot who was Athrun's academy classmate, as well as his rival. Yzak is currently an intelligence officer at PLANT staff headquarters. He visits Orb on a mission to transport the Strike Freedom and Infinite Justice.

Mobile Suits
The Strike Freedom and Infinite Justice Gundam return from DESTINY, joined by a new mobile suit, the GOUF Ignited Custom. Further character and mecha details are available on the MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM SEED FREEDOM ZERO website: https://en.gundam-official.com/seed/freedom/

Japanese Voice Cast and Staff Comments

Kenichi Suzumura (Japanese Voice of Shinn Asuka):
To everyone who's loved and supported the Gundam SEED series for so long, thank you so much!
I'm really happy that we get to bring you a new story again after "SEED FREEDOM."

This time, it's the story of the time leading up to that one.
If you've seen "FREEDOM," I think you'll enjoy the characters' words and relationships all over again, from a different angle.
Personally, I'd still really love for you to keep an eye on Shinn! I did my best to put his earnest feelings and inner conflict into his voice.

Watch "ZERO" and you'll want to watch "FREEDOM" again. I'd be happy if that kind of fun spreads. Please go take in their story in theaters!

Soichiro Hoshi (Japanese Voice of Kira Yamato):
We had the recording sessions around the time "SEED FREEDOM" was in theaters, so I'm excited that it's finally getting released.
I felt nervous in all sorts of ways during "FREEDOM," but strangely, I'm feeling pretty relaxed this time.
I hope all the fans who've been waiting can enjoy it soon.

Akira Ishida (Japanese Voice of Athrun Zala):
Alright, everyone, now it's time for "ZERO"!
Thank you for the warm reception of "FREEDOM."
I'm sure some of you were left wondering what on earth happened between "DESTINY" and "FREEDOM." Well, "SEED FREEDOM ZERO" is here to answer all of that and put those nagging questions to rest. Don't miss it!

Daisuke Ono (Japanese Voice of Leonard Valway):
My connection to "GUNDAM SEED" goes back exactly 20 years, to "STARGAZER." Back then, I voiced Sven, a Natural in the Earth Alliance. This time, I'm playing Leonard, a Coordinator in ZAFT. Having experienced both sides, there's a perspective I can see now that I couldn't before. I'm so happy to be part of "GUNDAM SEED" again after all this time!

Director Mitsuo Fukuda:
"With 20 Years of Yearnings"
This is the final work completed by my late wife Chiaki Morosawa, the series composition writer. Until not long ago, I was halfway resigned to the idea that the screenplay might forever remain on the shelf, but now it has been actually made into a film thanks to the ardent support of all the fans. This story shows the characters' yearnings that Chiaki was so eager to depict, and links together "DESTINY" and "FREEDOM." I sincerely hope that everyone will enjoy it.

Recognition highlights Full Sail's industry-focused approach to preparing the next generation of music business professionals

WINTER PARK, Fla., Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Full Sail University has been named to Billboard Magazine's 2026 Top Music Business Schools list, recognizing the university's Music Business program for its hands-on approach to preparing students for careers across the evolving global music industry.

Recognition highlights Full Sail's industry-focused approach preparing next generation of music business professionals

For more than a decade, Billboard has highlighted institutions that are educating the next generation of music industry leaders, as well as artists and producers who recognize the importance of the business skills these schools teach. Billboard's 2026 list includes schools whose programs span areas such as music business, management, production, performance, publishing, and related fields.

"Being recognized by Billboard Magazine among its 2026 Top Music Business Schools list is a tremendous honor and a reflection of the exceptional talent, innovation and dedication of our students, faculty and alumni," said Garry Jones, President, Full Sail University. "Our university is committed to preparing the next generation of music industry leaders with the knowledge and skills they need to thrive in a rapidly evolving global entertainment industry. This recognition affirms the strength of our music business program and the extraordinary work happening across our university community."

Full Sail University's Music Business Bachelor of Science is designed around a project-based approach to learning and is available both on campus and online. The program prepares students to pursue opportunities throughout the music business, including artist development and management, music marketing, publishing, live events, streaming, and emerging music ventures. Students develop skills in areas including music business management, copyright and publishing, rights and royalties, artist development, marketing, distribution, data analysis, fan engagement, finance, leadership, and entrepreneurship. Coursework and projects are designed to place these concepts in practical, industry-oriented contexts.

As the music business continues to evolve through changes in technology, distribution, audience engagement, data, and emerging tools such as artificial intelligence, Full Sail's Music Business program combines foundational business knowledge with specialized music industry education. The program's curriculum is intended to help students understand both the creative and commercial sides of the music ecosystem while developing practical skills that can be applied across artist development, management, marketing, publishing, live events, and other areas of the industry.

Billboard Magazine's 2026 Top Music Business Schools list appears in the publication's October 2026 print issue and online. For more information about Full Sail University and its Music Business degree program, visit Full Sail University's official website.

About Full Sail University:

Full Sail University is an award-winning educational leader for those pursuing careers in entertainment media and emerging technologies. Founded in 1979, Full Sail has received numerous accolades throughout its over 45-year history, including most recently being named a 2026 "Top Game Design School" by The Princeton Review and one of "The 30 Best Film Schools in the U.S. and Canada" in 2026 by MovieMaker Magazine. Full Sail University is a graduate and undergraduate degree-granting institution offering on-campus and online degree programs in areas related to Art & Design, Business, Film & Television, Games, Media & Communications, Music & Recording, Sports, and Technology. With over 100,000 graduates worldwide, Full Sail alumni have worked on countless award-winning projects with individual recognition including Oscar®, Emmy®, Grammy®, Addy® and The Game Award honors.
