Super Girl Brings Free Women's Surf, Sports, Music and Lifestyle Festival to Jacksonville Beach Nov. 7-8

Super Girl's 20th Season Concludes with Elite Women's Surfing, 1,500+ Female Athletes Across 10 Sports and a Free Music Festival featuring 15 Artists

JACKSONVILLE BEACH, Fla., Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Following events in August and September, ASA Entertainment's Super Girl Surf Festival presented by Jersey Mike's will return to Jacksonville Beach Nov. 7–8 for the final stop of its milestone 20th season, bringing two days of women's surf, sports, live music, wellness and entertainment to the Jacksonville community. 

This summer, Super Girl celebrated its 20th year in Oceanside, California, and Virginia Beach, Virginia, continuing its longstanding mission to provide women in sports, music and entertainment with a platform to inspire, uplift and empower the next generation.

Now in its sixth year in Jacksonville Beach, this nationally televised festival will feature more than 1,500 female athletes across 10 sports, a World Surf League (WSL) women's competition, 15 live concerts and an interactive Festival Village featuring 16 free fitness and wellness classes, leadership panels, youth mentorship programs, a female art exhibition, local food and beverage vendors and more than 50 interactive brand activations. All competitions, concerts, classes and event activities are free and open to the public. 

"After two successful stops on the West Coast and in the Mid-Atlantic, the excitement heading into Jacksonville Beach is at an all-time high," said Rick Bratman, CEO of ASA Entertainment and Founder of the Super Girl Festival Series. "The level of female talent coming together across surfing, sports and music is remarkable, and we can't wait to bring that energy to Jacksonville as we close out an incredible 20th year celebration."

SUPER GIRL CONCERT SERIES: The weekend will feature 15 free live performances, headlined by Switchfoot, Lupe Fiasco, B.o.B and Gym Class Heroes. The lineup also spotlights a list of incredible female artists, including Emily Zeck, ANORA, Hello Sister, Flailing Idiot, McKenzi Brooke, Annie Dukes, Grom & The Jacks, Kalani Rose & The Vibe, Dove Bomb and Lucy Spotts.

PRO WOMEN'S SURFING RETURNS TO JACKSONVILLE BEACH: A World Surf League (WSL) QS2000 women's competition returns to the Jacksonville Beach Pier with a field expected to include former Super Girl champions Eden Walla, Kirra Pinkerton, Leilani McGonagle, Sage Erickson, U.S. Olympian Bryce Wettstein, local standout Lanea Mons and some of Florida's top rising surfers.

NEW THIS YEAR: Jacksonville Beach will welcome professional freestyle trampolining hosted by the Freestyle Trampoline Association, bringing a new high-energy competition to the festival as part of Super Girl's 20th anniversary season. The weekend will also mark the conclusion of the inaugural Quest for the Cape, with select athletes completing the three-stop points race spanning Oceanside, Virginia Beach and Jacksonville Beach to earn the coveted Super Girl cape.

Festival admission is free, with advance online registration required for concert access. Entry is first-come, first-served until capacity is reached. Premium VIP Packages are also available, featuring pit access, complimentary food and beverages, private VIP bars, shaded and elevated seating, deluxe restrooms and private entry.

The event is proudly supported by Jersey Mike's Subs, Visit Jacksonville, Florida Blue, Monster Energy, Sun Cruiser, SEAGLASS Wines, Atlantic Self Storage, SpringHill Suites Oceanfront, Athletic Brewing, Botanic Tonics, Rancho La Gloria, SG REVIVE, Body Glove, The Local, Mad Hippie and additional partners.

The surf competition will run at the Jacksonville Beach Pier from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. both days. The Festival Village at SeaWalk Pavilion and Latham Plaza will run Saturday (Nov. 7) from 11 a.m. to 10 p.m. and Sunday (Nov. 8) from 11 a.m. to 8 p.m.

The event will be televised from January 10 to April 30 on 28 national and regional broadcast partners, and will be streamed live on Nov. 7 - 8 from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. EST via 8 digital partners, including at www.supergirljax.com and twitch.tv/supergirlseries.

For schedules, concert information, concert registrations, sports competitions and more, visit supergirljax.com and follow @supergirlpro on social media.

ABOUT SUPER GIRL: The Super Girl Festival Series spans three annual sports, music, and lifestyle festivals across the West Coast, Southeast, and Mid-Atlantic with a mission to create athletic, social, cultural, educational and entertainment opportunities for women.

ABOUT ASA ENTERTAINMENT: Founded in 1994, ASA Entertainment Group, LLC is an action sports event, television and content production agency focused on creating customized, turnkey marketing programs that range in scale from grassroots to global. ASA's events span surfing, skateboarding, BMX, inline skating, freestyle motocross, snowboarding, esports and music, with content distributed globally. releases.body:
Actors Laya DeLeon Hayes and DaSan Frazier Named 2026 I Aspire Ambassadors

WASHINGTON, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The 4th Annual HBCU First LOOK Film & TV Festival (HBCUFLF) returns to Howard University November 5 -7, with STARZ as its inaugural presenting sponsor.

Under the theme "How to Be the Next," the three-day Festival will create an immersive experience connecting students and emerging creators with HBCU alumni actors, filmmakers, producers and industry leaders through screenings, master classes and interactive, hands-on sessions.

Actors and content creators Laya DeLeon Hayes (Doc McStuffins, Why Did I Get Married Again) and DaSan Frazier (Tough Love: Atlanta, Straw) will serve as the festival's 2026 I Aspire Ambassadors and host the Salute THEM Awards luncheon, where winners of the HBCU First LOOK Film Challenge, selected from more than 450 entries, will be announced and awarded $5,000 and internship opportunity.

The luncheon will also celebrate the 2026 I Aspire 25, recognizing HBCU alumni across five categories: Visionaries, Changemakers, Storytellers, Filmmakers and Entrepreneurs. This year's honorees include Michael Strahan, Eva Marcille, Jamila Mustafa, Colby Muhammad Nixon and Tone Bell, among others.

HBCU First LOOK's growing network of entertainment, media and brand partners is central to its professional development mission, helping build the pipeline of HBCU talent through industry insight, direct interaction and career-building opportunities.

STARZ, home to the critically acclaimed and award-winning drama "P-Valley" and the iconic "Power" franchise, continues to take the lead by creating opportunities for women and underrepresented audiences in front of and behind the camera. The network will participate in key programming during the festival, further underscoring its commitment to supporting diverse talent and emerging storytellers.

As one of the founding sponsors of the Festival, ANDSCAPE will celebrate its 10th anniversary, highlighting a decade of powerful storytelling at the intersection of sports and culture. The celebration will feature a special Clips & Conversations tribute with award-winning producers, Sheila Matthews and Jesse Washington, showcasing memorable stories and ANDSCAPE's cultural impact.

The 2026 lineup includes producer Autumn Bailey-Ford, who will examine the increasingly global nature of film production, and actress and filmmaker Nicky Micheaux, who will lead a master class on the rise of vertical storytelling. Grammy Award-winning producers Jimmy Jam & Terry Lewis will explore the relationship between music and film.

Creator-focused sessions will feature Alexis Powell, creator of The Jennifer Hudson Show's viral "hit" Spirit Tunnel; Howard University alumnae and content creators Jade & Jadah; media personality Jamila Mustafa; and independent filmmakers and producers the Vanzant Brothers.  Actress and I Aspire 25 honoree Kennedi Reece, who appears on CBS' Beyond the Gates and featured in Netflix's upcoming A Different World reboot, will participate on a leading lady panel.

New this year, aspireTV hosts a Clips & Conversation spotlighting its expansion into original scripted programming with New State of Mind, an HBCU-set comedy from producer Bentley Kyle Evans that follows first-year students navigating college life.

"HBCU First LOOK was created to build a pipeline that turns exposure into experience," said Sheila Eldridge, founder of the HBCU First LOOK Film & TV Festival. "This year, 12 Howard University students are helping produce the festival, lending a direct voice to programming and interactive elements presented. It's truly produced by students, for students—giving them a seat at the table and an active role in bringing the festival to life."

Black Girl Vitamins will host Fueling Your Future; a two-day wellness and career activation centered on how physical well-being supports the sustainability needed for creative careers.  TV One returns with a 'red carpet' readiness experience supports Micheaux's master class on vertical storytelling.

Additional partners include HBCUgo.tv, Storytellers Lab, Café Mocha Network, the Howard University Radio Network and the D.C. Office of Cable Television, Film, Music and Entertainment (OCTFME).

The HBCU First LOOK Film & TV Festival will take place at the Armour J. Blackburn University Center at Howard University, 2397 6th Street NW, Washington, D.C. For registration, programming updates, media coverage and additional information, visit www.hbcufirstlook.com and info@hbcufirstlook.com. 

On all social platforms @HBCUfirstlook  #hbcufirstlook #Elevatefilmmakers #TAKETHELEAD,  #BeTheNext

About HBCU First LOOK Film & TV Festival

Founded by Howard University alumna Sheila Eldridge, the HBCU First LOOK Film & TV  Festival inspires a new generation of diverse talent and storytellers in film, television and broadcasting. The festival provides a platform for emerging creators to showcase their work, connect with executives and build a pipeline of career opportunities while celebrating Black filmmakers rooted in the HBCU culture.

Past sponsors and media partners include iHeartMedia - Black Information Network,  HBCYOU, Andscape, NBC, ESPN, TVOne, Oxygen True Crime, Howard University Television + Film, Howard University Television (WHUT), Howard University Radio Network, SiriusXM Channel 141 & 142 and the Cafe Mocha Radio Network.

STARZ (NASDAQ: STRZ) is the leading premium entertainment destination for women and underrepresented audiences, and home to some of the most popular franchises and series on television. STARZ offers a robust programming mix for discerning adult audiences, including boundary-breaking originals and an expansive lineup of blockbuster movies, and is embodied by its brand positioning "We're All Adults Here." Complementary to any platform or service, STARZ is available across a wide range of digital OTT platforms and multichannel video distributors and is a bundling partner of choice. STARZ is powered by an industry-leading advanced technology, data analytics and digital infrastructure and the highly rated and first-of-its-kind STARZ app.

Andscape is a content studio that explores the depth of Black identity through its power in sports and culture. Magnified by the power and reach of The Walt Disney Company, the Andscape umbrella includes daily journalism, film, television, book publishing and music.

AspireTV is the television network that celebrates and reflects Black culture, life and style in a way that is inspiring, authentic and entertaining. AspireTV+ is a subscription streaming service for Black culture and urban lifestyle entertainment. For more information, visit www.aspire.tv, facebook.com/AspireTV, @TVaspire on YouTube, Instagram and X. releases.title: FRANK BRIEGMANN PROMOTED TO CHAIRMAN & CEO OF UNIVERSAL MUSIC EUROPE, AUSTRALIA, NEW ZEALAND, CANADA & DEUTSCHE GRAMMOPHON
releases.body:
Proven artist champion combining creative leadership, commercial expertise, and a deep commitment to local culture

New structure will increase agility and create bigger impact for local, regional and global stars

SANTA MONICA, Calif. and BERLIN, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Universal Music Group, the world's leading music entertainment business, today announced the promotion of Frank Briegmann to Chairman & CEO, Universal Music Europe, Australia, New Zealand, Canada & Deutsche Grammophon. This move brings unified leadership to a diverse group of territories, each with its own rich mix of cultures but sharing enormous potential to develop local talent into regional and global stars. Briegmann will continue to report to Sir Lucian Grainge, Chairman & CEO of Universal Music Group.

Today, artists have the potential to reach audiences around the world from day one. Briegmann has a proven track record of helping them realize that potential, working with leaders across territories to build strong local teams, nurture distinctive music cultures, and develop homegrown talent for success at home, regionally, and globally. Throughout his career, he has also opened up new commercial and creative opportunities for artists, including reimagining Deutsche Grammophon for the modern era.

The new structure is designed to create more opportunities for artists across borders by increasing agility and enabling closer collaboration. In a rapidly evolving music ecosystem, Briegmann's wider remit will help UMG anticipate and embrace change, using technology to amplify expertise, sharpen execution, and bring markets closer together.

Sir Lucian Grainge, Chairman & CEO, Universal Music Group said "Frank and I have worked together for more than 20 years, and he's a fierce artist champion with a proven track record of building long-term careers. He combines creative expertise with business acumen and the insights of data and technology. Just as importantly, he respects what makes every market different and knows how to give great local leaders the freedom and support to succeed. Frank's promotion is all about the power of possibility; making it easier for artists, ideas, and opportunities to travel across borders."

Frank Briegmann said "Great artists can emerge anywhere, and today they can find an audience almost everywhere. That makes strong local expertise more important. Our responsibility is to understand and nurture what makes each market dynamic and distinctive, while giving artists the investment, local expertise, and global reach to realize their full potential. I'm grateful to Lucian for his trust and this new opportunity to take on this broader responsibility. Over the years, I have seen what becomes possible when great local teams work closely together across borders. I look forward to building on that experience with this exceptional group of leaders and creating even more opportunities for artists throughout these markets and around the world."

Briegmann will work closely with the established leadership in each market, including Olivier Nusse who continues as CEO, Universal Music France; Sean Warner who continues as President & CEO, Universal Music Australia & New Zealand; and Julie Adam who continues as President & CEO, Universal Music Canada.

As part of his expanded role, Briegmann will also work with UMG's leadership in Europe, including the U.K. and Iberia, to create stronger connections across markets through technology, data and commerce.

Spain will continue to be led by Luis Fernández, President, Universal Music Spain, and Portugal will continue to be led by Ana Hernandez, Managing Director, Portugal, both reporting to Jesus Lopez.

The United Kingdom will continue to be led by Dickon Stainer, Chairman & CEO, UK, reporting to Sir Lucian Grainge.

Frank Briegmann

The appointment marks the latest step in Briegmann's more than three-decade career in the music industry and expands his international responsibilities.

Briegmann joined Universal Music in 2004 as CEO of its German business, becoming the youngest executive ever to lead a major music company in Germany. His responsibilities have since expanded across Central, Northern and Eastern Europe, alongside his global leadership of Deutsche Grammophon.

Throughout his career, Briegmann has championed local talent and distinctive music cultures, investing in artists and repertoire while helping them reach audiences far beyond their home markets. He has driven digital transformation and built new areas of business, combining strong local expertise with UMG's global reach. At Deutsche Grammophon, he has applied the same approach, combining the stewardship of the world's most renowned classical label with innovation in formats and audience development.

Briegmann is a board member of the Federal Association of the Music Industry. He also serves on Deutsche Bank's Eastern Regional Advisory Board, as well as on the boards of trustees of the renowned C/O Berlin Foundation and the German Sports Aid Foundation (Stiftung Deutsche Sporthilfe).

About Universal Music Group

At Universal Music Group, we exist to shape culture through the power of artistry. UMG is the world leader in music-based entertainment, with a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content. Featuring the most comprehensive catalogue of recordings and songs across every musical genre, UMG identifies and develops artists and produces and distributes the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music in the world. Committed to artistry, innovation, and entrepreneurship, UMG fosters the development of services, platforms, and business models in order to broaden artistic and commercial opportunities for our artists and create new experiences for fans. For more information, visit www.universalmusic.com.

HOUSTON, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Jiffy Lube®, an industry leader in fast oil changes and preventive automotive maintenance, announces its new promotion with Matchbox The Movie, a live-action feature film inspired by Mattel's line of iconic vehicles. With an oil change that is as fast as a speeding toy car, Jiffy Lube is helping bring the film's adventure and action to life with an exclusive limited-edition Jiffy Lube-branded Matchbox die-cast car.

Packaged in premium Matchbox The Movie blister card artwork, the vehicle captures the adventurous spirit of the upcoming film while celebrating Jiffy Lube's role in helping drivers stay road-ready.

"Jiffy Lube is excited to collaborate with Matchbox The Movie, bringing together two iconic brands celebrating cars and the thrill of getting behind the wheel," said Suzanne Clerkin, Chief Marketing Officer, Jiffy Lube, LLC. releases.title: Polymath and CineCity Studios to Explore a Tokenized Film Investment Platform
releases.body:
The collaboration will marry Polymath's digital securities infrastructure with CineCity's film production ecosystem to explore a tokenized film investment vehicle

TORONTO and CHICAGO, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Polymath Research Inc., a provider of enterprise-grade infrastructure for regulated digital securities and tokenized financial instruments, today announced its collaboration with CineCity Studios, a Chicago film and television production facility, to explore the development of a technology-enabled investment platform targeted towards film and entertainment investors.

Under the proposed structure, Polymath would serve as a technology partner to develop a tokenized film investment vehicle, providing infrastructure and expertise to support digital securities issuance, investor onboarding, compliance workflows, investor management, and the ongoing administration of tokenized interests. Polymath is a technology provider. It is not a broker-dealer, funding portal, investment adviser, or placement agent, and is not offering, recommending, or providing advice with respect to any security.

The initiative addresses a longstanding challenge in independent film finance: connecting quality productions with capital efficiently while giving investors a structured way to participate in a diversified portfolio of entertainment-related opportunities. According to Natalie Hirsch, Interim Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer of Polymath:

"The film industry is just one of many exciting examples of where tokenization can solve real-world capital formation problems. CineCity has the facilities, industry relationships, and production ecosystem, while Polymath brings the technology and capital markets infrastructure. Together, we have an opportunity to build a modern investment model around an asset class that historically has been inaccessible to many private investors."

The proposed investment strategy is expected to evaluate opportunities across the film-finance lifecycle and a range of financing structures. Final investment parameters, structure, and offering terms remain subject to legal, regulatory, and commercial review.

CineCity Studios operates a 140,000-square-foot film and television production facility in Chicago that has hosted major productions from Disney, Fox, Netflix, Comcast, NBCUniversal, and Tyler Perry Studios, as well as commercial productions for global brands including BMW, Rolls-Royce, Lamborghini, Xfinity, and Foot Locker/Nike, among others. The studio has also invested in expanding its technology and production capabilities as it continues to support Chicago's growing independent film and television community. According to Stanley Wozniak, Managing Partner of CineCity Studios:

"There's a tremendous amount of capital looking for differentiated investment opportunities, while filmmakers are constantly looking for more efficient ways to finance and produce quality productions. The film and television industry has a constant, growing need for new content. The exciting addition of VP LED Studios on campus brings cutting-edge virtual production, motion capture, multi-cam tracking, Unreal Engine, and AI integration to Chicago. We're bringing next-generation filmmaking to the studio with LED virtual production, combining immersive digital environments and real-time technology to expand creative possibilities and give filmmakers greater control. With VP LED, you can be anywhere. Working with Polymath gives us an opportunity to bring frontier technology into that equation and explore an investment model that can connect these two worlds in a way that has never before been possible."

Future productions at CineCity Studios qualify for Illinois' expanded Film Production Tax Credit, a 35% credit on eligible in-state spending. For investors, the credit creates an opportunity to reduce the effective cost of qualifying production expenditures by 35%, allowing a greater portion of invested capital to be directed toward the production and its revenue-generating assets. With the program extended through 2038, CineCity Studios offers productions a long-term opportunity to take advantage of one of the nation's most competitive film incentives. The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, introduced in 2026, would add a federal credit of 20% on U.S. labor. If passed as described, a Chicago production could combine Illinois' 35% credit with the federal 20% credit for a total of 55%, which would make Illinois one of the strongest places in the world to film.

For Polymath, the proposed collaboration would represent another application of tokenization beyond traditional financial assets and real estate, demonstrating how digital securities infrastructure can be applied to intellectual property, entertainment, and alternative investments.

About Polymath

Polymath develops enterprise-grade infrastructure for the issuance, compliance, and lifecycle management of regulated digital securities and tokenized financial instruments. Through its purpose-built technology and capital markets ecosystem, Polymath enables issuers and market participants to create and manage tokenized representations of real-world assets within compliant frameworks, supporting investor onboarding, regulatory controls, and post-issuance administration.

On August 18, 2026, Polymath announced an agreement to be acquired by TruGolf Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: TRUG), a transaction expected to bring Polymath's purpose-built blockchain and tokenization infrastructure to the U.S. public markets, subject to customary closing conditions.

Learn more at polymath.network

About CineCity Studios

CineCity Studios is a 140,000-square-foot Chicago-based production campus providing comprehensive studio, virtual production, and office facilities for film and television. The facility supports independent movies, major motion picture productions, commercial campaigns, and entertainment industry events such as Filmscape, Half-Rez, Chicago International Film Industry Days, the SAG-AFTRA Baron Awards, the Actors Empowerment Summit, the Pop-Up Asian Film Festival, the Latino Film Festival, IATSE Marketplace, the Best of the Midwest Film Festival Awards, and Chicago Innovation. CineCity Studios advances education, professional training, and industry collaboration, helping strengthen and connect Chicago's growing film and television production community.

Learn more at cinecitystudios.com

Important Notice

The investment vehicle described in this release remains under development. No securities are currently being offered pursuant to this announcement. Any future offering will be made only pursuant to applicable offering documents and in accordance with applicable securities laws and regulations. This release is not an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy any security, and is not a recommendation with respect to any investment.

Forward-Looking Statements

This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of applicable U.S. and Canadian securities laws. Forward-looking statements include, without limitation, statements regarding the anticipated collaboration between Polymath and CineCity Studios, the expected benefits of the collaboration, the development and structure of a potential tokenized film investment vehicle, potential investment strategies and opportunities, the availability of film production tax credits and the status of proposed legislation, future adoption of tokenized assets, and the proposed acquisition of Polymath by TruGolf Holdings, Inc.

These forward-looking statements are based on current expectations, estimates and assumptions and are subject to known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors that may cause actual results or developments to differ materially from those expressed or implied by such statements. Such risks include, without limitation, the parties' ability to develop and implement anticipated initiatives, changes in market, economic and regulatory conditions, the tax credits referred to herein being unavailable, evolving legal and compliance requirements relating to digital assets and tokenized securities, technological challenges, the pace of adoption of tokenized securities and digital assets, and the satisfaction of conditions required to complete the proposed acquisition of Polymath by TruGolf. Readers are cautioned not to place undue reliance on forward-looking statements, which speak only as of the date made. Polymath undertakes no obligation to update or revise any forward-looking statements.

Assessment of 40 Museums found that 30 percent are Failing, receiving the Lowest Grading Category of "Critically Deficient."

NEW YORK, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ADL (the Anti-Defamation League) today launched State of the Arts: Advancing Jewish Inclusion in Arts, Entertainment and Culture, a first-of-its-kind body of research and digital platform documenting the systemic exclusion and marginalization of Jewish and Israeli artists across American cultural life. The initiative from the ADL Ratings and Assessments Institute brings together a comprehensive look at three major cultural sectors –museums, live entertainment, and publishing– alongside a companion investigation from the ADL Center on Extremism into the activist networks driving this exclusion.
releases.title: New ADL Research Reveals Systemic Exclusion of Jewish and Israeli Artists Across Museums, Entertainment and Publishing
releases.body:
Assessment of 40 Museums found that 30 percent are Failing, receiving the Lowest Grading Category of "Critically Deficient."

NEW YORK, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ADL (the Anti-Defamation League) today launched State of the Arts: Advancing Jewish Inclusion in Arts, Entertainment and Culture, a first-of-its-kind body of research and digital platform documenting the systemic exclusion and marginalization of Jewish and Israeli artists across American cultural life. The initiative from the ADL Ratings and Assessments Institute brings together a comprehensive look at three major cultural sectors –museums, live entertainment, and publishing– alongside a companion investigation from the ADL Center on Extremism into the activist networks driving this exclusion.

"Jewish artists are being canceled, blacklisted and pushed out of American cultural life. We knew the situation was bad, we just didn't know how bad, and no one had documented it this way before," said Jonathan Greenblatt, ADL CEO. "Forty leading museums, not one includes Jewish identity in its DEI commitments. Authors are being told to strip Hebrew words and change Jewish character names just to get published. Jewish and Israeli performers are being harassed off stages and dropped from lineups. This is antisemitism and anti-Israeli discrimination, plain and simple, and the arts and culture sector needs to wake up before Jewish voices are silenced entirely."

Key Findings from the Reports

"Behind the Frame": A Quiet, Systemic Erasure in America's Museums

ADL conducted the first-ever systematic evaluation of antisemitism and Jewish representation across 40 leading U.S. art museums, developed in consultation with a 15-member external expert panel of artists, curators, collectors and museum leaders, and grading institutions across three categories: policies and internal standards, art and artist representation, and partnerships and programming. Of the 40 museums invited to review and corroborate their assessments before publication, 23 (58 percent) participated, while the remaining half did not engage in the process. The findings reveal a pattern of erasure by omission:

  • Highest standard remains the exception: Only one of the 40 museums assessed – the Berkeley Art Museum & Pacific Film Archive – achieved the Gold Standard. Other strong performers, earning a place in the Good Showing category, included The Cleveland Museum of Art and the Detroit Institute of Arts.
  • Around one-third were critically deficient: Twelve of 40 museums (30 percent), including major institutions such as the Philadelphia Museum of Art and The Broad, received the lowest possible rating of Critically Deficient.
  • Jewish American Heritage Month received minimal recognition: Only one of 40 museums demonstrated recognition of Jewish American Heritage Month in 2026, even as 24 of 40 museums (60 percent) continued actively recognizing other heritage months during the same period. Moreover, only six of the assessed museums (15 percent) recognized JAHM prior to October 7, five completely ceased doing so by 2026 while the remaining one has not done dedicated programming.
  • Many museums hold substantial, even world-class, Jewish and Israeli collections, yet these works are often absorbed into broader narratives that obscure their Jewish or Israeli significance or are difficult to discover online.

"Missing Chapter": Suppression of Jewish Voices in Publishing

This report, based on secondary research and more than 30 interviews with authors and publishing professionals, identifies seven anti-Jewish trends reshaping the publishing industry since October 7, 2023:

  • Suppression of books with Jewish, Israeli or Zionist characters and themes at the acquisition stage, with authors describing pressure to remove Hebrew words, Israeli settings, and even Jewish-sounding character names.
  • Blacklisting and boycotts of Jewish, Israeli and Zionist authors, including a viral spreadsheet that sorted authors by perceived political affiliation and urged readers not to buy their work.
  • Boycotts of Israeli publishing and institutions, including a 2024 letter signed by more than 1,000 writers calling for a boycott of Israeli publishers.
  • Author-level exclusion from festivals and events.
  • Review-bombing and online harassment, including books receiving negative Goodreads ratings before anyone could have read them.
  • Struggles to get and keep literary agents: Jewish, Israeli and Zionist authors described being told directly that their Jewish or Zionist identity, not the quality of their work, made them "too risky" to represent.
  • Institutional silence and failure to name antisemitism directly, including at organizations like the Authors Guild and PEN America. When statements are issued, they frequently frame the issue as a broad matter of censorship, civility, free expression or generalized anti-bigotry, rather than directly naming the targeting of Jewish and Zionist authors.

Author and photographer Alyssa Rosenheck described the shift in her own career: "This is what literary antisemitism looks like. It doesn't announce itself with swastikas. It hides behind excuses, shifting standards, institutional silence, community exclusion, and decisions that become impossible to separate from the climate surrounding Jewish voices after October 7."

"Dark Stage": Jewish and Israeli Performers Are Being Canceled, Harassed and Silenced

This report and interactive case archive document 65 cases across 41 U.S. locations, the most recent from August 2026, showing how Jewish, Israeli and openly Zionist artists face growing scrutiny, protest, disruption and cancellation across live music, comedy, dance, film and campus programming.

Key trends identified include:

  • Protest activity expanding from political advocacy into cultural exclusion, with campaigns increasingly aimed at preventing Jewish or Israeli artists from performing at all, as seen in repeated demonstrations against dozens of artists, like Matisyahu, the Batsheva Dance Company, and the Israel Philharmonic.
  • Security concerns functioning as a "security veto," where the mere prospect of protest activity, rather than a concrete threat, is enough to cancel events, as occurred with musicians Mikey Pauker and Raviv Kaner.
  • Informal cultural boycotts and institutional distancing that unfold privately, including lost bookings and withdrawn invitations, such as Israeli singer Noga Erez's account of losing international bookings because she is Israeli.
  • Normalized audience disruption and harassment, including comedian Judy Gold being told "You're a Jew" during two shows in one weekend in April 2026, and singer-songwriter Regina Spektor being heckled mid-performance.
  • Social media escalation that compresses institutional decision-making and turns local disputes into national controversies within hours.
  • Institutional inconsistency, with venues and organizations responding unpredictably to controversies, leaving artists unable to anticipate how their appearances will be treated.

Companion Investigation: The Activist Networks Organizing to Exclude Jewish and Israeli Artists 

Alongside the three sector reports, the ADL Center on Extremism released an investigation on the activist networks organizing to infiltrate and pressure cultural institutions, including major museums, in order to exclude Jewish and Zionist artists and disrupt their operations. ADL has tracked a prominent and escalating trend of anti-Zionist protests targeting cultural institutions, including Jewish and Holocaust museums and Jewish entertainers. These trends have involved violence and physical intimidation, harassment, Holocaust trivialization, expressions of support for terror and antisemitic tropes, vandalism, extreme forms of disruption, organized blacklisting and coercive exclusion.

Companion Survey: What the U.S. Public Actually Thinks

A non-nationally representative survey of 951 U.S. adults, conducted by ADL in July 2026, further underscores that this exclusion is not being driven by audience demand: strong majorities of Americans said they would support Jewish and Israeli inclusion across galleries, performances and books, even as many respondents simultaneously said it was "understandable" that others would avoid such work, a disconnect that may explain how exclusion takes root and persists.

"This research shows a clear and consistent gap between perceived market risk, what Jewish and Israeli authors are being told, and actual audience demand," said Shira Goodman, ADL's Vice President of Public Affairs and Special Initiatives. "The interviews ADL carried out with literary professionals for this research, surfaced a recurring pattern of authors being told by agents and publishers to strip Jewish and/or Israeli themes and characters from their work over fears it won't sell or is too much of a risk. The survey findings suggest this risk aversion is a misperception, not a market reality, and something that urgently needs to be addressed by the industry."

The Bottom Line

These findings reflect a combination of organized pressure campaigns, institutional risk-aversion, and structural blind spots in how museums, entertainment venues and publishers recognize and respond to antisemitism.

ADL is calling on museums, publishers, agents, venues and cultural institutions across the country to close these gaps: to name antisemitism explicitly in policies and DEI commitments, to recognize Jewish American Heritage Month alongside other heritage observances, to resist pressure campaigns rooted in identity-based exclusion, and to trust the data showing that American audiences want, and will support, Jewish and Israeli inclusion in the arts.

ADL is the leading anti-hate organization in the world. Founded in 1913 to protect the Jewish people, ADL works to stop the defamation of the Jewish people and secure justice and fair treatment to all. In the face of rising antisemitism and extremism, we protect, advocate, and educate, through a mix of programs and services using the latest innovations and technology, and seek to create a world without hate. More at www.adl.org.

Presented At: The Topfer at Zach Theater

From over 700 submissions, the Selection Committee chose 40 films in eleven competitive categories: features, shorts, micro-shorts, music videos, documentaries, series episodes, trailers, avant-garde films, commercial and brand films, hybrid live-action films, and student films.

The festival arrives as Texas begins distributing funds from Senate Bill 22, which commits $1.5 billion to the state's film incentive program over the next decade.

"Our mission is to build a physical space where filmmakers, artists, and fans can meet the people making these films and see how the work actually gets made," said Aaron Sanchez, Founder and President of AAIFF.

Featured speakers include Pinar Seyhan Demirdag (Founder & CEO, EVRN), Jason Fisher (Founder & CEO, StageRunner), Henry Daubrez (Founder, Odd Kid), Nik Kleverov (Co-founder & CCO, Native Foreign), Davide Bianca (Co-founder, CCO and CTIO, GRAiL), Jason Zada (Founder & CCO, Secret Level), Rupert Cresswell (Co-founder & CCO, Elevado Studio), Adrienne Lahens (Co-founder & CEO, Infinite Studios), Billy Boman (Founder, Boman Studios), Joni Dobrov (Co-founder & CCO, Exact), and C. Sean Yuksel (Founder, GRAFX Co. & Partner, Dreamspace).

This year's judges are director and cinematographer Louie Schwartzberg, production designer Rick Carter, Fox Entertainment's Jon Flynn (EVP and Head of FoxNXT), producer and director Sarba Das, journalist and filmmaker Seema Mathur, and generative artist BLVCKL!GHT.

Programming begins with The Global Virtual GenJam Hackathon, a free 48-hour event for creators worldwide, October 8 to 10, with Machine Cinema and AITX. Winning films screen at the festival.

releases.title: USANA CEO Kevin Guest Shares Three Ways to Celebrate International Music Day
releases.body:
SALT LAKE CITY, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- In recognition of International Music Day on Oct. 1, USANA Health Sciences (NYSE: USNA) Chairman and CEO Kevin Guest is urging people to experience music as a force that can reduce stress, lift spirits and connect people across cultures.

International Music Day celebrates the world's diverse musical traditions and music's ability to advance peace, friendship, and mutual appreciation. Guest, a lifelong musician who plays guitar and sings, says the day offers a simple invitation: slow down, listen and share music with a friend.

"Music is medicine for the soul," Guest said. "It can meet us where we are emotionally, help us reset, and bring people together even when they're from different backgrounds or languages."

That conviction is deeply personal. In his bestseller, All the Right Reasons: 12 Timeless Principles for Living a Life in Harmony, Guest writes that music filled his childhood home and became his passion. With a love for music, his parents bought a piano before they could afford a car, and Guest grew up singing, playing instruments and dreaming of performing on stage.

"When music comes from the heart, the connection between the musician and the audience is honest and powerful," Guest said. "Music speaks to the soul like nothing else can. It has transformed my life."

Research points to two clear benefits of making music part of daily life:

  1. Music can help regulate stress and emotion. A review of 47 studies involving 2,747 people found that music therapy can significantly reduce physical and emotional stress. Research also suggests that listening to music can calm the body and help people manage difficult emotions.



  2. Music can strengthen human connection. Research on music and social bonding indicates that listening, singing and making music together can encourage shared emotion, coordination and a stronger sense of belonging.

Guest offers three ways to celebrate International Music Day:

  1. Listen beyond your usual playlist. Choose a genre, artist or musical tradition from another culture. Give it your full attention and learn something about the people and history behind it.



  2. Experience music with other people. Attend a local concert, school performance, community event or open-mic night. Live music creates a shared experience that a solo playlist cannot fully duplicate.



  3. Share a song that matters to you. Send a favorite tune to a friend or family member and share why it matters. Then ask them to send one back. A simple exchange can start a meaningful conversation and introduce both of you to something new.

"You don't need to be a professional musician to feel music's power," Guest said. "Sing, play, listen or share a song. On Oct. 1, let music help you find a little more peace within yourself and a little more harmony with the people around you."

About Kevin Guest

Kevin Guest is Chairman and CEO of USANA Health Sciences, a global health and wellness company based in Salt Lake City. He is also a musician, author, speaker and humanitarian. His book, All the Right Reasons, shares lessons on leadership, integrity, relationships and purpose. All proceeds from book sales go to feed hungry children. Visit kevinguest.com for more information.

About USANA Health Sciences

USANA (NYSE: USNA) has provided nutrition and lifestyle products for more than 30 years. Its portfolio includes award-winning supplements, Celavive® skincare and healthy living products. USANA products are used by athletes, Olympians and health-conscious consumers in more than 25 markets worldwide.

What began as a partnership rooted in mentorship and empowering women in the industry has grown into something far bigger: Legacy Distribution's acquisition of global distribution powerhouse Vision Films.

LOS ANGELES, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This extraordinary combination brings together the unique strengths of both companies, uniting their content portfolios and operations into a single distribution entity. Dana Webber, CEO and Managing Partner of Legacy Distribution, will be the CEO of the expanded company operating under "Vision Films." Lise Romanoff, Founder and Managing Director of Vision Films, will transition into a consultant role; she will represent Vision Films at AFM in November. Vision will continue to offer acclaimed new releases alongside the robust merged libraries of features, TV series, documentaries, specials, and music programming.

Vision's deep library spans decades and includes award-winning and critically acclaimed independent films from all genres, television series, documentaries, narrative features, and specialty programming that has been distributed across theatrical, digital, and broadcast platforms to audiences in more than 190 countries. It is a prestigious VOD aggregator and direct supplier to all major global TVOD, SVOD, and AVOD platforms.

"I've spent years building Vision Films into a company I'm proud of. This is a dream opportunity to pass the baton to a colleague and friend who shares my commitment and dedication. Dana is the right leader for this next chapter of Vision's library, to seamlessly take care of my producers, company, and everyone who helped me build it. I could not find a better partner to carry on and grow my legacy (pun intended)," shares Lise Romanoff.

"Vision Films' global reach and powerful operations position us to advance our mission of delivering diverse and compelling content to audiences worldwide," says Dana Webber. "Lise is widely respected across the media industry for building a leading global content distribution business through sheer grit and vision."

Vision Films' extensive library consists of Murder Between Friends, Time Hoppers, Christmas With A Crown, The Healer, My Secret Billionaire, Tango Shalom (a.k.a. In the news release, Reel Wheels Entertainment™ Unveils Hundreds of Film and Television Icons, Backed by Award-Winning Hollywood Talent, issued 30-Sep-2026 by Reel Wheels Entertainment LLC. over PR Newswire, we are advised by the company that the original version did not include public-facing contact details as incorrectly formatted by PR Newswire.

Reel Wheels Entertainment™ Unveils Hundreds of Film and Television Icons, Backed by Award-Winning Hollywood Talent

The extraordinary private collection spans vehicles, aircraft, props, wardrobe and memorabilia, forming the foundation of a new global experiential entertainment platform.

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Maybe it was the Lamborghini Countach poster on your bedroom wall. Maybe it was Jake Ryan's Porsche 944 in Sixteen Candles. Maybe it was the Thunderbird from Thelma & Louise.

"The cars are the gateway. They open the door into an entire world of film and television."

Somewhere along the way, a car stopped being transportation and became part of a memory.

For the past three years, Reel Wheels Entertainment™ ("Reel Wheels") has been assembling those memories in physical form.

Now, the company is stepping into the public spotlight with a private collection spanning hundreds of vehicles, aircraft, props, wardrobe, memorabilia and entertainment assets connected to some of the most recognizable movies, television shows and moments in popular culture.

At a time when almost anything can be generated, streamed or digitally recreated, Reel Wheels is building around something increasingly powerful: real community formed around physical objects people can see up close and experience together.

But Reel Wheels is not being developed as a traditional museum, and the cars themselves are only the beginning.

"The cars are the gateway," said Aaron Phillips, CEO of Reel Wheels. "They open the door into an entire world of film and television. The characters, scenes, props, music and memories people already carry with them."

Phillips describes the vision as a cultural time tunnel, reconnecting audiences with what they loved growing up, surrounding them with what they love today, and creating anticipation for what comes next.

FROM COLLECTION TO EXPERIENCE

The collection includes original screen-used pieces, production-related artifacts and recreations, with provenance identified individually.

Among its holdings is the original screen-used cockpit from Airplane! Co-writer and co-director Jerry Zucker recently sat down with Reel Wheels for an interview about the film, the cockpit and why physical pieces of filmmaking still matter decades later. Reel Wheels plans to release that conversation soon.

"These objects also carry memories that belong to the audience as much as to us. People tell me they watched Airplane! with their dad, or on a first date, or at a sleepover where they laughed until they couldn't breathe. Seeing something real from the film brings that moment back. It connects people to a time in their own lives, not just to the movie," Zucker said.

Other highlights include an aircraft used in M*A*S*H, a screen-used mid-engine Dodge Charger from F9: The Fast Saga, a production aircraft fuselage associated with Sully, an original production stunt proton pack from Ghostbusters, The Cannonball Run ambulance, and vehicles, props and wardrobe connected to Men in Black and other celebrated film and television properties.

The assets currently visible publicly represent only a portion of Reel Wheels' holdings. Additional vehicles, aircraft and significant entertainment memorabilia continue to be documented and introduced.

A WORLD-CLASS TEAM OF INDUSTRY VETERANS

Reel Wheels has assembled a world-class design and production team capable of helping brands, studios, resorts, hospitality groups and destination developers integrate Reel Wheels assets into their own creative vision, from a single high-impact activation to a fully developed immersive environment.

Rick Carter, advisor to Reel Wheels, is a two-time Academy Award-winning production designer whose credits include Avatar, Lincoln, Jurassic Park, Forrest Gump and The Fabelmans.

"What could be more real than Reel Wheels?" Carter said. "These are the cars we all dreamed of driving and owning, the cars that made us want to be those characters and ignited our sense of speed, adventure and imagination in the 'reel worlds' of classic movies."

Doug Meerdink, Chief Creative Officer of Reel Wheels, has spent more than two decades working in feature-film art direction and production design.

"Reel Wheels gives us the opportunity to extend cinematic storytelling beyond the screen," Meerdink said. "By placing extraordinary physical assets at the center of immersive environments, we can transport audiences directly into the stories they love."

Veteran picture-car specialist Dennis McCarthy, founder of Vehicle Effects and advisor to Reel Wheels, brings decades of experience across more than 100 motion pictures, including extensive work throughout the Fast & Furious franchise, Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice and Avengers: Endgame.

"Cars in movies and television are more than transportation, they're characters," McCarthy said. "The right car can tell you who someone is before they ever say a word."

BUILT AROUND A PARTNER'S VISION

"We don't expect a partner to build their vision around our collection," Phillips said. "Our job is to understand their vision and use our assets, designers and production capabilities to help make it extraordinary."

Potential applications range from brand activations and resort programming to touring entertainment, studio collaborations and permanent destination-scale attractions.

Reel Wheels is also exploring opportunities internationally, including in Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, as investment in tourism, hospitality and location-based entertainment creates opportunities for ambitious physical experiences at scale.

"A recognizable car may be what gets someone through the door," Phillips said. "But the destination is the world it came from."

AN INVITATION TO CREATE

Reel Wheels is inviting filmmakers, production designers, technologists, global brands, hospitality leaders, studios, destination developers and storytellers to imagine what can be built around the collection.

"After three years of collecting, preserving, building and imagining what Reel Wheels could become, we're ready to open the door," Phillips said.

The cars are the gateway. The stories are the destination.

ABOUT REEL WHEELS

Reel Wheels is an experiential entertainment company built around a private collection spanning hundreds of vehicles, aircraft, props, wardrobe, memorabilia and entertainment assets connected to film, television and popular culture. The company is backed by a world-class team of industry veterans spanning production design, art direction, picture cars and experiential entertainment, bringing decades of experience from major motion pictures and global entertainment projects.

The collection includes assets with differing provenance, including original screen-used pieces, production-related assets and recreations. Reel Wheels identifies provenance individually and does not represent every asset as an original screen-used piece.

The publicly displayed collection represents only a portion of Reel Wheels' holdings, with additional vehicles, aircraft and entertainment memorabilia continuing to be documented and introduced.

For media inquiries, partnership opportunities, collection-related questions, or to learn more about Reel Wheels Entertainment™, please contact Aaron Phillips directly at aaron@reelwheels.com or by phone 310 879 5289

Photographs of The Beatles, Paul McCartney, The Pretenders, Neil Young, and more are shown alongside the record albums they covered, playable on Wrensilva record consoles, through February 2027

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --

WHAT: A new photography and listening installation at Wrensilva | Los Angeles pairs Linda McCartney's music photography with the album covers that featured her work, alongside Wrensilva record consoles where vinyl copies can be played. Artists featured include The Beatles, The Cimarons, Denny Laine, Paul McCartney, The Pretenders, Professor Longhair, and Neil Young.

WHEN: Open through February 2027. Gallery hours: Monday - Saturday, 11 a.m.-6 p.m.

WHERE: Wrensilva | Los Angeles, 8625 Melrose Ave., West Hollywood, CA 90069

BACKGROUND: Linda McCartney (née Eastman, 1941 – 1998) didn't direct her subjects. She was already in the room, camera in hand, while some of the most magnetic artists of her generation lived their lives around her. Her professional photography career began with shooting musicians, and music photography continued as a steady thread throughout her life.

McCartney had a particular skill for putting musicians at ease and producing uniquely unguarded portraits. For the most part, she rejected the stiff studio setups in favour of informal settings and nature. She preferred prolonged shooting sessions where exchanging knowledge and enthusiasm for the music shared space with the photography itself. She photographed people as she found them, never encouraging contrived performance for her lens.

Photography connected with all of the facets of her career and life - musician, activist, food entrepreneur, family documentarian. Her photographs on display here were used on album covers. Some were the result of official commissions from record labels; some were personal photographs lifted out of their intimate context. Shown here beside the records that enshrined them, to be enjoyed alongside the albums themselves, which are available to play on a Wrensilva record console.

Presented by Wrensilva, The Linda McCartney Archive LLP, and MPL Communications.

Handmade in San Diego since 2016, Wrensilva® crafts the ultimate record consoles—timeless centerpieces that invite you to slow down and reconnect with the music that defines you. Seamlessly blending generational-quality craftsmanship with modern audio performance, each console is built with beautifully grained hardwoods and enduring material selections. Created for design-minded music lovers, Wrensilva consoles offer effortless transitions between vinyl and streaming. With every detail thoughtfully considered, Wrensilva transforms listening to music into a ritual—one that brings warmth, beauty, and connection into your home. Learn more at wrensilva.com.

About MPL Communications

MPL Communications is Paul McCartney's company, founded in 1969. It manages his catalog, his post-Beatles work, and his archive, including the Linda McCartney Archive.

releases.body:
LOS ANGELES, Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Scientology Network's acclaimed Signature Performances will debut Mark Isham: The Voice Within this October, offering an intimate look inside the making of his latest album.

Mark Isham records his boldest musical creation yet at the legendary Mad Hatter Studios.

The documentary follows Grammy and Emmy-winning artist Mark Isham—the iconic trumpeter, New Age giant, celebrated composer and electronic music pioneer—as he returns to the studio to create At the Carousel Club, his first new album in 15 years. Blending the artistry of master musicians with electronic synthesis, Isham shapes a sound that pushes the boundaries of his already expansive body of work.

Stepping into the legendary Mad Hatter Studios—famed for recordings by artists ranging from Paul McCartney to Prince—Isham candidly reflects on the challenges and expectations surrounding the project. Behind-the-scenes moments document creative risks, breakthroughs and the experiences that have defined his musical journey, giving viewers rare access to a composer continually redefining his sound.

Joining him is a handpicked ensemble of superb musicians, including legendary drummer Vinnie Colaiuta, vocalist Ayo Awosika, guitarist Nels Cline, bassist Kaveh Rastegar and the Orchid String Quartet. Their collaboration forms the backbone of the album's richly layered arrangements, bringing Isham's electronic compositions to life through ensemble performance.

The film also explores Isham's far-reaching career, which spans more than four decades and over 400 film and television projects, including his Academy Award–nominated score for A River Runs Through It and the box-office hits 42 and The Accountant. His genre-crossing collaborations include artists such as Bruce Springsteen, Van Morrison, Willie Nelson, Joni Mitchell and The Rolling Stones—a testament to the breadth of his influence.

Reflecting on the album, Isham explains: "I cast people that I trust. And the music has evolved for them, for their voice to be especially effective in the music. And each step of the process has done that. Now the album is here and it's exhilarating."

Scientology Network debuted on March 12, 2018, launched by David Miscavige, ecclesiastical leader of the Scientology religion. Since then, Scientology Network has been viewed in over 240 countries and territories worldwide in 17 languages. Satisfying the curiosity of people about Scientology, the network takes viewers across six continents, spotlighting the everyday lives of Scientologists, showing the Church as a global organization and presenting its Social Betterment programs that have touched the lives of millions worldwide. The network also showcases documentaries by independent filmmakers who represent a cross section of cultures and faiths, but share a common purpose of uplifting communities. Scientology Network's innovative content has been recognized with more than 175 industry awards, including Tellys, Communitas and Hermes Creative Awards.

Broadcast from Scientology Media Productions, the Church's global media center in Los Angeles, the Scientology Network is available on DIRECTV Channel 320, DIRECTV STREAM, AT&T U-verse and can be streamed at scientology.tv, on mobile apps and via the Roku, Amazon Fire and Apple TV platforms.

releases.title: Boulder, Colorado, Hosts the 2027 Sundance Film Festival and Sets the Stage for Adventure Across Northern Colorado
releases.body:
From Rocky Mountain wildlife and Western heritage to craft breweries, thriving food scenes and celebrated arts communities, six Northern Colorado destinations offer plenty of reasons to turn a trip to the 2027 Sundance Film Festival into a wider Colorado adventure.

BOULDER, Colo., Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- In January 2027, the Sundance Film Festival will debut in Boulder, Colorado, after more than four decades in Park City. Taking place from January 21-31, 2027, the Festival's first edition in its new Colorado home will put Boulder firmly in the international spotlight. Beyond the screenings, premieres and creative energy of the Sundance Film Festival, six distinctive Northern Colorado destinations offer even more reasons to stay longer and explore the region.

Boulder: Where Creativity Meets the Outdoors

Set against the dramatic backdrop of the Flatirons, Boulder combines an energetic, creative spirit with the kind of immediate access to nature that defines Northern Colorado — a combination that will take on new significance when the Sundance Film Festival makes the city its new home starting January 21-31, 2027. At the heart of the city, pedestrian-only Pearl Street will celebrate its 50th anniversary in 2027, marking five decades as a vibrant gathering place lined with independent boutiques, galleries, restaurants, breweries and cafés. Boulder's wider culinary scene has also earned recognition from the MICHELIN Guide. Just minutes from downtown, Chautauqua Park provides a gateway to miles of hiking trails beneath the Flatirons, with its historic Chautauqua Auditorium also set to become one of the Festival's official venues. This means Sundance Film Festival visitors can easily experience the best of Boulder as they attend screenings at iconic venues, decompress in the natural outdoor setting and enjoy Boulder's rich food, coffee and shopping scene throughout their Festival journey.

With one-of-a-kind venues, Sundance Film Festival visitors can move easily between screenings and the outdoors, starting the morning in the mountains before returning downtown for the Festival's premieres, events and creative buzz.

Estes Park: Take the Story into the Rockies

Surrounded by soaring peaks and sweeping alpine landscapes, Estes Park allows travelers to experience Northern Colorado at its wildest, serving as the basecamp for Rocky Mountain National Park. Winter transforms the area into a quieter landscape of snow-covered trails and frozen lakes, with visitors able to explore on foot or by snowshoe and enjoy some of the park's most popular areas without the summer crowds. Wildlife remains part of everyday life here, with elk frequently seen around Estes Park and opportunities to spot mule deer and other native species throughout the surrounding landscape. Back in town, independent shops, restaurants, breweries and cozy mountain accommodations provide somewhere to warm up from a day outside. For something more leisurely, the scenic Riverwalk follows the Big Thompson and Fall rivers through the heart of downtown.

Fort Collins: Beer, Food and a Soundtrack of its Own

With a lively downtown, celebrated craft beer scene and strong independent spirit, Fort Collins is one of Northern Colorado's most energetic cultural hubs. The city is perhaps best known for brewing, with New Belgium Brewing and Odell Brewing Co. among the names that helped put Colorado craft beer on the map, alongside a growing collection of smaller local breweries. Historic Old Town Fort Collins provides the city's social heart, bringing together restaurants, cafés, boutiques, galleries and live music venues within its characterful streets. Music is woven particularly strongly into Fort Collins' identity, from intimate local performances to Mishawaka Presents' winter concert series, which brings live music to venues around the city, while its celebrated canyon-side amphitheater remains one of the region's best-known music destinations. Fort Collins is also one of Colorado's most bike-friendly cities, with an extensive network of trails making cycling an easy way to discover its neighborhoods, breweries and natural surroundings.

Loveland: Where Art is Part of the Landscape

Known as one of Colorado's most established arts communities, Loveland has built an identity around sculpture, craftsmanship and creativity. The city's artistic heritage is perhaps most visible at Benson Sculpture Garden, where visitors can wander among an extensive collection of sculptures in a landscaped outdoor setting, while Chapungu Sculpture Park showcases monumental stone works by Zimbabwean artists. Downtown, galleries, murals and public artworks continue the creative thread, alongside independent shops, restaurants and local businesses. Visitors can also explore exhibitions at the Loveland Museum or discover more about the artists, sculptors and bronze foundries that have helped shape the city's reputation as a center for the arts. Beyond its creative credentials, Loveland sits within easy reach of lakes, trails and foothills, allowing visitors to combine culture with Northern Colorado's outdoor lifestyle.

Longmont: A Taste of Northern Colorado

With an independent food and drink scene and a strong connection to local makers and producers, Longmont offers plenty of reasons to arrive hungry and thirsty. The city is home to renowned craft breweries, including Left Hand Brewing Company and Oskar Blues Brewery, alongside Wibby Brewing, which specializes in American craft lagers inspired by traditional German brewing techniques. Food lovers can explore Cheese Importers, a family-run Longmont institution with an extensive cheese and specialty-food market, before discovering the restaurants that feature Latin American cuisine, coffee shops and independent businesses clustered in the city's historic downtown arts and cultural district. Longmont's agricultural surroundings also remain an important part of its identity, creating connections between local farms, producers and the city's evolving culinary scene.

Greeley: A Diverse Culture Takes Center Stage

Greeley's arts and culture take center stage at the Union Colony Civic Center, a major performing arts venue that brings nationally touring artists, musicians, comedians and family entertainment to Northern Colorado. Public art, from murals to sculptures, reflects a diverse and vibrant culture. And within walking distance of downtown, the University of Northern Colorado brings jazz legends to campus and shares performing and visual arts as a vital part of the community. Visitors can discover craft beer at WeldWerks Brewing Co., explore the flavors of 477 Distilling, and experience Western heritage at local museums and special events like the century-old Greeley Stampede and others. Home to a growing creative sector, where artists, makers and entrepreneurs are shaping the city's evolving identity, Greeley celebrates community, arts, heritage and culture with a welcoming vibe.

About Explore Northern Colorado

Explore Northern Colorado is a collaborative tourism partnership bringing together six distinctive destinations across Northern Colorado: Boulder, Estes Park, Fort Collins, Greeley, Longmont and Loveland. Working together to showcase the diversity of the region, Explore Northern Colorado connects visitors with experiences spanning the Rocky Mountains and great outdoors, vibrant arts and culture, locally rooted food and drink, Western heritage and thriving creative communities. The partnership aims to inspire visitors to stay longer, explore further and discover the individual character of each destination while experiencing Northern Colorado as a connected and compelling year-round destination. For more information, visit explorenortherncolorado.com.

releases.title: AMERIGO: THE SEARCH FOR THE AMERICAN DREAM WINS FIVE HONORS AT THE ACCOLADE GLOBAL FILM COMPETITION
releases.body:
Award-Winning Documentary Returns to PBS Stations Nationwide

Ahead of 2026 Elections

Accompanied by New Civics Education Guide for Students, Teachers, Families 

NEW YORK, Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AMERIGO: The Search for the American Dream, the documentary that traveled across America asking people what the American Dream means today, has received five honors in the August 2026 season of the Accolade Global Film Competition.

The film received the Award of Excellence Special Mention for Documentary Feature, one of the competition's top honors, as well as Awards for Direction (Adam Mason) and Editing (Paul Crowder), and Award of Merit Special Mention for Cinematography and Award of Merit Special Mention for Narration/Voice-Over recognizing David McCourt's narration of the documentary.

The recognition comes as AMERIGO prepares to return to PBS audiences across the country ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Since its premiere, AMERIGO has aired in over 90% of households across the country. It's second national broadcast is also expected to air in the majority of American households before the midterm elections.

"This recognition means a great deal to all of us who made AMERIGO," said McCourt. "But the film was never really about us. It was about the people we met across America who opened their homes, their workplaces, and their lives to us. These awards belong, in a very real sense, to them."

Accompanying the broadcasts will be a new AMERIGO Civics Guide, created to help teachers, students and families explore and discuss some of the critical issues facing their communities this election year.

Over two years, McCourt and the AMERIGO team traveled across the United States listening to Americans from different regions and backgrounds, capturing the real-life pressures shaping people's lives – from the cost of housing, healthcare, and education; wages and economic opportunity; the strength of local communities; trust in institutions; and whether the next generation will have the same opportunities as the generation before it.

McCourt added: "As the country approaches another important election, I hope AMERIGO can do something increasingly rare – give people with different experiences and different points of views a reason to sit in the same room, listen to one another and talk about the country we want to leave to the next generation. The big issues we explore did not begin in Washington; they are issues consistent in so many communities all across America and this film is about giving a voice to everyday citizens. AMERIGO does not tell viewers what to think, whom to blame, or how to vote. The film and the accompanying civics initiative invite people to listen, question, discuss, and decide for themselves."

To view the trailer and join the national dialogue, visit AD250.com.

The film explores the past, present, and future of the American Dream through conversations with people from across the United States, reflecting on work, opportunity, technology, and community.

ABOUT McCOURT ENTERTAINMENT

McCourt Entertainment, led by Emmy Award–winning producer and entrepreneur David McCourt, is a global media company developing innovative, socially resonant storytelling across film, television, and digital platforms. Its credits include the acclaimed children's programming Reading Rainbow (26 Emmys); Miracle Boys miniseries directed by Spike Lee; and the UN Works documentary series What's Going On? which included "Child Soldiers in Sierra Leone", hosted by Michael Douglas, and "Child Refugees in Tanzania" featuring Angelina Jolie. In addition to AMERIGO, a documentary on the legendary musicians Crosby, Stills & Nash is scheduled for release at the end of 2026.

American Public Television (APT) is the leading syndicator of high-quality, top-rated programming to the nation's public television stations. Founded in 1961, APT distributes 250 new program titles per year and more than one-third of the top 100 highest-rated public television titles in the U.S. APT's diverse catalog includes prominent documentaries, performance, dramas, how-to programs, classic movies, children's series, and news and current affairs programs. APT also licenses programs internationally through its APT Worldwide service and distributes Create® TV and WORLD™, public television's premier news, science, and documentary channel. For more information, visit APTonline.org.

South Florida PBS is Florida's largest public media company including Public Broadcasting stations WXEL-TV, serving the Palm Beaches and the Treasure Coast and WPBT2, serving Miami-Dade and Broward counties, and the Health Channel, the only 24/7 channel dedicated to health in the nation. South Florida PBS connects organizations and institutions across our region and preserves South Florida's history. Leading the way in the global society, South Florida PBS is committed to creating and presenting award-winning programs focused on kids, education, arts and culture, health, environment, science, and civic engagement.

releases.title: Avex Music Group CEO Brandon Silverstein Expands Global Role as Avex Acquires His S10 Entertainment
releases.body:
Avex increases its ownership to 85%, with an agreement to reach 100% ownership over time

LOS ANGELES and TOKYO, Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Avex Inc. (TSE: 7860) ("Avex"), the publicly traded global entertainment conglomerate led by CEO Katsumi Kuroiwa, has increased its ownership of S10 Entertainment acquiring 85% of the company from Silverstein and his partners. The transaction further integrates S10 into Avex Music Group and advances Avex's vision of one global music company.

"S10 is an exceptional management company that is playing a key role in realizing our global ambitions," said Katsumi Kuroiwa, CEO of Avex Inc. "Bringing S10 into Avex reflects our confidence in Brandon's leadership and our commitment to growing Avex's global music business. Together, we will bring the full breadth of Avex's capabilities to artists and creators around the world."

Silverstein continues as CEO of S10 and Avex Music Group, a board member and equity partner in Avex Music Group. Alongside the acquisition, he assumes a broader role in shaping Avex Group's global music strategy, working in close partnership with the Avex board to develop opportunities and strategic partnerships across recorded music, publishing, live entertainment, touring and investments. Avex Inc. drove nearly $1 Billion in revenue in its last fiscal year.

The transaction follows Avex's March 2025 acquisition of the S10 Music Publishing catalog, marking a second acquisition involving the businesses Silverstein built and deepening his partnership with Avex.

At the time of the publishing acquisition, S10 reported more than 22 global No. 1 hits and 50 billion streams worldwide, with a publishing repertoire that included songs recorded by Justin Bieber, Drake, Tate McRae, Doja Cat, Post Malone and Rihanna, among others.

The latest acquisition builds on two years of publishing development, including the integration of S10's publishing catalog, new songwriter signings and global partnerships. Since Silverstein became CEO in 2025, Avex Music Group has announced a global publishing administration partnership with Bruno Mars and launched an initial $100 million publishing acquisition initiative.

Its songwriters' achievements include Kamal Wilson's Grammy Award for Best R&B Song for co-writing Kehlani's "Folded." In June 2026, Silverstein and Avex Inc. CEO Katsumi Kuroiwa accepted Billboard's Global Growth Award on behalf of Avex Music Group.

"S10 began with a belief in exceptional talent and what we could build around it," said Silverstein. "I'm proud of what our artists, songwriters and team have accomplished, and grateful to the partners who helped us get here. This next chapter is an opportunity to build on that work at a greater scale with Avex, investing in talent, developing new businesses and creating more opportunities across markets."

Avex's vision of one global music company brings its music businesses around the world closer together across recorded music, publishing, artist management, marketing, live entertainment and touring. The strategy connects talent development, music rights and global partnerships, creating more opportunities for artists, songwriters and business partners across the group. Catalog acquisitions and strategic investments will support this growth alongside the signing and development of new talent.

Avex's label strategy combines continued investment in the global careers of XG and ONE OR EIGHT with the signing and development of artists from the United States and other global markets. The ambition is to build a global roster with the creative support, resources and reach to compete at the highest level.

"I'm grateful to Max Matsuura, Katsumi Kuroiwa, Shinji Hayashi and the Avex board for their continued trust and support," said Silverstein. "The global platform Avex has built is extraordinary, and together with our teams around the world, I look forward to extending it as one global music company."

In the transaction Silverstein was represented by Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP.

Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
