"We Shall Overcome" music video by Pynk Beard premieres September 25, 2026.

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Anzie Blue Records and Surf Club today announced the September 25 release of By Any Means: The Album, featuring music from and inspired by the feature film BY ANY MEANS now in theaters. The album will be distributed globally by The Orchard. BY ANY MEANS is distributed domestically by Paramount Pictures. Bonnie Greenberg served as the music supervisor and executive music producer for the film.

Ole Smoky Distillery is the marketing partner for By Any Means: The Album, with plans including an upcoming tour by Pynk Beard and select album artists. CEO Mike Novy says, "We're proud to partner with these artists and the music community to bring such iconic American songs to life. Nothing brings people together like music, except for passing around a jar of Ole Smoky moonshine!"

The album is executive produced by Surf Club co-founder Hit-Boy, whose extensive production credits include Beyoncé, Jay-Z, Travis Scott and Drake, and Dr. Blum, whose credits include Twenty One Pilots, Big Sean and Nas. Parasol Music, co-founded by Martin Wave, served as a creative and production partner on the album.

Musically directed by Anzie Blue Records' country artist and GRAMMY®-nominated songwriter Pynk Beard, By Any Means: The Album brings together artists across generations and genres to reinterpret songs connected to the sound and spirit of the 1960s. Brandy, Kashus Culpepper, Keb' Mo', Tone Stith, and others put their own stamp on songs from iconic artists — including three performers in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame's premiere induction class: Ray Charles, Sam Cooke, and James Brown.

Regarding new single "We Shall Overcome," Pynk Beard says "There are very few songs that transcend time quite like this one. I'm honored to be a part of this project and particularly this song. The lyrics speak to the hope that I think we should all share for this world. Hate will not win. We WILL overcome."

Three songs from the BY ANY MEANS film are featured on the album, including Elsie's "I Love Your Lovin' Ways" (popularized by Rock Hall inductee Nina Simone) and Parson James & ASHBY's "Talking About My Baby" (popularized by Rock Hall inductees The Impressions and written by solo Rock Hall inductee Curtis Mayfield) in addition to the title track. "By Any Means" makes The Isley Brothers the latest of over 40 Rock Hall inductees to record a Diane Warren song.

Much of the album was recorded at FAME Studios in Muscle Shoals, Alabama in less than a week — bringing the project to a place with deep roots in American soul music and to Pynk Beard's home state. Artists include 2'Live Bre, Ariel J., ASHBY, Brandy, David Kushner, Denitia, Elsie, Kashus Culpepper, Keb' Mo', nanawho, Parson James, Pynk Beard, Reyna Roberts, Saekyi, Steve Ray Ladson, Tatiana Marie Clark, The BoykinZ, The Isley Brothers, and Tone Stith.

Net proceeds from the album will benefit the Black Music Action Coalition (BMAC), supporting the organization's work to advance equity, expand opportunity, and create pathways for the next generation of artists, creatives, and music industry professionals.

The partnership with the Black Music Action Coalition extends the album's impact beyond the music itself. Net proceeds from By Any Means: The Album, will support BMAC's work to protect and advance the legacy of Black creators while investing in the artists, executives, and emerging leaders who will shape the future. The collaboration reflects the shared belief at the heart of the film and its music: that culture can be a powerful force for progress, and that honoring the legacy of those who came before us must include creating opportunity for those who come next.

The official "By Any Means" music video, featuring The Isley Brothers and Kushner, was released September 4. Watch here: https://youtu.be/pZaWebkmJDY Directed by Fran Strine of F26 Productions — who directed Dolly Parton's Live at London O2 Arena film — the video will be followed on September 25 by Pynk Beard's "We Shall Overcome," also directed by Strine.

Diane Warren explains her inspiration for the title track, "By Any Means":

"I wanted to write a song that captured the spirit of the film, which is about those who go beyond the rules to do what is necessary. My idea was to take an iconic artist who came from that era and pair them with an artist from this current era. Having The Isley Brothers come on board was a dream come true. They are as amazing today as they were when they were performing during the time of these events, and they are so authentic to this story.

"David Kushner is a great young singer who sounds like he could have come from that era too. He is a young guy with an old-soul voice. The combination of him and the Isleys is pure magic, and together they have created a song that could live in many eras to come. I'm proud to be a part of it."

For Ronald Isley, the film's story carries a personal connection:

"Having lived through the Civil Rights era, this story is personal. We saw firsthand the courage, sacrifice and struggle it took for change to come. Music has always had the power to speak to what people are going through, and Diane Warren has written a song that carries that kind of meaning. It was an honor for Ernie and me to be a part of it and to lend our voices to a film that remembers this history while reminding a new generation why it still matters."

Ernie Isley adds, "I believe the film and the song will have a major impact. Ronald and I are happy to be involved with this project."

David Kushner says:

"It's an honor to be a part of the music that soundtracks a powerful film like By Any Means. I'm a huge fan of Mark Wahlberg, and being part of this song alongside Diane Warren, a songwriter I've looked up to since I fell in love with music and began writing songs, as well as The Isley Brothers, is beyond surreal and has been an incredible experience."

ABOUT BY ANY MEANS

BY ANY MEANS stars Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Mark Wahlberg and is directed by Elegance Bratton from a screenplay by Sascha Penn. Inspired by a true story and set in the 1960s, the film follows a young Black FBI agent (Abdul-Mateen II) sent to Mississippi to investigate a wave of brutal killings targeting civil rights leaders. Forced to work alongside notorious hitman Greg Scarpa (Wahlberg), he finds himself pulled into a deadly hunt where justice and vengeance begin to blur.

releases.title: ENCOUNTERS IN THE MILKY WAY A NEW FILM COMING TO THE PLANÉTARIUM ON OCTOBER 6
releases.body:
MONTREAL, Sept. 23, 2026 /CNW/ -- Just as the planets orbit the Sun, our solar system continues its own journey through our galaxy. Explore the Milky Way, discover its history, its future, and the dynamic transformations constantly taking place within it in the new film presented by the Planétarium | Espace pour la vie, Encounters in the Milky Way, opening October 6 and narrated by Chilean-American actor Pedro Pascal. The film is produced by the American Museum of Natural History in New York, with major support from and in partnership with NASA.

Synopsis

Discover the chance encounters that have shaped our place in the universe. Reaching billions of years into the past and peering millions of years into the future, Encounters in the Milky Way is a time-traveling journey about the cosmic movements that shape our galactic neighbourhood.

Witness spectacular moments in our solar system's past and future, including the paths of stars, comets, interstellar debris, and visually stunning gas and dust clouds--and, visualized for the first time, a dramatic, ongoing merger of our galaxy with a smaller satellite galaxy.

Developed by a team that includes astronomers, science visualization experts, and artists, Encounters in the Milky Way is made possible by data from one of the most transformative projects of the past century: the European Space Agency's Gaia mission, dubbed the "billion-star survey" for mapping the precise positions, distances, and motions of nearly 2 billion stars in our galaxy.

Contribution from an expert at the Planétarium de Montréal

As part of ongoing collaborations related to the publication of scientific articles, Jackie Faherty, a senior research scientist at the American Museum of Natural History in New York and curator of the film project, called on Jonathan Gagné, a scientific advisor at the Planétarium, to visualize the distribution of young stars in a region near the Sun. The information compiled and provided by Jonathan--namely, the position and velocity of these stars--comes primarily from a database he developed himself as part of his own research, a reference source for which his expertise is sought on a regular basis.

Encounters in the Milky Way is the first production to shed light on the history of our galaxy's cosmic motion and its influence on our solar system.

About the Service de l'Espace pour la vie, des grands parcs et du Mont-Royal

The Espace pour la vie museums and the network of major parks are at the heart of this service. Its activities contribute significantly to the quality of life of Montrealers. It plays a key role in the city's appeal and influence. With its five science museums, natural habitats, urban forest, and public spaces, the Service de l'Espace pour la vie, des grands parcs et du Mont-Royal is dedicated to protecting nature and promoting biodiversity. Through its efforts in conservation, restoration, development, research, and education, it contributes to Montreal's socio-ecological transition.

releases.title: Itibari-Waynne & Partners (IWP) Team with SHARE to Connect Filmmakers with Investment Capital
releases.body:
Partnership combines IWP's investor-focused financing model with SHARE Studios' creator infrastructure to help filmmakers fund projects while retaining intellectual property ownership

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Itibari-Waynne & Partners (IWP), an Agentic financing platform focused on de-risking capital for creative small businesses, has partnered with SHARE to create a new pathway for independent filmmakers to access financing while maintaining ownership of their intellectual property and participating in the long-term financial upside of their projects.

The alliance combines IWP's investor-focused capital de-risking strategies with SHAREs' collaborative infrastructure, profit-sharing models and distribution networks. Together, the companies aim to address one of independent filmmaking's persistent challenges: connecting creators and their projects with investment capital while providing a structure that allows filmmakers to retain control of their work.

IWP's funding model connects investors with creator-led projects, without requiring creators to surrender their intellectual property. Led by Bruce Waynne and Itibari Zulu, IWP brings experience across entertainment and finance to channel investment capital into the creator economy.

"This partnership addresses access to capital while recognizing that funding a project shouldn't mean giving away rights," adds Bruce Waynne, CEO of IWP. "We are creating a stronger connection between investors, creators, and the financial value generated by the creator economy."

Through the association, IWP's financing model will be paired with SHAREs' platform, which provides filmmakers with tools to connect, build crews, structure projects and negotiate transparent backend profit-sharing agreements.

SHARE's infrastructure is designed to help creatives mobilize communities, organize independent productions and maintain control over their work. When combined with IWP's capital resources, the companies intend to provide filmmakers with both financing opportunities and the infrastructure needed to prepare and advance projects.

"As a filmmaker myself, I've spent years navigating the same frustrating catch-22 so many creators face: agents and managers often want financing in place before giving you access to talent, while investors want recognizable talent attached before they'll consider funding the project," explains Erin Norman, CEO & Co-Founder of SHARE Studios. "When I learned about IWP and met their team, I felt genuinely hopeful about what this could mean for the future of our industry. It can get crews back to work, creating sustainable careers and help reshape a financial system that is long overdue for change."

Filmmakers and creators can register for early access and begin preparing their projects ahead of upcoming funding opportunities through IWP.

Following an initial email registration, creators will be guided through five steps intended to help organize and strengthen their projects for future funding consideration.

Filmmakers are encouraged to assemble key project elements including cast, crew, production materials, budgets and other relevant information so projects are prepared when IWP funding opportunities become available and investor review begins.

releases.title: QubicaAMF and ROLLER Forge Long-Term Partnership to Shape the Future of the Bowling and Family Entertainment Industry
releases.body:
QubicaAMF and ROLLER announce their partnership and introduce Conqueror ROLLER, the all-in-one management solution for bowling and multi-attraction entertainment centers, which is already live with shared customers around the globe.

LONDON, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- QubicaAMF, the world's largest bowling equipment and technology provider, and ROLLER, the leading venue management platform for modern attractions, today announced a long-term strategic partnership to shape the future of family entertainment. The partnership brings together two leaders in their respective industries around a shared vision for a unified guest experience with continued investment from both companies. Together, the two partners have developed Conqueror ROLLER, an all-in-one solution already live in bowling and entertainment centers across the globe, with continued innovation planned through their shared product roadmap.

Bowling is a $10 billion global industry, with more than 100 million people bowling each year across 125 countries. Traditional bowling centers are evolving into multi-attraction entertainment destinations, and operators are increasingly managing experiences that extend far beyond the lanes. Yet the technology powering those venues often remains fragmented, with separate systems for bowling operations, reservations, and other attractions.

"The bowling industry is in the middle of a major shift. Bowling remains at the heart of the venue, but operators are rapidly building broader entertainment experiences around it," said Emanuele Govoni, CEO of QubicaAMF. "The technology powering these venues must bring bowling and other attractions together. QubicaAMF and ROLLER have formed a long-term partnership, and with a shared vision, we will continue to build what operators need to shape the next generation of family entertainment."

At the center of the partnership is the Conqueror ROLLER solution, which unifies QubicaAMF's Conqueror X bowling and lane management technology with ROLLER's venue management platform. For operators, this solves a critical problem: combining bowling and multi-attraction management to unify the guest experience while making it easier for staff to delight guests. ROLLER can now power the full guest journey across a venue's entertainment offerings, including lane management through QubicaAMF's integrated technology.

"The best technology should make a complex venue feel simple to run and seamless for guests to experience," said Luke Finn, CEO of ROLLER. "Together with QubicaAMF, we've created a solution that unifies the guest journey from the moment guests book their first game to every time they come back. This is a long-term commitment to our industry, and we will continue building what operators need next."

A unified guest experience helps venues convert more bookings, increase revenue per guest, drive repeat visits, maximize lane utilization, and operate more efficiently by combining venue and attraction management with a complete on-lane entertainment ecosystem. Joint QubicaAMF and ROLLER customers are already seeing the impact:

  • Lumos in Texas increased its share of revenue generated online by 5.5x.
  • Queens in London increased multi-activity bookings by 64%.
  • NIKITO, headquartered in Paris, went live in less than three months and saw 100% of staff prefer the new system.

Tenpin, one of the United Kingdom's largest bowling operators, with 60 venues across the country, is bringing the joint QubicaAMF and ROLLER solution across its portfolio.

"Our vision is to create one seamless experience across all of our activities," said Roy Whitmore, IT Director at Tenpin. "Unifying all of our activities with bowling is critical to achieving that goal. The joint solution from QubicaAMF and ROLLER is a major step forward in making that vision a reality, and we're excited to bring it live across our portfolio of venues."

Today's announcement is the next step in a broader partnership, with QubicaAMF and ROLLER working from a shared product roadmap to sync more of the bowling and venue experience over time. Planned capabilities will bring more of the venue operation together, including waitlist management, in-game adjustments, and unified capacity management across all attractions.

To learn more about the integration, visit qubicaamfbowling.com/conqueror-roller or meet the teams at IAAPA Expo Europe at ExCeL London, September 21–25, 2026. Visit ROLLER at booth S3103 or QubicaAMF at booth S1806. A press conference will be held at the QubicaAMF booth S1806 from 3:50–4:10 p.m. on September 22.

About ROLLER

ROLLER is the cloud-based venue management platform for modern attractions, purpose-built to remove friction from the guest experience at every touchpoint. The company's all-in-one platform simplifies its customers' business processes, improving efficiency and maximizing revenue. ROLLER's comprehensive solution includes: Online Checkout & Ticketing, Point-of-Sale, Integrated Payments, Memberships, Gift Cards, Waivers, Self-Serve Kiosks, Cashless Wallets, Guest Surveys, and more. To learn more, visit www.roller.software.

About QubicaAMF

QubicaAMF is the largest and most innovative bowling equipment and technology provider in the world with over 700 employees worldwide. We build and modernize more bowling entertainment centers than any other company in the industry and have an installed base of more than 10,000 centers in 90 countries. The company has a sales and distribution network with worldwide reach and maintains the largest R&D team for electro-mechanical products, software, electronics, and entertainment systems in the industry.

QubicaAMF has over 100 years of experience and can provide the perfect combination of bowling equipment, products, and services for new or existing bowling entertainment centers, FECs, cinemas, or any other facility in the hospitality, retail, or restaurant industry. Our ongoing mission is Making Bowling Amazing. We are convinced that bowling has so much more potential to attract and entertain even more people. With our products, we will help our customers fully unleash that potential.

The company has U.S. headquarters in Richmond, Virginia and European headquarters in Bologna, Italy. To learn more, visit www.qubicaamfbowling.com.

releases.title: Global PR Firm Red Banyan's Campaign Supporting the Nova Music Festival Exhibition Named Finalist in Ragan's 2026 Zenith Awards
releases.body:
Strategic Communications Campaign Brought Nova Survivors' Testimony and Exhibition's Message of Remembrance to National Media, Policymakers and Community Groups

FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla., Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Global PR firm Red Banyan's strategic communications campaign supporting the Nova Music Festival Exhibition has been named a finalist in the Event/Experiential category of Ragan's 2026 Zenith Awards.

The Nova Music Festival Exhibition is a powerful memorial bearing witness to the massacre that took place at the gathering in Israel on October 7, 2023. It exhibits the grounds of a festival that was devoted to music, peace and love, and the harrowing results of the attack that unfolded that day and turned a celebration into tragedy.

Visitors follow a timeline of the festival from its final hours of music and dancing into the attack itself, moving through remains salvaged from the grounds: scorched cars, bullet-riddled bathroom stalls and the personal belongings left behind. Throughout, the voices of survivors, bereaved families and returned hostages tell the story of what they lived through, with many attending the exhibition in person as witnesses. The experience ends in the healing room, a sanctuary where visitors can reflect and find solace after what they have seen. Above them, the words "We will dance again" hang as a declaration of resilience and hope.

Red Banyan secured substantive coverage in national, local, Jewish and interfaith media throughout the exhibition's runs in Washington, D.C., and Chicago, with a communications campaign developed around the victims whose lives were taken or forever changed that day. The firm guided messaging efforts grounded in firsthand accounts and forensic evidence, spearheaded media relations, prepared survivors and exhibition leaders for interviews, and supported press and VIP events, leading to sustained public attention on the exhibition's mission and the testimony it was created to preserve.

In Washington, D.C., where October 7 is often discussed through the lens of geopolitics, Red Banyan's campaign extended into public affairs and community relations efforts, with the agency engaging political, civic and religious networks to amplify the exhibition's impact. This included working with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) to invite members of Congress, collaborating with the Jewish Federation of Greater Washington and coordinating efforts with various community groups. The firm also facilitated a program with the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum that brought Holocaust survivor Nat Shaffir and Nova Music Festival survivor Noa Beer together to share their testimony across generations.

"The Nova Exhibition asks people to look directly at what happened on October 7 and remember the human beings behind every headline," said Evan Nierman, Founder & CEO of Red Banyan. "Our team was trusted to carry those stories into the national conversation with accuracy, dignity and care. Ragan's recognition is deeply meaningful because it honors work rooted in truth, remembrance and the voices of survivors."

Winners of Ragan's 2026 Zenith Awards will be announced during a ceremony on November 5, held in New York City.

Recognized for Excellence in Reputation Management and Crisis Communications

Ragan's recognition adds to a series of honors for Red Banyan's work across proactive public relations campaigns, crisis communications and reputation management. In 2026, the firm earned a ranking in the Chambers Crisis & Risk Management Guide and was ranked the No. 1 boutique crisis communications firm in the U.S. by O'Dwyer's. CEO Evan Nierman also earned gold in the Best Crisis Communications Leader category at the World Communications Forum Association's Davos Communications Awards. Most recently, Guide to Florida named Red Banyan a "2026 Best of Florida" regional winner in the Business Consulting Firms category.

About Red Banyan:

Red Banyan is an award-winning strategic communications firm specializing in high-stakes reputation management. The firm advises business leaders, organizations, institutions and high-profile individuals operating in scrutinized or regulated environments where perception, trust and brand equity directly influence outcomes. Drawing on deep expertise across strategic communications and brand building, crisis communications, legal and litigation PR, government relations, media training, and online reputation management, Red Banyan delivers disciplined, strategy-led communications designed to support business growth and navigate moments that test it. Learn more at https://redbanyan.com.

releases.title: MUSIC DAY IN CANADA BRINGS 60+ CANADIAN ARTISTS TO STAGES ACROSS THE COUNTRY ON SEPTEMBER 26
releases.body:
20 cities and 20+ live events come together for one national day celebrating Canadian music, local venues and the communities that sustain them.

VANCOUVER, BC, Sept. 22, 2026 /CNW/ -- On Saturday, September 26, Music Day in Canada will connect stages across the country for one shared national celebration of Canadian music.

More than 60 artists across 20+ live events in 20 cities will perform as venues, music organizations, local producers and communities come together under one national banner.

From St. John's to Vancouver, Music Day in Canada is built around a simple idea: Canadian music is shaped locally, and those local scenes become stronger when the country pays attention together.

"Canada doesn't have one music scene. It has hundreds of them," says Michael Sriven,  Founder of Music Day In Canada.   "Music Day in Canada gives those communities a shared date and a national platform while keeping the artists, venues and people who build music locally at the centre of it."

The September 26 program stretches across genres, generations and types of stages.

In Saskatoon, six Saskatchewan acts will take over Gather Local Market for five hours of free live music. Edmonton will see multiple independent venues participating across the city. Oshawa will enjoy a free show at the Biltmore theatre featuring Wine Lips, The Anti-Queens, Shiv & the Carvers and Sigh Die . In Barrie, Brian John Harwood, Andy Colonico, Beasley and Graham Scott Fleming will come together for an all-country night at The Queens Hotel.

On the East Coast, events extend through St. John's, Antigonish, New Glasgow, Sydney, Charlottetown, Fredericton, Truro  and Moncton, while additional programming takes place in Winnipeg, Regina, Calgary, Mississauga, Abbotsford, Kelowna, Whitehorse and Vancouver.

Some events are free and all ages. Others take place in established independent music venues. Each city determines what Music Day looks and sounds like in its own community.

LOCAL SCENES. ONE NATIONAL MOMENT.

Music Day in Canada is led by The Lemmon Foundation, with Lemmon Entertainment curating and producing the national platform alongside local venues, producers, artists and music organizations.

Rather than building the same event in every market, Music Day connects existing local infrastructure and new community-led programming through coordinated national promotion, partnerships and visibility.

The model is designed to strengthen the people and places already doing the work: putting artists on stages, bringing audiences into local rooms and creating opportunities for Canadian music to be discovered live.

The day also connects to the Foundation's year-round work supporting artists and aspiring industry professionals through education, mentorship and professional development.

SEPTEMBER 26, 2026

Music Day in Canada takes place Saturday, September 26, with events currently announced in:

Abbotsford • Antigonish • Barrie • Calgary • Charlottetown • Edmonton • Fredericton • Kelowna • Mississauga • Moncton • New Glasgow • Oshawa • Regina • Saskatoon • St. John's • Sydney • Vancouver • Winnipeg • Whitehorse • Truro

Programming and ticketing vary by city.

The complete and continuously updated national schedule is available at musicdayincanada.com.

ABOUT MUSIC DAY IN CANADA

Music Day in Canada connects local stages into one national moment, strengthening visibility, participation and long-term sustainability for live music across the country. Led by The Lemmon Foundation, the initiative brings together artists, venues, producers, music organizations, partners and audiences while allowing each participating community to build programming that reflects its own local music scene.

releases.title: "Detroit Remembers Richard Smallwood" A Concert Tribute to Honor the Gospel Music Icon This October
releases.body:
BMJ Productions and Empowerment Church present a two-night tribute, 50-member choir, legendary Detroit artists and musicians led by Bill Moss Jr. in a celebration of Smallwood's five-decade legacy.

SOUTHFIELD, Mich., Sept. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hundreds of metro Detroiters will pay tribute to one of gospel music's most influential composers this fall, as BMJ Productions LLC and Empowerment Church present Detroit Remembers: Richard Smallwood, a two-night musical tribute concert Friday, October 9 and Saturday, October 10, 2026, at Empowerment Church in Southfield, Michigan sponsored by Salathiel Records. Tickets are available for $30 in advance, $40 at the door and $75 VIP through bmjproductionsll.com or empowermentmi.org.

The event honors Richard Smallwood, the Grammy-nominated composer, pianist and choir director who died in December 2025 at age 77. Over four decades, Smallwood blended classical training earned at Howard University with the fervor of traditional Black gospel, creating songs including "Total Praise," "Center of My Joy" and "I Love the Lord" that reached mainstream audiences through artists such as Whitney Houston and Destiny's Child.

The tribute will bring 15 of his most iconic songs to life through a 50-member choir and celebrated Detroit talent, led by:

  • Bill Moss Jr., Visionary Music Director
  • Pam English, Vocal Director and Master Clinician
  • Alvin Waddles, Principal and Featured Artist
  • Rev. Kimberly Whitsett, Artistic Director
  • Ernest Tolbert, Band Director

Moss, son of gospel great Bill Moss Sr. of Bill Moss and the Celestials and part of the extended Clark Sisters family, brings his own deep Detroit gospel roots to the production, making the concert both a tribute to Smallwood's national legacy and a homecoming for the city's gospel community.

"Richard Smallwood didn't just write songs, he gave the church a new language for worship," said Bill Moss Jr., renowned gospel artist and Art and Music Director for Empowerment Church. "This isn't just a concert, it's a love letter to a man who changed how the world worships. Detroit is going to feel every note."

Sponsorship opportunities are available for organizations that want to connect with a highly engaged audience of faith leaders, music lovers and community members across Southeast Michigan, including logo placement, event visibility and complimentary VIP tickets. Ticket and sponsorship inquiries can be directed to shantl.olovson@gmail.com.

SASKATOON, SK, Sept. 19, 2026 /CNW/ -- Tonight, the Canadian Country Music Association® (CCMA®) marked country music's biggest night in Canada; the 44th annual CCMA Awards. Taking over SaskTel Centre in Saskatoon for the third time, the 2026 CCMA Awards showcased a powerhouse line-up of performers and presenters, celebrating the achievements of Canada's country music community over the last year. For those who want to relive the magic of the evening, or watch for the first time, the 2026 CCMA Awards are streaming on Crave.

Cameron Whitcomb was the big winner of the night, taking home Entertainer of the Year and Male Artist of the Year, while also earning the Ford F-150 Album of the Year award for The Hard Way. Hosts James Barker Band claimed the coveted Fans' Choice award and were named Group or Duo of the Year for the fourth consecutive year, while Meghan Patrick earned her third Female Artist of the Year Award. Sully Burrows was recognized as Breakthrough Artist or Group of the Year presented by FACTOR, with Nate Haller and Tenille Townes taking home Musical Collaboration of the Year for "Backfire." Thelma & James were awarded Video of the Year for "Parking Lot Prayers," and Josh Ross celebrated his third-consecutive win for Single of the Year for "Hate How You Look."

releases.title: Lainey Wilson, Jelly Roll and Lukas Nelson Share Their Songs and Stories at All for the Hall Los Angeles with Special Guest John Mayer
releases.body:
Gala fundraiser concert supports Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum education programs

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- "It's gonna be a good night, I feel it in my bones," Lainey Wilson told the audience gathered at All for the Hall Los Angeles right at the start of the show. "We've got a few surprises up our sleeve."

The intimate, guitar pull-style concert, presented Thursday night (Sept.18) at The Novo featured Wilson alongside Jelly Roll and Lukas Nelson taking turns and sharing songs in the classic Nashville songwriter tradition as part of a fundraiser for the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum's education programs. It was a night of stories, laughter and, true to Wilson's word, musical surprises.

Before the music began, the museum's CEO Kyle Young touched on the ongoing importance of the institution's mission as a place of education and study as country music continues to grow. "The artists, writers and musicians who have come before and are sure to come after us are worthy of study celebration and honor," he said.

The three performers assembled for All for the Hall Los Angeles were excellent examples of the breadth of country music in the present, each working in a distinct lane but appreciative of one another's contributions. Wilson served as the affable and gracious host, calling Jelly Roll and Nelson her "brothers in country music" and thanking them for coming. "I've got some of the best friends in the world," she said. "Every time I holler at y'all to be somewhere, y'all show up. That's a real friend."

For his part, Nelson demonstrated that he's a twin threat as a soulful singer and a masterful guitar player who performs with intensity. His performances included "Just Outside of Austin" about the place where he grew up, "Forget About Georgia" and "More Than Friends," for which Wilson hopped off her stool and swayed to the rhythm as she added harmony vocals. The pair also paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton by performing a portion of the 2013 Kenny Rogers and Parton duet "You Can't Make Old Friends."

Nelson wrapped up with a searing rendition of "Find Yourself," which he wrote while working on the music for the 2018 film "A Star Is Born." The song first appeared on his album Lukas Nelson & Promise of the Real, and it got an immediate endorsement from the film's female lead, Lady Gaga. "She loved it so much," he said. "She sang on the actual recording of the song."

Jelly Roll was quick to show his appreciation of Nelson's talents. "You're so good, it's almost hard to like you," he quipped. His banter kept the audience laughing appreciatively throughout the night, whether he was adding playful asides about Wilson's wedding to Devlin Hodges ("That wedding was fancy. Everything was free!") or his colorful past on the wrong side of the law. The Nashville native effortlessly blended humor with the sincerity of his songs, which were inspired by the struggle, doubt and redemption that have marked his journey, performing his hits "Liar," "I Am Not Okay," "Need a Favor" and "Save Me," which featured powerful vocal accompaniment from Wilson. 

"Thank you for wearing your heart on your sleeve," Wilson said to Jelly Roll.

Wilson was brimming with down-home charm and in fine voice as she talked about her life and journey. As she introduced "4X4XU," she noted that she had married a man who goes by the nickname of "Duck."

"I thought I couldn't get any more redneck, and God's like, 'I've got jokes!'" Wilson talked about her family's history taming horses before launching into "Wildflowers and Wild Horses," and belted the high note of "Heart Like a Truck" with gusto, earning enthusiastic applause as she did it. "I have to sing that note for the rest of my life," she said. "Every time I come up on it, I'm like, 'Lord Jesus, you better be with me now!"

To cap things off, Wilson had a special guest waiting in the wings and brought out John Mayer to the audience's delight. The pair gave the debut live performance of their recently recorded collaboration "Phone, Keys, Wallet," with Mayer adding harmonies and his fluid electric guitar licks. Wilson recalled recording the song and thinking out loud that she wanted Mayer to be a part of it. They managed to catch him in a Los Angeles studio and played the track over a tinny cellphone speaker, but it was more than enough to get him on board. "I said, 'Let's go,'" Mayer recalled.

The spirit of being game and loving the music shone through with each artist's selections throughout the evening, which Wilson described as a nourishing experience. "My heart is so full," Wilson said. "If y'all keep having me, I'll keep being here."

All for the Hall Los Angeles also featured a performance from the museum's flagship education program, Words & Music, which instructs young people on the craft of writing songs. Students from Manual Arts High School in Los Angeles took the stage with acclaimed country songwriters Liz Rose and Phil Barton to perform an original song created through Words & Music, "I'll Overcome," that offered a message of strength and resilience.

Festivities for All for the Hall kicked off Wednesday (Sept. 17) with a reception for invited attendees at the Los Angeles home of Sarah and Neil Moritz. Songwriters Hillary Lindsey, Lori McKenna and Liz Rose — known collectively as the Love Junkies — were joined by Phil Barton to give a backyard serenade of hits including such award-winning songs as "Humble and Kind," "Blue Ain't Your Color," "You Belong with Me" and "Girl Crush."

All for the Hall was envisioned in 2005 by Country Music Hall of Fame member and board president Vince Gill, who proposed the idea of donating proceeds from one annual performance to the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum. In the two decades since, All for the Hall concerts have raised more than $8 million in support of the museum's educational initiatives. Funds raised from the concerts support the museum's educational initiatives, which directly served more than 125,000 people last year through in-person and virtual programs.

About All for the Hall

Launched in 2007, the All for the Hall campaign began with Country Music Hall of Fame member and Museum Board President Vince Gill challenging himself and his fellow artists to donate proceeds of one annual performance to the nonprofit museum. The concert series has rotated between New York, Los Angeles and Dallas. Keith Urban has hosted recurring All for the Hall benefit concerts in Nashville since 2009. In 2024, Blake Shelton hosted an All for the Hall benefit concert in Oklahoma. Funds raised from the events support the museum's educational initiatives, which directly served more than 125,000 people last year through in-person and virtual programs.

About Words & Music

Words & Music® is the Museum's flagship education program that teaches people how to write original songs and connects them to Nashville's professional songwriting community through interactive workshops. For nearly 50 years, Words & Music has served nearly 200,000 participants and currently engages more than 14,000 participants each year — locally, nationally and internationally. Words & Music empowers people to express themselves and share their stories through songwriting. Songwriting builds essential academic skills and supports overall well-being for people of all ages.

About the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum:

The Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum collects, preserves and interprets country music and its history for the education and entertainment of diverse audiences. In exhibitions, publications, digital media and educational programs, the museum explores the cultural importance and enduring beauty of the art form. Among the most-visited history museums in the United States, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum was awarded the country's highest honor in the arts, the National Medal of Arts, in 2024. Accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, the museum is operated by the Country Music Foundation, a not-for-profit 501(c)(3) educational organization chartered by the state of Tennessee in 1964. The Country Music Foundation operates Historic RCA Studio B®, Hatch Show Print® poster shop, Haley Gallery, CMA Theater, CMF Records, the Frist Library and Archive and CMF Press. Museum programs are supported in part by the Tennessee Arts Commission.

More information about the Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum is available at www.countrymusichalloffame.org or by calling (615) 416-2001.

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- It's time for a new doll in the dollhouse. MGA Entertainment (MGA), the company behind Bratz®, Rainbow High® and L.O.L. Surprise!®, today released Mirror Mi's first original single and cinematic music video, bringing the brand's six emotion-inspired characters to life through music and live-action storytelling. With the fashion dolls already available at major retailers nationwide, the debut invites fans deeper into Mirror Mi, a connected world where dolls, original music, fashion and emotional storytelling come together.

At the heart of Mirror Mi are six fashion dolls, each embodying a signature emotion through her own distinct personality, point of view and style. Highly detailed fashions, striking silhouettes, long rooted hair, premium styling, 15 points of articulation and collectible accessories make each doll as expressive as the character she represents, giving fans a tangible way to connect with her story and explore the feelings that make her unique.

The cinematic music video takes those personalities and emotions beyond the dollhouse and into an elite performing arts academy, where the characters pursue their creative passions while navigating friendship, self-expression and change. As their feelings evolve and their auras shift, they discover the unique power within every emotion. For the first time, fans can experience the characters' individual styles and relationships unfolding together on screen.

Produced in partnership with London Alley Entertainment, the award-winning creative studio behind some of today's biggest music videos, the release marks the first doll-based project directed by Grammy-nominated filmmaker Colin Tilley, whose distinctive visual storytelling has helped shape some of today's biggest artists.

"With Mirror Mi, we set out to create a world as layered and expressive as the fans it was created for," said Josh Hackbarth, Chief Marketing Officer at MGA Entertainment. "The dolls are the first point of connection, but music and storytelling allow us to reveal so much more about who these characters are and the emotions that shape them. Every look, lyric and storyline uncovers another side of their personalities, giving fans another opportunity to connect and see themselves reflected in these characters."

Meet the six core characters of Mirror Mi:

  • Blaze Maxx™ (Electric): She's tough, outspoken, and brave. Her rockstar energy amps up her friends and fans. She's fiercely loyal and will always have your back.
  • Amora Valentina™ (Love): When she is not crushing, she is gushing about her love for her friends! She has the biggest heart and always sees the good in people.
  • Luna Skye™ (Dreamy): People say she has her head in the clouds, but that's only so she can whisper to the moon. She's full of whimsical ideas, always dream journaling and perfecting her night-time skin care routine.
  • Akiko Kittyama™ (Cozy): She adores all things comfy and cozy! Whether she's planning the perfect chill day or giving a big, warm hug, she knows how to make everyone feel right at home.
  • Shai Meadows™ (Sheepish): Sweet, quiet, and gentle, Shai may not always say what's on her mind, but her kindness and creativity speak for itself. She can make her friends smile without saying a peep!
  • Suki Goldpetal™ (Fragile): Soft-spoken and sensitive, she feels everything deeply. She might appear delicate, but she dances like nobody's watching. When she embraces who she is, she shines like gold. 

The debut music video marks the beginning of Mirror Mi's next chapter across product and entertainment. The story will continue through stylized stop-motion films and an animated short-form series launching later this year, giving fans more ways to follow the characters, their relationships and their emotional journeys.

The brand will also expand its product lineup with Mirror Mi Mini Dolls, small reflections with supercharged emotions. Rather than miniature replicas of the fashion dolls, each four-inch Mini Mi reimagines a character's signature feeling as a heightened collectible expression all its own, designed to be customized, posed, displayed and taken on the go.

Mirror Mi fashion dolls are available now at major retailers nationwide. The debut music video is streaming now on YouTube. Mini Mis launch in October, with select styles available for preorder at MGAE Shop beginning September 23.

For more information and updates on upcoming releases, follow @MirrorMiOfficial on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and Spotify.

MGA Entertainment is on a mission to inspire imagination and creativity through innovative toys, entertainment, and experiences that transform play into limitless possibilities. As the largest privately held toy and entertainment company in the U.S., MGA is a global leader in designing and delivering world-class consumer products that spark wonder and drive play forward. Headquartered in Los Angeles with offices worldwide, MGA's portfolio spans a dynamic range of original and licensed brands — from toys, dolls, games, and electronics to fashion, home décor, and entertainment content including hit movies and TV series. The company is recognized for its bold approach to storytelling, trendsetting design, and deep commitment to quality. The award-winning MGA family includes fan-favorite brands such as L.O.L. releases.body:
AMSTERDAM, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Let's be honest. The live music industry still runs its operations across email threads and spreadsheets at large. Booking agencies, artists, managers and crews coordinate deals, contracts, logistics, and money through systems that were never designed to connect.

ABOSS spent the past decade building an operating system for live music, to solve this problem from a place of deep industry experience. Booking agencies, artists, and crews can manage their shows in one structured environment; from the back-office to center-stage. However, while the hustle is real and the front-end often catches the spotlight, the adoption of new technology in the back-end can move like a slow jam on a Sunday afternoon.

"After all those years, deals are still made on relationships, and they're still being executed in chaos," said Arvid Silos, founder of ABOSS. "If your data lives in inboxes and spreadsheets, you're leaving margins on the table."

ABOSS is built with structured collaboration, dealmaking and business logistics in mind across two environments on the same record. The Agency Platform is where booking agencies run deals, contracts, financial tracking, planning, and pre-production. Artist Pro is where artists and their teams access, review, and work on the same data. A true single source of truth solution.

That split is also the platform's position on who owns the data. Operational information in live music has long sat with the agency, or been scattered across inboxes and spreadsheets. Agencies running on ABOSS are already offering artists a record they can own, access and control, while the agency continues to run the operation. The infrastructure has been there for a decade. However, hardly any artist or manager claims it: of the roughly $1 billion in deal value moving through ABOSS this year, artist-owned records cover about 4%.

A mobile application extends that record onto the road: schedules, travel, and ops, available offline, with summaries. Records are exposed through an open API to empower a new layer of specialized workflows and integrations to improve the live music stack.

SAPPS AI, offering platform-agnostic AI-native micro-apps for live music, is one of those layers that recognizes the power of ABOSS as a system of data supply. AI Models need data that is substantial, owned, structured, secure, and current, contextualized to specific business cases. AI does not replace architecture. That's where ABOSS turns admin into a commercial opportunity in the age of AI.

It's one thing to jump on the AI hypetrain, it's another thing to diligently navigate it, nurturing trust and strongholding this promise ABOSS built the operating system for live music on; to elevate the way we all work in music.

releases.title: Toronto Sauna Festival Transforms Evergreen Brick Works into a Three-Day Celebration of Sauna, Cold, Music and Movement
releases.body:
Following a sold-out debut, Toronto's sauna culture gets a major expansion with 20+ saunas, international sauna masters, immersive rituals, bigger music acts and triple the amount of wellness programming

TORONTO, Sept. 17, 2026 /CNW/ -- Sauna culture has exploded beyond the traditional spa--and Toronto is getting a three-day festival built around it.

Produced by Unbounded, this year's festival will transform Evergreen Brick Works into a sprawling wellness playground, occupying more than three times the footprint of its debut, bringing together hundreds of sauna rituals, world-class Aufguss masters and practitioners from across Canada and Europe, alongside movement classes, cold plunges, live music, DJs, breathwork, sound experiences, recovery treatments, food and more.

The result is less a traditional wellness event and more a three-day social and cultural experience built around the rituals of heat and cold.

"Last year showed us that people are looking for something much bigger than simply going to a sauna," says Nick McNaught, founder of Unbounded. "We saw 1,500 people come together to sweat, plunge, move, listen to music and connect with each other. That response gave us the confidence to completely rethink what this event could become. This year, we've tripled the space, expanded to three days and brought together sauna traditions and talent from around the world, while creating a place where people can spend hours exploring, whether they step into a sauna or not."

Sauna Culture from around the world meets Festival Culture 

At the center of the festival will be a constantly changing program of guided rituals and free-flow experiences within the sauna village. 

International sauna masters and practitioners from Germany, Poland, Romania and Estonia will join Canadian talent to showcase the breadth of global sauna culture--from highly performative Aufguss ceremonies and herbal infusions to body scrubs and traditional Banya-inspired rituals.

Cold immersion will run throughout the festival, with both guided and free-flow plunges giving guests the opportunity to move between heat and cold at their own pace.

But the festival is designed to be about more than what happens inside a sauna.

Guests can move through an expanded wellness landscape featuring yoga and Pilates, breathwork and sound baths, meditation, recovery and longevity experiences, skin and herbal treatments, live music and DJs, as well as food, tea and non-alcoholic beverages. Interactive installations and unexpected activations will be woven throughout the Evergreen Brick Works site. 

KC Roberts, Meagan Delima [performed for Barack Obama], The Coffee Party and more will take over different elements of the festival's entertainment programming. 

A New Immersive Opening Night: October 2

Toronto Sauna Festival will kick off its 2026 edition with A Journey Through the Elements, a signature opening-night celebration on October 2 that invites guests into an immersive world, culminating into a one-night only artistic centrepiece.

Guests will begin their journey into the festival by cycling through four elemental zones: Earth, Air, Water and Fire. At the heart of the evening is a large-scale performance inspired by these elements, transforming the main space into a theatre for one-night only. Each element will be interpreted through a different wellness and artistic practice, from Aufguss to Cymatics, fire breathing to live music, this night marks the beginning of a weekend designed to blur the lines between wellness, nightlife and culture.

A Festival You Can Make Your Own

Rather than following a traditional festival schedule, Toronto Sauna Festival is designed around choice and discovery.

Saturday and Sunday programming will include a variety of sessions, each with their own atmosphere and lineup. Guests can move between saunas, cold plunges, guided rituals, movement classes, recovery spaces, music, food and other activities at their own pace.

The festival reflects the growing evolution of sauna and cold culture: practices that were once primarily associated with health and recovery are increasingly becoming social spaces--places to gather, meet people, listen to music, move, relax and experience something together.

October 2–4, 2026

Evergreen Brick Works

Toronto, Ontario

In partnership with Therme Group.

Tickets and festival information are available at torontosaunafestival.com.

Unbounded creates social wellness experiences built around sauna, cold immersion and community. Through these experiences, Unbounded is helping introduce a new generation to sauna culture in Toronto.

releases.title: Regal Delivers Its Biggest Domestic Summer at the Box Office Since 2018
releases.body:
Revenues up 35.3% thanks to strong performance with the biggest movies of the summer

KNOXVILLE, Tenn., Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Regal's gross domestic box office revenues grew more than 35% year-over-year this summer, marking the company's biggest summer in eight years.

Performance in the period (May 1-Sept. 7) was driven by outstanding delivery across all movies with particular strength on the biggest films of the summer, Spider-Man: Brand New Day and The Odyssey. The company took 18.2% of share on Spider-Man and 19.5% of The Odyssey, both well ahead of its 16.5% share of the market as a whole.

"A summer like this starts with filmmakers and studios making films that people really want to see on a big screen, and there have been a lot of them already this year," said Eduardo Acuña, Chief Executive Officer of Regal Global Entertainment. "The slate had real depth and range to it, and audiences kept coming back to share it with family and friends. I'm grateful to Regal's theatre teams who worked so hard to look after moviegoers, and to the staff in our offices who set the summer up so well. Our partners are putting money into films worth seeing, and we're putting money into the experience of watching them—moviegoers get the benefit of both."

The depth of the movie slate this summer played a key part in the success of the season. Alongside the summer's two biggest releases, Toy Story 5, Michael, The Mandalorian and Grogu, Obsession, The Devil Wears Prada 2, Backrooms, and Minions & Monsters each brought a different audience into theatres. The strength of the schedule was consistent from the first weekend in May through Labor Day rather than being concentrated in a handful of dates.

Premium large formats continue to contribute to ongoing growth through company investment in renovating theatres with expanded premium offerings including the recently opened Regal Sherman Oaks Galleria in Los Angeles. Regal's premium format box office rose 63% year over year and represented 22% of the circuit's summer revenue in the period, up from 18% a year ago, and contributing a third of the company's total increase. IMAX revenue at Regal more than doubled, RPX grew 80%, ScreenX grew 45%, and 4DX grew 13%. Premium formats made up more than 60% of Regal's gross on The Odyssey, a third on The Mandalorian and Grogu, and a quarter on Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Standard format revenue grew 29% over the same period, showing that the increase came from across the circuit rather than from premium alone.

About Regal Global Entertainment

Regal Global Entertainment operates the second-largest theatrical exhibition business in the world with 7,648 screens across 629 locations. Through its Cinema City, Cineworld, Picturehouse, Planet, and Regal brands, the company is committed to delivering exceptional moviegoing experiences through premium large formats, innovative loyalty and subscription programs, enhanced food and beverage offerings, and outstanding guest service.

releases.body:
Agreement establishes new cross-border pathway for artists, labels, and rights holders

WASHINGTON, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SoundExchange, the largest neighboring rights organization in the world, and Music Nation Copyrights Management (MusicNation), a pioneer in music rights management in the United Arab Emirates, today announced the signing of a groundbreaking reciprocal agreement to strengthen cross-border neighboring rights administration and create new revenue streams for rights holders in the United States and the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

The agreement builds on SoundExchange's previously announced partnership with MusicNation to provide technology, data, and industry expertise supporting neighboring rights administration in the UAE. Together with MusicNation's partnership with BMI, the agreement reflects MusicNation's pivotal role in building the UAE's premier music licensing and royalty distribution infrastructure across neighboring rights, public performance rights, and mechanical rights. MusicNation was established as a collective management organization (CMO) to ensure that local and international performing artists, record labels, songwriters, publishers, and other rights holders are fully and fairly compensated for the use of their works in the UAE and, through reciprocal arrangements, in other markets where their works are used commercially. 

Michael Huppe, President and CEO of SoundExchange, said, "This groundbreaking reciprocal agreement with Music Nation will open a new revenue stream for SoundExchange artists and rights owners whose music is played in the UAE while ensuring Emirati creators are compensated when their music is played in the United States. It also enables SoundExchange to seamlessly provide these services for some of its partner CMOs around the world, who have the option of collecting UAE royalties through their existing agreements with SoundExchange."

For MusicNation, the agreement represents another step in developing a globally connected rights management framework for the UAE. As the country's music, entertainment, hospitality, and cultural sectors continue to expand, MusicNation is building the infrastructure needed to support trusted licensing, transparent royalty collection, and accurate distribution for creators and rights holders in the UAE and around the world.

Rasha Khalifa Al Mubarak, Chairwoman of MusicNation, said, "Music is one of the most powerful expressions of identity, culture, and human artistry. As the UAE continues to develop and attract foreign investment into its creative economy, we have a responsibility to build the systems that ensure artists and rights holders are respected, and that musical IP is protected and fairly compensated to global standards. This agreement with SoundExchange represents a national and industry milestone, advancing MusicNation's mission to create a transparent, globally connected music rights ecosystem in the UAE and strengthens the foundation for a more sustainable creative future for our region."

Amer M. Samhoun, CEO of MusicNation, said, "This agreement marks a pivotal step in MusicNation's international role as the UAE's music rights infrastructure continues to expand. It gives international CMOs and rights partners confidence that they can work with MusicNation in the UAE through a transparent and efficient system, and participate in the opportunities created by one of the region's fastest-growing creative markets."

SoundExchange manages a worldwide network of more than 100 agreements with CMOs, covering 93% of the available global neighboring rights market. Nearly 600,000 artists and rights owners entrust SoundExchange to collect worldwide royalties on their behalf. Its agreement with MusicNation adds the UAE to that network and supports greater connection between the nation's rights holders and the global neighboring rights ecosystem.

About MusicNation

MusicNation, a pioneer in music rights management in the UAE, licenses the rights of authors, publishers, sound recording owners and performers throughout the United Arab Emirates (UAE). These rights are referred to as neighboring rights (for sound recordings), public performance rights (for musical compositions) and mechanical reproduction rights (also for musical compositions). With world-class partnerships and technology, MusicNation is helping implement the UAE's vision for the protection and enforcement of musical copyrights by developing a world-class music licensing and royalty distribution infrastructure. MusicNation, with its partners BMI and SoundExchange, will help ensure that music creators and rights holders are fully and fairly compensated for the use of their work. For more information, visit https://www.wearemusicnation.ae.

About SoundExchange

SoundExchange is the largest global neighboring rights organization in the world, redefining how creators in the music industry get paid. By turning data into fast, accurate revenue for artists and rights owners, we have collected and distributed more than $13 billion in digital performance royalties to date on behalf of more than 800,000 music creators. As the sole organization designated by the U.S. government to administer the Section 114 sound recording license, SoundExchange seamlessly collects and distributes digital performance royalties from platforms like Pandora, SiriusXM, iHeartRadio, and thousands more, as well as all available international performance royalties through a strong global partnership network. For more information, visit soundexchange.com.

releases.body:
The four-part mystery drama from creator Mark E. Swinton, executive produced by Tyler Perry, released all four episodes at once

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Clark Moore, the Laredo, Texas-born actor with more than 65 credits across television, film, and video games, appears as Lt. Jeff Gibson in Route 187, the four-part mystery drama now streaming exclusively on Paramount+. All four episodes were released Wednesday, September 16, 2026.

Created, written, and directed by Mark E. Swinton and executive produced by Swinton and Tyler Perry for Tyler Perry Studios, Route 187 is set in the fictional, crumbling city of South Winslow and follows the residents who depend on the city's bus route. The story opens with the brutal murders of a bus driver and a high school basketball star, beaten to death on a bus, an act that ignites community outrage and pulls authorities into a hunt for the culprits caught on video. As the investigation widens, it collides with a string of missing Black women cases and a killer who has operated undetected for years. The series stars Christopher Livingston, Elijah Collins, Tonia Jackson, Lawrence Robinson, Rico Ball, and Cuyle Carvin, alongside Moore.

"Clark brought a steadiness to this set that you notice immediately. He shows up prepared, he listens, and he makes the scene better for everyone standing in it. I'm glad audiences are finally going to see this work."

Cuyle Carvin, actor, Route 187 (Paramount+)

Moore plays Lt. Jeff Gibson, a police lieutenant working the South Winslow case as it grows from a single bus stop into something far larger than the community first understood.

"South Winslow is fiction, but the pattern underneath it is not. Cases like these get worked hard when the cameras are on and quietly shelved when they aren't. Mark Swinton wrote a show that refuses to let that go, and playing a man carrying the weight of that investigation was the kind of work you don't get offered every year."

Clark Moore, actor (Lt. Jeff Gibson, Route 187)

Route 187 arrives with a festival run already behind it. The series was an official selection of the 7th Annual LightReel Film Festival in Washington, D.C., where it opened the festival in June 2026, and was officially accepted into the RSF Martha's Vineyard African American Film Festival, one of the summer's most closely watched showcases for Black storytelling.

The role also lands squarely in the territory Moore is best known for. Much of his career has been built on blue-collar authority in detective, lawman, and military parts, from SEAL Team and NCIS to S.W.A.T. and Yellowstone, and Lt. Gibson extends that line into one of the most talked-about independent productions of the year.

Route 187 closes out a three-production year for the SAG-AFTRA actor. Moore appeared as Detective Moreno in Lifetime's Murder in Music City, which premiered in February, and as guest star Caleb Easton in Hulu's Furious, the Elizabeth Meriwether crime thriller that ran through August.

Moore's career highlights include a recurring role as D.A. Stanny Sanders in the ABC limited series Women of the Movement, executive produced by Will Smith and Jay-Z, and a leading performance in Aaron Mahnke's Amazon Prime series Lore. Born and raised on his father's ranch in Laredo, Texas, Moore studied film at The University of Texas at Austin before relocating to Los Angeles. His special skills include Krav Maga, weapons handling, and horseback riding, capabilities that inform his approach to tactical, military, and western roles.

All four episodes of Route 187 are now streaming exclusively on Paramount+. The official trailer is available on YouTube, and the series can be followed on Instagram at @route.187.

For more information about Clark Moore and his complete filmography, visit officialclarkmoore.com/credits or his profile on IMDb.

releases.title: Aristotle Jones Launches Campaign to Establish July as "Appalachian Soul Month" With Release of New Album and Book
releases.body:
Appalachian Soul Power and Companion Novel Mountain Alchemy Arrive September 22, 2026

Campaign Launch Celebrates the Artists, Music and Cultural Traditions That Have Helped Shape Appalachia's Place in Music History

OSAGE, W.Va., Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Award-winning West Virginia singer, songwriter, storyteller, and author Aristotle Jones, known as "The Appalachian Soul Man," will mark the September 22 release of his new album, Appalachian Soul Power, and companion book, Mountain Alchemy, by launching a campaign to establish July as Appalachian Soul Month, celebrating the artists, music, and cultural traditions that have helped give Appalachia its soul.

The Appalachian Soul Month campaign seeks to establish an annual celebration spotlighting the many sounds of Appalachia and their place in the larger story of American music. The initiative will honor the artists who came before, celebrate those carrying those traditions forward, and encourage new audiences to discover and share Appalachian music and culture.

"For me, Appalachian Soul has never been about creating another genre or putting a new label on the music," Jones said. "It is about recognizing what has always been here. Soul, Gospel, Blues, Folk, Country, R&B, and Rock & Roll have crossed paths in Appalachia for generations. Artists from these mountains, towns, churches, clubs, front porches, and communities have helped shape American music, even when Appalachia hasn't always been included in that story."

As part of the campaign launch, Jones is asking people to share an Appalachian artist who has moved them, inspired them, or deserves to be discovered. Participants can honor an artist from the past, introduce someone making music today, or share a favorite song, performance, photograph, memory, or story using #AppalachianSoulMonth.

The campaign coincides with the release of Appalachian Soul Power, a 10-track album drawing from the region's vast musical traditions. Percussive guitar, piano, horns, layered vocals, and a tightly connected rhythm section move throughout the record, shifting between intimate moments and high-energy arrangements.

The album serves as a musical companion to Mountain Alchemy, a fictional work Jones drew from family and community stories that peppered his childhood. Together, the projects explore Black Appalachian culture, resilience, community, and cultural memory, with the songs providing a musical landscape for themes at the heart of the book.

"I can't think of a better way to release this record than by using the moment to celebrate something much bigger than me," Jones said. "I want us to remember the artists who came before us, celebrate the people making music here today, and introduce each other to voices we may not know yet."

Jones was named a 2026 United States Artists Fellow, selected for the 2026–2027 Central Appalachia Living Traditions Emerging Artists Cohort, funded by Mid Atlantic Arts, and featured on the Summer 2026 cover of Morgantown Magazine. In July, Jones and his band won the International Blues Competition Affiliate Challenge and will represent West Virginia at the 43rd International Blues Challenge, January 19–23, 2027, in Memphis.

Appalachian Soul Power and Mountain Alchemy are available beginning September 22, 2026, via Jonesin' Records.

releases.body:
PHILADELPHIA, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This Kids Music Day, Keep Music Alive is inviting people across the country to grab anything they can find and start drumming. The nonprofit's "Drum on Anything" Challenge is a fun, social media-driven campaign encouraging musicians, students, families and music fans of all ages to post a short video of themselves "drumming ON anything WITH anything" while helping raise awareness and support for music education. Inspired by the ALS Ice Bucket Challenge, participants are asked to use #DrumOnAnything, tag three friends to take part, and either share their own video or make a donation to a music education nonprofit of their choice. Music education organizations nationwide are also encouraged to use the challenge to engage supporters and raise funds for their own programs.

More than 1,200 locations across all 50 U.S. states, Canada and 15 additional countries are expected to participate in the 11th Annual Kids Music Day, with special events and promotions designed to celebrate and support children making music. Kids Music Day activities will take place from Friday, September 18 through Sunday, October 11. Families in the United States and Canada can find participating events in their area by entering their ZIP or postal code on the locator page at KidsMusicDay.org. International participants can find events by scrolling below the map and selecting their country's flag.

Kids Music Day events will feature a wide variety of hands-on and family-friendly activities, including musical instrument petting zoos, student performances, free trial music lessons, kids open mics, ukulele, drum and guitar circles, instrument donation drives, special Kids Music Day promotions and more. These activities are designed to give children more opportunities to experience the joy of making music while highlighting the importance of music education in communities around the world.

Kids Music Day is supported by a number of popular family-friendly brands including CASIO, Kala Brand Music, Independence Blue Cross, Les Paul Foundation, Music Nomad Equipment Care, Panyard, Remo Percussion and Taylor Guitars.  Keep Music Alive is honored to welcome these valued partners, helping to support more kids to start their own musical journey.

13-year-old violinist Sabrina Patel returns as Kids Music Day Spokesperson this year as she continues her quest to perform the National Anthem at major events in all 50 states.  Currently young Sabrina is 90% complete on her quest having performed in 45 States at major sporting and other events. Major league sports teams welcoming Sabrina so far include MLB's Texas Rangers (ALCS Playoffs), Colorado Rockies, Cleveland Guardians, Detroit Tigers, Boston Red Sox, NBA's Dallas Mavericks, Detroit Pistons, Charlotte Hornets, Atlanta Hawks and WNBA's Connecticut Sun

Over a dozen celebrity artists are also showing their support for Music Education by lending their name as Kids Music Day Ambassadors including:   Julie Andrews, Jack Black, Ann & Nancy Wilson of Heart, Pat Benatar & Neil Giraldo, Michael Feinstein, Kenny Loggins, Richie Sambora, Sarah McLachlan, Vanessa Williams, Victor Wooten, Todd Rundgren, Neil Nayyar, Philip Lawrence, Bernie Williams, Damien Escobar and Mandy Harvey.

Helmed by Richard Gordy, Rooted in Craft takes viewers on a journey into the factories, foundries, and quarries, showing a unique behind-the-scenes look at the process that HTD's handmade furniture goes through before the product is ever shipped to your door. Filmed on location in Rajasthan, India, and in Austin, Texas, this documentary shows a whole different side of the industry that is often never seen.

The Best Documentary recognition, certified by Festival Director Ali Alkhafaji and the rest of the panel, comes as HTD looks to expand the work of its Mango Foundation. Building on more than a decade of planting trees, the foundation's next chapter will introduce new sustainability initiatives, including efforts to test and improve access to clean drinking water in HTD's operating communities.

The Austin Spotlight Film Festival, celebrating a decade of championing independent filmmakers, announced the winners following a weekend of screenings and industry events. For more information and to view the full list of the 2026 award winners, please visit the official Austin Spotlight Film Festival website at: https://www.austinspotlightfilmfestival.com/2026-awards 

To watch the award-winning documentary Rooted in Craft, you can view the full film here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jfj1bREUl5c.

About Home Trends & Design: Home Trends & Design (HTD) is an Austin-based furniture company specializing in sustainable, handcrafted solid wood furniture. Dedicated to exceptional heirloom-quality construction, HTD emphasizes eco-friendly practices, sustainable materials, and low-VOC finishes across its collections. By partnering directly with global artisans, HTD celebrates the intersection of traditional craftsmanship and modern design, while its Mango Foundation drives ongoing environmental and community initiatives worldwide.
