releases.title: HIGH LINE AND CHANEL CULTURE FUND CO-COMMISSION ALISON NGUYEN FOR FIFTH HIGH LINE ORIGINALS FILM
releases.body:
Nguyenʼs Prior Occupants Unearths the Industrial and Cultural Histories of the High Line and Westbethʼs Past

NEW YORK, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The High Line and CHANEL Culture Fund today announced that Prior Occupants, a new film by Alison Nguyen commissioned by the High Line as the fifth High Line Originals film, and the second High Line Originals co-commissioned with CHANEL Culture Fund, is now on view. The High Line Channel, located in the High Lineʼs covered passage at 14th Street, screens Prior Occupants daily from 10am to 10pm on a loop, through November 16, 2026.

Prior Occupants explores the obscure nuclear history of Westbeth Artist Housing's building—the former headquarters for Bell Laboratories, a research facility tied to the development of communication technologies and, later, the atomic bomb. Inspired by a severed fragment of the original High Line freight rail left embedded in Westbeth's facade, and the High Line's own history of transformation, Nguyen reflects on the historical narratives that persist—and those quietly erased—within sites of adaptive reuse.

"Through extensive research, ongoing conversations and relationship-building with Westbeth residents past and present, and highly crafted visual choreography, Alison Nguyenʼs Prior Occupants sheds vital light on the industrial and scientific legacies built into our surroundings,ˮ said Taylor Zakarin, associate curator of High Line Art. "Iʼm thrilled the High Line and CHANEL Culture Fund could collaborate with Alison to bring this compelling work to life, and to present it outdoors by the very spaces she investigates.ˮ

"Great artists enter into a dialogue with history, revealing new ways to understand the present. Through her new commission, Alison Nguyen excavates the layered histories surrounding the High Line, uncovering a legacy of innovation and human experimentation—and raising questions about technology, memory, and our shared future that feel more urgent than ever,ˮ said Yana Peel, President of Arts, Culture & Heritage, CHANEL. "CHANEL Culture Fund is proud to continue our partnership with the High Line in support of artists whose original ideas celebrate the singular power of human imagination. By bringing ambitious moving-image commissions into public space, we hope to spark curiosity and reflection for the millions of people who encounter them amid the extraordinary urban landscape of the High Line.ˮ

"I'm grateful for the support of the High Line and CHANEL Culture Fund which gave me the resources to create a work that examines the invisible structures of power embedded in a site,ˮ said artist Alison Nguyen. "As the filmmaking process unfolded, relationships I formed with past and present Westbeth artists along with architectural archives opened up directions for the film which I had not anticipated, and was thrilled by.ˮ

Long before Westbeth's conversion into a historic public housing community for artists in 1970, the site was occupied by Western Electric and later Bell Labs—a crucible of innovation where critical cinema, telecommunications, and military technologies were researched, including components later used in the development of the atomic bomb.

Both Bell Labs and Westbeth Artist Housing are places created to pursue large, even utopian ideals. In the case of the former, technological innovation; in the case of the latter government-funded artist housing. Prior Occupants explores what remains of the pursuit of these ideals, how the surrounding architecture has shaped its inhabitants, and the contradictions of present-day Westbeth in the context of the High Lineʼs surrounding neighborhood.

Prior Occupants is an assemblage of audiovisual material including sculpturally re-filmed archival documents, choreographed performance sequences, and layered fragments of audio interviews with the very residents and architects who have shaped Westbeth and the High Line. Through this collage of voices and textures, the artist explores individual and collective relationships to place, technological acceleration, and mortality, and foregrounds the ways in which the structures of the past quietly haunt our future-present. Questioning the relationship between ruination and cultural production, the work asks: What does it mean to stage the decay of an industrial past within public environments and within public artist housing? What role does nature play in these acts of preservation?

Nguyenʼs film weaves together infrastructure, memory, and technology to consider how the legacy of the nuclear age continues to shape our collective experiences, and positions the High Line not just as a space for leisure, but as an active conduit of our historical consciousness.

Alison Nguyen is a visual artist working across video, installation, performance and painting. Using approaches of speculative fiction, documentary research and embodied performance, Nguyen creates works that reconsider how narratives operate within the individual, the institution, the archive, and within the politics of cultural memory.

In addition to Prior Occupants, CHANEL Culture Fund and High Line Art presented a special two-day screening, on September 6 and 7, of two prior commissions from The Window, CHANEL Culture Fund's site-specific public art program in Central London for cutting-edge works exploring the breadth of todayʼs digital technologies. The screening featured Our Bodies (2024-2025), by Cecilia Bengolea, and Inhale/Exhale (2021) by Noémie Goudal.

Another work from The Window, The Last Post (2010) by Shahzia Sikander, will be included in a forthcoming High Line Channel exhibition alongside The Hedge ofi Halomancy (2025) by the artist duo Hylozoic/Desires (artist Himali Singh Soin and musician David Soin Tappeser) in November 2026. Following its exhibition on the High Line, Prior Occupants will screen at The Window in London.

Part of High Line Channel, High Line Originals is High Line Artʼs commissioning program for artists working in time-based media. This initiative invites emerging or underrecognized US-based artists, nominated by a trusted group of contemporary curators, to submit a proposal for a new video work that considers the context of the park in a meaningful way and will resonate with our diverse audience.

High Line Originals launched in 2019 with Tourmalineʼs Salacia, which is now held in the Museum of Modern Artʼs permanent collection. Other past commissions include Onyeka Igweʼs The Miracle on George Green (2021) and Alicia Mersyʼs NYC Wisdom (2024). In 2025, High Line Art partnered with CHANEL Culture Fund, and together co-commissioned Frank WANG Yefengʼs Groundless Flower – ཨ (2025).

ABOUT THE ARTIST

Alison Nguyen (b. 1986, Wilmington, Delaware) lives and works in New York, New York. Solo screenings and exhibitions of Nguyen's work have been presented at Storefront for Art and Architecture, New York, New York (2026); Art Basel Hong Kong Encounters, Hong Kong (2025); Murmurs, Los Angeles (2024); Museum of Modern Art, New York, New York (2023); MIT List Center for Visual Arts, Cambridge, Massachusetts (2023); and e-flux, Brooklyn, New York (2023). Nguyen has participated in group exhibitions and screenings at the Busan Biennial, Busan, South Korea (2026); Kunsthalle Mechelen, Mechelen, Belgium (2026); Vienna Secession, Vienna, Austria (2024); EMAP x Frieze Seoul Film, Seoul, South Korea (2024); National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Korea, Seoul, South Korea (2023); The Everson Museum, Syracuse, New York (2022); The Dowse Art Museum, Lower Hutt, New Zealand (2021); The International Studio & Curatorial Program, Brooklyn, New York (2019 & 2020); KAJE, Brooklyn, New York (2020); and Microscope Gallery, Brooklyn, New York (2017).

She has participated in film festivals around the world, including Oberhausen International Film Festival, International Shorts Online (2021); CPH:DOX, Copenhagen, Denmark (2021); Edinburgh International Film Festival, Edinburgh, United Kingdom (2021); Ann Arbor Film Festival, Ann Arbor, Michigan (2020); Open City Documentary Festival, London, United Kingdom (2019); Channels Festival International Biennial of Video Art, Melbourne, Australia (2019), and True/False Film Festival, Columbia, Missouri (2018); among others.

Nguyen has received residencies and fellowships from Pioneer Works, New York Foundation for the Arts Artist Fellowship in Film/Video, International Studio & Curatorial Program, The Institute of Electronic Arts, BRIC, and Squeaky Wheel Film and Media Art Center. She was a 2023-2024 Studio Fellow at the Whitney Independent Study Program.

ABOUT HIGH LINE ART

Founded in 2009, High Line Art commissions and produces a wide array of artworks on the High Line, including site-specific commissions, exhibitions, performances, video programs, and a series of billboard interventions. Led by Cecilia Alemani, the Donald R. Mullen, Jr. Director & Chief Curator of High Line Art, and presented by the High Line, the art program invites artists to think of creative ways to engage with the unique architecture, history, and design of the park, and to foster a productive dialogue with the surrounding neighborhood and urban landscape.

For more information on High Line Art, please visit thehighline.org/art.

ABOUT THE HIGH LINE

The High Line is a public park on the West Side of Manhattan operated, maintained, and funded by the nonprofit conservancy Friends of the High Line. Through our work with communities on and off the High Line, Friends of the High Line is devoted to reimagining public spaces to create connected, healthy neighborhoods and cities.

Built on a historic, elevated rail line, the High Line was always intended to be more than a park. You can walk through the gardens, view art, experience a performance, enjoy food or beverage, or connect with friends and neighbors—all while enjoying a unique perspective of New York City.

Nearly 100% of our annual budget comes through donations. The High Line is owned by the City of New York, and we operate the park under a license agreement with NYC Parks.

For more information, visit thehighline.org and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, and Tiktok.

ABOUT CHANEL CULTURE FUND

CHANEL Culture Fund fosters a vibrant network of creators and innovators to advance the ideas that shape culture worldwide. Core programs include CHANELʼs Art Partners, nearly fifty international institutions whose leaders are supported in the development of ground-breaking, long-term initiatives that bring innovation to the cultural landscape. The CHANEL Next Prize celebrates artists and accelerates their future successes through access to resources and mentorship. And the podcast CHANEL Connects amplifies the voices of thought-leaders across disciplines, generations, and geographies—tackling the defining issues of our time.

From driving artistic innovation with technology at CalArts in Southern California to catalyzing creative freedom at scale at Hamburger Bahnhof in Berlin, from championing game-changing artists at the Venice Biennale to celebrating the brightest directors at the British Film Institute and opening Chinaʼs first public contemporary art library at the Power Station of Art in Shanghai, CHANEL Culture Fund extends a century of commitment to the arts and champions creative audacity for a better future.

SUPPORT

Lead support for High Line Art comes from Amanda and Don Mullen. Major support is provided by The Brown Foundation, Inc. of Houston, Charina Endowment Fund, and Shelley Fox Aarons and Philip E. Aarons.

Major support of High Line Artʼs digital infrastructure is provided by Bloomberg Philanthropies.

Program support for High Line Art is provided by Sarah Arison, Suzanne Deal Booth, Charlotte Ford, Molly Gochman, and Joyce F. Menschel.

Additional support is provided by Agnes Gund and Shane Akeroyd.

High Line Art is supported, in part, with public funds from the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of Governor Kathy Hochul and the New York State Legislature, and the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the New York City Council, under the leadership of Speaker Julie Menin.

Major support for High Line Originals is provided by CHANEL Culture Fund.

releases.body:
Program, Led by Multi-GRAMMY®-Nominated Artistic Director Chris Walden, Spotlights the Late Producer/Composer's Masterful Early Work

 Sunday, October 18, 2026, 3:00 PM, at Camarillo's Rancho Campana Performing Arts Center

VENTURA, Calif., Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Ventura Music Festival presents Pacific Jazz Orchestra: A Tribute to Quincy Jones, an exploration of Jones' masterful early work from the 1950s and 60s, featuring guest vocalists Nayanna Holley and Adam "Aejaye" Jackson, Sunday, October 18, 2026, 3:00 PM, at the Rancho Campana Performing Arts Center in Camarillo.

Pacific Jazz Orchestra Artistic Director Chris Walden, a seven-time GRAMMY®-nominee and lead arranger for the Oscars, leads the group's driving 19-piece Big Band Ensemble through his original arrangements of Jones' genre-spanning work onstage and onscreen, transporting the audience to the icon's musical roots.

Highlighting Jones' prolific output, the program features selections from his big band recordings, among them The Quintessence (1962), which exemplify his innovative approach to jazz orchestration. Also featured are some of Jones' masterful arrangements for legendary singers such as Frank Sinatra and Sarah Vaughan, including his collaboration on Vaughan and Violins (1959), in which Jones' orchestration beautifully complements her vocal prowess.

From Jones' contributions to film and television scoring, the Pacific Jazz Orchestra Big Band Ensemble performs themes from The Pawnbroker (1964) and In the Heat of the Night (1967), which illustrate his tremendous versatility and uncanny ability to convey complex emotions through music as well as his significant impact on the soundscape of American cinema.

Jones was a household name for decades, but long before Michael Jackson and "We Are the World," the musician/arranger/producer worked his way up, first from humble beginnings as a jazz trumpeter and then scoring films when he moved to Los Angeles. His lifelong impact is considerable, including a long list of those whom he mentored, among them Walden himself.

Holley, a vocalist and vocal contractor, has been a member of the house band for NBC's The Voice for more than ten seasons and performed for several seasons in the house band of American Idol. Her film credits include The Color Purple, The Eternals, Encanto, Coming 2 America, and Mulan. As a background singer, Holley has toured with P!nk, Kelly Clarkson, St. Vincent, Robbie Williams, Selena Gomez, and Sheryl Crow, among others. As a vocal contractor, Holley assembles and hires singers for film and TV programs such as the Academy Awards, The Voice, American Idol, The Talk, and The Late Late Show with James Corden.

Jackson is a seasoned vocalist and songwriter who brings a soulful blend of R&B, soul, and jazz to the stage. The Detroit-born vocalist, actor, and dancer began singing in church at age three. He has toured and recorded with Toni Braxton, John Tess, Billy Griffin, David Foster, Charo, Vesta Williams, Linda Hopkins, Harvey Mason. Josh Groban, Stevie Wonder, Melissa Manchester, Kenneth "BabyFace" Edmunds, Macklemore, Carole Bayer Sager, Patti Austin Marilyn McCoo and Billy Davis Jr, to name a few. His other passion is mentoring at-risk youth through such organizations as The Coalition for At Risk and Restoring Youth and In A World With Books. 

Pacific Jazz Orchestra has garnered critical acclaim for thrilling performances that "entertain, inspire, and enrich" (Variety). Major funders for Pacific Jazz Orchestra include GRoW @ Annenberg Foundation; the Alesia Alpert Family Foundation; the Natalie Cole Foundation; the Ella Fitzgerald Foundation; and Anonymous.

Rancho Campana Performing Arts Center is located at 4235 Mar Vista Drive, Camarillo, CA, 93010. For tickets ($15-$109) and information, visit https://www.venturamusicfestival.org or call (805) 648-3146.

For information about Pacific Jazz Orchestra, visit www.pacificjazz.org.

About Pacific Jazz Orchestra

PACIFIC JAZZ ORCHESTRA embraces and reflects the diverse and enthralling soundscape of Los Angeles, where the 40-piece ensemble was born, bred, and resides. The ultimate cross-over sensation, the nimble hybrid jazz big band and string orchestra comprised of powerhouse LA studio musicians deftly navigates musical styles ranging from jazz, Latin, soul, and R&B, to pop, musical theater, symphonic, and cinematic soundtracks.

Founded in 2022 by seven-time GRAMMY®-nominated composer/arranger/conductor Chris Walden, Pacific Jazz Orchestra has garnered critical acclaim for thrilling performances that "entertain, inspire, and enrich" (Variety). As artistic director and conductor, Walden creates a melting pot of original music and unique arrangements for every show, each with a specific theme, distinctive jazz flair, and lush orchestrations.

The ensemble is also noted for its ambitious collaborations with a wide range of guest artists, among them acclaimed singer/songwriter Rufus Wainwright, singer/actress Katharine McPhee, GRAMMY®-winning vocal group TAKE 6, and Tony Award-winner Aaron Tveit. Other projects have featured eminent violinist Caroline Campbell, celebrated saxophonist Ben Wendel, GRAMMY®-winning artist Ledisi, R&B/soul singer Adam "AeJaye" Jackson, vocal stylist Sheléa, and veteran blues and funk singer Billy Valentine.

Pacific Jazz Orchestra presents an annual concert series at various Southern California venues and has toured to Japan with its 18-piece big band configuration. It is LA's first resident jazz orchestra since 2006, when the Henry Mancini Institute closed its doors after an acclaimed ten-year run. A 501-(c)(3) non-profit organization, Pacific Jazz Orchestra is sponsored in part by the Herb Alpert Foundation. Its Advisory Board Members include David Foster, Quincy Jones (in memoriam), Monica Mancini, Alan Bergman (in memoriam), Rickey Minor, Harvey Mason Jr., and Ledisi.

About Chris Walden

Seven-time GRAMMY®-nominated composer/arranger CHRIS WALDEN is the artistic director and conductor of Pacific Jazz Orchestra. Hailed as a "distinguished conductor" (Audio Media International) and "gifted and well-connected arranger-composer" (Santa Barbara Independent) who pens "exquisite string arrangements" (The Arts Desk), Walden "has built an illustrious career working behind the scenes with some of music's biggest names" (grammy.com).

He has scored more than 40 feature and TV films and written more than 1,500 orchestral and big band arrangements for such artists as John Legend, Michael Bublé, Aretha Franklin, Paul McCartney, SEAL, Stevie Wonder, Rihanna, Barbra Streisand, and Josh Groban. He has also collaborated as an arranger and bandleader with jazz artists Diana Krall, Herb Alpert, Michael Brecker, Arturo Sandoval, and the Count Basie Orchestra and served as the lead arranger for the Academy Awards, Kennedy Center Honors, American Idol, and even the Super Bowl, arranging Jennifer Hudson's National Anthem performance. In addition to working closely with producers David Foster, Tommy LiPuma, and Phil Ramone, Walden's credits include conducting the Los Angeles Philharmonic, Hollywood Bowl Orchestra, Holland's Metropole Orkest, Boston Pops, Philadelphia Orchestra, Pittsburgh Symphony, and WDR Big Band Cologne, among others.

The German-born musician, who performs on trumpet and flugelhorn as well, composed music for German films and TV before emigrating to Los Angeles at the age of 29. Walden, who lives in Los Angeles, has served as trustee on the national board of the Recording Academy and past president of the American Society of Music Arrangers and Composers (ASMAC).

About Ventura Music Festival

The Pacific Jazz Orchestra concert is one of five events in the Ventura Music Festival's 2026 Fall Series, running October 11 through 18. The series opens October 11 with Tea and Trumpets, VMF's beloved signature afternoon tea and brass quintet experience, returning by popular demand. On Thursday, October 15, Artistic Director Nuvi Mehta leads Birth of Impressionism, a Classical Edge Concert blending live performance, history, and discovery at Ventura College Performing Arts Center. Friday, October 16 brings TAKE3 -- Where Rock Meets Bach -- to Ventura Music Hall, with a conservatory-trained, rock-star-electrifying violin, cello, and piano trio. On Saturday, October 17, the two most decorated fiddle players in IBMA history -- Michael Cleveland and Jason Carter -- perform at Mission Park in Ventura. The season closes December 15 with the celebrated twelve-voice ensemble Chanticleer in a special holiday concert at Ventura Center for Spiritual Living. Tickets for all VMF-presented Fall Series events are available at venturamusicfestival.org or by calling (805) 648-3146.

releases.body:
A new interpretation of Homer's "The Odyssey" that will intrigue audiences who enjoyed Nolan's "The Odyssey", and fascinate tech curious audiences that want to see the highest level ever achieved of an AI generated film

The film is in its entirety a one-person creation by writer/director Ash Koosha

The film's soundtrack is available as of today on Spotify

NEW YORK and LONDON, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fountain 0, the leading AI movie studio, announced that today it is releasing Odysseus: The Fall, a version of Homer's Odyssey that approaches the multidimensional story in all its depth and epic glory. Odysseus runs 150 minutes and a brand new trailer can now be found on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c75yg7_zLRE

Fountian 0 is the studio that created the first full length, live action film accepted by a major film festival with the world premiere of Dreams of Violets at the Tribeca Film Festival last month. The movie was very well received for both the quality of the production, and the fact that the subject matter could never have been captured in a film or made so close in time to the real events it dramatized, without having been generated by AI.

Ash Koosha, the writer/director/producer of Odysseus: The Fall was the sole creator of this film, as he was of Dreams of Violets. Ash is also co-founder of Fountain 0. This film also involved only part-time work by Ash over the course of four months. While every scene and image in the film is AI generated, all the writing and creative development of the film was the work of Ash just as in the Dreams of Violets film.

Ash Koosha stated, "The Odyssey is one of the most famous pieces of literature but a very challenging one to bring to the big screen. Scholars have offered many different perspectives of Odysseus' journey, and the one my film offers is intended to both stay true to the original text while offering my own sense of Odysseus the man where the book itself leaves a number of aspects ambiguous and open to personal interpretation."

Ash continued, "The Fountain 0 studio engine software, which for purposes of this movie, operated on top of the Kling video model, was improved dramatically from Dreams of Violets. It enabled the film to develop an extraordinary level of image creation of the many supernatural elements of Odysseus' journey. I feel extremely confident that with our software tool at their disposal, writer/director teams will be able to produce spectacularly good films - in very short periods of time at extremely low cost - equivalent to the highest levels of human production as Fountain 0 ramps up its production offerings."

Ash further elaborated: "It has always been my goal to create a system that could give a couple of people working together the ability to achieve the highest level of film production at incredibly low cost. Odysseus is undeniable proof that that aspiration has been achieved. Now my dream is to give all other storytellers the chance to do the same."

Pooya Koosha, producer and post-producer of the film, and co-founder of Fountain 0, stated: "The Fountain 0 software that is the "secret sauce" responsible for the extremely high quality of Odysseus is now at a stage that it can be used by writer/director teams without any need for significant training. Our multi-layered cinematic intelligence system is powered by deep understanding of how to translate artistic elements into technical logic. The three elements that guide the film creator through of pre-production, image generation, and post-production enable total collaboration with the Fountain 0 engine such that creative teams can develop their films with complete autonomy. Of course, a top-notch video model is essential to the process, and we are extremely grateful to the AI model Kling for its valuable contributions and its underwriting of the token cost of the film."

Tom Rogers, Executive Chairman of Fountain 0, and executive producer of the film, stated: "Nolan's The Odyssey, created quite a cultural zeitgeist moment this summer given the very enthusiastic embrace that it got from audiences. We wanted to take the fascination with Homer's story into the fall season with Odysseus: The Fall. The comparisons between the height of human film production and what so far is the height of AI generated film will be unavoidable. One key thing that should be kept in mind though is how AI generated film can democratize the movie industry and enable a spouting fountain of new movies to be created, and that 10,000 films of the quality of Odysseus: The Fall can now be created at the same cost of Nolan's film. One of the huge breakthroughs of the Fountain 0 software is its ability to minimize token expense and thus reduce the cost of high-quality, full-length film production - with all the enhancements, additions, reimagining, and editing that involves - to levels no AI company has come close to achieving.

One of the key aspects of this film is that the image and likeness of thirteen real people were incorporated as actors in Odysseus. Ash Koosha's image is used for the Odysseus character, Pooya Koosha for Eurylochus, and Tom Rogers for Mentor. Fountain 0 recently announced that Sunny Hostin, the co-anchor of The View (and six-time Emmy award winning journalist, attorney, and best-selling author), has entered into an agreement to license her image for appearances in upcoming films she would look to produce based on her books.

As part of Fountain 0's strategic development, the company will be focusing its efforts on attracting other well-known personalities and influencers who would like to enter into image licensing agreements and participate in the revenue upside of upcoming Fountain 0 films. Fountain 0 has created an online portal to review and vet potential partners based on their interest in entering into licensing agreements.

Fountain 0 believes not only AI reduces the cost of production, but the cost of marketing films can be greatly reduced by social media marketing to the followers of major influencers.

Pooya Koosha explained: "Fountain 0 tested a range of AI video models and ultimately chose Kling AI for its stronger control and consistency, which allowed Ash to direct the film in a way that felt closer to working on a traditional production set. The Kling 3.0 model series introduced industry-first native 4K output, preserving fine visual details and enabling the highest quality cinematic shots. The Kling 3.0 series have strong capabilities that are especially important when working with faces, skin texture, and other production-sensitive elements."

As of today, Odysseus: The Fall is now streaming at watch.fountain0.com, along with Dreams of Violets. The film is available for rent at a price of $9.99. Also released today is the soundtrack of the movie which will be available on Spotify. Ash Koosha has a deep history in the development of AI music. The lead song in the film is an interpretation of Seikilos Epitaph, an Ancient Greek song regarded as the oldest written musical composition for which both lyrics and melody survive.

releases.title: Musicologie Hits 100 Franchise Licenses Sold
releases.body:
The family-owned music education franchise built on inclusion and play keeps expanding its national footprint, with licenses now sold across 19 states.

COLUMBUS, Ohio, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Musicologie, the music education franchise founded by husband-and-wife team Kay and Joseph Barker, just crossed the 100-license mark, a milestone reached just over two years after selling its first franchise, positioning it among the few national brands in a category still dominated by independent, single-location music schools.

Kay and Joseph founded Musicologie in 2014 after years spent touring in their folk/pop band, Bella Ruse. Teaching lessons between tour dates to supplement their income, the pair discovered their real passion was in the classroom. "The goal has always been to make music, but when we started teaching lessons to supplement our band income, it became obvious teaching was our passion," Kay told Columbus Alive in an earlier interview.

That philosophy runs through every studio via The Musicologie Method®, built on a safe environment and education through play. It reflects the brand's mission to create inclusive communities of music explorers and empower teachers to build sustainable careers; one now reaching major markets nationwide through hundreds of teachers and hundreds of thousands of lessons a year.

"Every one of our 100 licenses represents a franchise owner who chose Musicologie after evaluating the brand and the space. That kind of conviction validates everything we've built: the method, the model, the community," said Joseph Barker.

Musicologie's franchise model centers on a membership-based program that helps build long-term customer relationships, backed by hands-on franchisee support.

"Reaching 100 licenses is a full-circle moment for us. We started this in a one-car garage because we believed every neighborhood deserved a place like Musicologie, and now we get to build that with a hundred other people who believe it too. We're just getting started!" said Kay Barker.

The private music lessons industry is estimated at $800 million in the U.S., and more than half of American parents enroll their kids in music lessons, per Pew Research Center.

About Musicologie

Founded in 2014 by Kay and Joseph Barker in Grandview Heights, Ohio, Musicologie is a music education franchise built on a membership-based lesson model. The brand has taught more than 10,000 students and now has 100+ locations in development. Learn more at musicologielessons.com/franchising.

About REP'M Group

REP'M Group is the franchise development firm behind Musicologie's growth strategy, supporting the brand's franchise sales, marketing and expansion efforts nationwide.

releases.title: COACH INTRODUCES "LIVE YOUR STORY" A NEW CAMPAIGN TURNING SELF-EXPRESSION INTO REAL-WORLD CONNECTION THROUGH STYLE AND MUSIC
releases.body:
Brought to Life Through a First-of-Its-Kind Global Cultural Partnership with Spotify

Starring Actress Elle Fanning Across Four Films, Each Co-Starring and Soundtracked by Musicians PinkPantheress, SOYEON, Lilas, and Shan Yichun

NEW YORK, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, Coach introduces "Live Your Story," the brand's Fall 2026 campaign celebrating how style and music enable self-expression and real-world connection. Building on Coach's ongoing exploration of identity and personal narratives, the campaign moves from self-expression as an individual pursuit to connection as a collective experience, turning to music as a powerful expression of both individuality and community. "Live Your Story" introduces a new global cultural partnership with Spotify into the campaign as a core pillar and features five Coach global ambassadors, including four musicians with deep cultural resonance and combined global reach. The campaign spotlights Coach's iconic Tabby bag, including five special-edition Tabbys inspired by the starring talent, and a new collection of concert ticket bag charms designed to invite personalization and spark conversation.

THE CONCEPT

"Live Your Story" was inspired by in-depth conversations with Gen Z consumers, who shared a desire to spend less time on screens and more time connecting in the real world—and a belief that music, particularly live music, can be a powerful conduit for self-expression and community. At the heart of the campaign is the idea that real connection requires courage: the vulnerability to show up as yourself, let yourself be seen, and participate fully in moments unfolding in real time. In this way, "Live Your Story" brings Coach's purpose, the Courage to Be Real, to life across campaign films, custom product, personalized playlists and in-person experiences around the globe.

"At Coach, we start with the people, not the category—listening closely to what matters to them and how they are navigating the world. In our conversations with Gen Z, we heard a powerful tension: they long to spend less time behind screens and connect more deeply in real life, but stepping out of digital comfort and into the vulnerability of being fully present takes courage," said Joon Silverstein, Coach Chief Marketing Officer.

"Music is uniquely powerful in creating space for real connection. It is deeply personal—a soundtrack to identity and emotion—but it also creates a shared language that helps people find one another and feel they belong. 'Live Your Story' brings our purpose, the Courage to Be Real, to life by showing what can happen when people take that step together—when individual expression becomes shared experience."

THE CAMPAIGN

The four films anchoring the campaign each feature a different trailblazing musician with deep cultural resonance and a distinct sound. Beyond starring in the films, each artist contributes one of their own songs to the soundtrack—including a newly-released solo single from SOYEON—allowing their music and personal style to shape the story onscreen. The musicians include PinkPantheress, a new Coach global ambassador and British singer-songwriter and producer whose innovative sound and genre-defying production have made her one of music's most exciting young artists. She is joined by returning global ambassadors: Korean singer-songwriter and producer SOYEON, Japanese singer-songwriter Lilas, and breakthrough Chinese singer Shan Yichun.

As a narrative through-line, Oscar-nominated American actress Elle Fanning appears in every film, driving the story figuratively and literally. In a first for Coach, 12 Gen Z music-lovers from around the world also appear in the film and stills—each has a personal story about the ways live music has changed their lives and their sense of self.

Directed by Emmy-nominated director Vincent Haycock, the four campaign films underscore the power of music and style to enable self-expression and connection in the moment. Elle Fanning appears as the driver of a bus on its way to a music festival. As the other cast members board and the featured musician's song begins to draw them together, the passengers transform from isolated individuals, each absorbed in their own world, into a community united through style and music.

Coach's iconic Tabby bag also plays a starring role in "Live Your Story," acting as a conversation starter that helps foster connection in the films and appearing across campaign content in key silhouettes. A special assortment of five Tabbys inspired by Elle Fanning, PinkPantheress, SOYEON, Lilas, and Shan Yichun reflects each talent's personal style. The bags are complemented by a new selection of concert ticket bag charms, designed to evoke keepsakes from live shows and invite customers to become part of the moment: collecting them, using them to personalize their bags, or sharing a set with a friend.

THE PARTNERS

"Live Your Story" reflects how Gen Z already moves through the world, using music and style to figure out who they are and connect with others. Coach champions the courage to explore and express who you are, while Spotify, one of the least regretted places young people spend time online, helps people discover music, artists and creators in ways they genuinely value. They're bringing those worlds together through live experiences and on Spotify, including a bespoke "Live Your Story" hub on Spotify where fans can discover how courage shows up in their relationship with music, discover and share their personalized listening persona, and explore playlists shaped by their music tastes.

"This fall, Coach and Spotify come together in a first-of-its-kind global cultural partnership built around a clear insight: Gen Z doesn't separate identity into categories," said Silverstein. "What they wear, what they listen to, and the communities they belong to are all part of the same personal story. Coach champions the courage to explore and express who you are, while Spotify shapes how people discover and engage with music, artists, and creators. Together, we're creating shared experiences at the intersection of music and style that bring people together and come alive through participation—as people shape them and make them their own."

As a global campaign rooted in cultural relevance, "Live Your Story" comes to life through partnerships tailored to the platforms and communities shaping culture in each market. In China, Coach is partnering with QQ Music, the country's leading music streaming platform, to create a market-specific expression of the campaign through curated playlist integrations and original programming. Local storytelling will also extend the brand's existing work with video-sharing platform Bilibili through a series of video podcast episodes featuring leading Gen Z creators discussing the power of music and style to foster self-expression and connection.

"Spotify is where fans are engaged, not just passing through. Our partnership with Coach taps into that positive attention by giving fans real ways to connect across music, fashion, and culture, from the Tabby Tour to the campaign hub on Spotify. These are the kind of integrated experiences that create meaningful impact for fans and brands alike," said Brian Berner, Spotify's VP of Advertising Partnerships.

THE EXPERIENCE

The shared expression of Coach's partnership with Spotify takes shape through the award-winning Tabby Tour—a global, traveling experience that transforms the campaign's bus journey into a real-world platform for live music, creative participation, and community. Across stops in the United States, United Kingdom, Japan, and South Korea with Spotify, and China with QQ Music, consumers will experience live performances and conversations with rising artists, customize Coach products, and participate in experiences shaped by each local community. In China, activations begin in Chengdu on November 6 at the Coach x QQ Music Live Your Story Music Festival and continue with tour stops in Shenzhen and Nanjing.

A tour bus inspired by the one Elle Fanning drives in the campaign films connects the story onscreen to real life, while playlists and content extend the energy of each stop beyond the moment. Together, the digital and physical experiences create a journey from personal discovery to shared experience.

As part of campaign launch, the Tabby Tour will kick off today in New York City. For updates and more information on the campaign, visit https://www.coach.com/content/courage-to-be-real and https://open.spotify.com/presents/coach-hub-62f46

releases.title: Vision Films Announces North American Digital Release of 'Line Of Control'
releases.body:
The full-length feature is adapted from the acclaimed novel The Collaborator by Mirza Waheed

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Vision Films Inc. will release the critically acclaimed feature film Line Of Control on Transactional VOD throughout the United States and Canada on October 6, 2026, through a deal with Scott J. Jones and Artist View Entertainment.

Line Of Control is based on The Collaborator, the acclaimed debut novel by Mirza Waheed, set in Kashmir in 1993 during the insurgency. Told through the experiences of a Kashmiri Muslim teenager caught between militants and the Indian Army, the film offers a deeply personal perspective on the political unrest, violence and atrocities surrounding the Line of Control - the boundary separating Indian-administered Kashmir from Pakistan-administered Kashmir. Watch the official trailer HERE.

Written and directed by Travis Hodgkins, Line Of Control is produced by Rashaana Shah and Cristy Coors Beasley and executive produced by Chaitra Vedullapalli, Joseph Lanius, Namrata Sharma, and Swetha Pakala. Although rooted in a specific and emotionally charged period of history, the film reflects conflicts that continue to unfold around the world over religion, land, identity, and loyalty.

Synopsis: During the Kashmir insurgency in 1993, a teenage boy's best friend disappears amid the escalating violence. Determined to find him, the boy is coerced into working for an Indian Army captain, entering fields of fallen fighters to recover identification cards and weapons. Pushed to the edge and confronted with impossible choices that test his morality, loyalty, and sense of self, he discovers the true meaning of friendship, loss, and survival.

The international cast includes Rudi Dharmalingam (The Lazarus Project, Our Girl, The Split, Wakefield), Nitin Ganatra (EastEnders, Sweetpea), Vikram Kapadia (The Night Manager—Indian adaptation, Made In Heavan), Nikhil Singh Rai (Call the Midwife) and Georgian Indian model and emerging actress Anastasia Jairath.

The production consulted representatives of the Indian Army to help ensure military accuracy. Principal photography took place in the Caucasus Mountains of Georgia, where the filmmakers received military support and protection from the Georgian Army because of ongoing tensions in the region.

Lise Romanoff, CEO and Managing Director of Vision Films shares, "Line of Control is an emotional and impactful story of a tragic conflict that is unfortunately, all too familiar throughout history and around the world. It is important that these stories are shared as reminders of survival and rebirth."

"Mirza Waheed's novel refuses to reduce Kashmir to a headline," said writer-director Travis Hodgkins. "What moved me was the deeply human story of a young man struggling to preserve his conscience when every possible choice carries a cost. I hope the film allows audiences to feel the weight of that experience."

"Bringing Line Of Control to the screen demanded extraordinary commitment from everyone involved," said producer Rashaana Shah. "We are proud that audiences across North America will now have the opportunity to discover this story and the remarkable work of our cast and crew."

The film enjoyed rave reviews from outlets including Kashmir Times, Outlook India, Take 2 Indie Review and more. Its celebrated international festival run began with a world premiere at the San Diego International Film Festival followed by its Asian premiere at the Kala Ghoda Arts Festival in Mumbai and screened at the UK Asian Film Festival in London, the Joburg Film Festival in South Africa, the Karama Human Rights Film Festival in Jordan, and the Antakya Film Festival in Turkey.

Line Of Control will be available to rent or purchase beginning October 6, 2026, on major digital platforms, including iTunes/Apple TV, AmazonInstant, Google Play and Fandango at Home, as well as participating cable platforms throughout the United States and Canada.

For more information, please visit and follow @lineofcontrolmovie on Instagram.

The original score for Line Of Control, composed by two-time Emmy® Award nominee Wayne Sharpe, is available to stream or purchase on all major digital music platforms, including Spotify, Apple Music/iTunes, Amazon Music, and YouTube Music.

About Vision Films

Vision Films is a leading independent sales and VOD aggregator specializing in the licensing, marketing, and distribution of over 800 feature films, documentaries, and series from some of the most prolific independent film producers in the world. Led by Lise Romanoff, Managing Director/CEO Worldwide Distribution, Vision Films releases 2-4 films a month across Theatrical, VOD, DVD, and television platforms. visionfilms.net

About Mirza Waheed

Mirza Waheed was born and raised in Kashmir and currently lives in London. His debut novel, The Collaborator, was shortlisted for the Guardian First Book Award and the Shakti Bhatt Prize, considered for the Desmond Elliott Prize and named a Book of the Year by The Telegraph, New Statesman, Financial Times, and other publications. releases.title: The Country They Call Life Lands at Catalina Film Festival After Four-Award Sweep at Film Invasion Los Angeles
releases.body:
Writer-director Grace Sims' debut short - starring Sydney Cole Alexander (Severance, Mission: Impossible – The Final Reckoning) and featuring Bates Wilder, Jerah Milligan, Taylor Rose, and the late Dee Freeman - also screens at the LA Women in Film Festival

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fresh off a four-award sweep at Film Invasion Los Angeles, the debut short film from writer-director, Grace Sims, The Country They Call Life, has been named an Official Selection of the Catalina Film Festival - ranked among the world's top festivals by FilmFreeway and named one of MovieMaker Magazine's "50 Film Festivals Worth the Entry Fee." The Catalina bow arrives alongside an upcoming screening at the LA Women in Film Festival, with additional festival announcements expected in the months ahead.

At Film Invasion Los Angeles, The Country They Call Life took the festival's highest honor: Best in Fest: Best Live Action Short Film - and swept three Grand Jury Awards

  • Best Director - Grace Sims
  • Best Produced Screenplay - Grace Sims
  • Best Lead Performer - Sydney Cole Alexander

The film stars Sydney Cole Alexander (Severance, Mission: Impossible – The Final Reckoning) as Maxine, leading an ensemble that includes Bates Wilder (American Fiction), Jerah Milligan (Astronomy Club, Black Mirror), Taylor Rose (The Good Wife), and the late Dee Freeman (Shameless).

A poetic exploration of agency and reconciliation, The Country They Call Life draws directly from writer-director Grace Sims' own path. Childhood epilepsy often kept Sims on the sidelines, sharpening her into a quiet observer from an early age - a perspective later widened by a life lived in motion, from Hawaii to South Africa, and by chapters spent as a young missionary, a film student, and an agency creative leading visual research for major studio releases at BOND. Those experiences shape her character-driven voice as a storyteller.

"I wanted to tell a story that left room for all of the complicated, sometimes contradictory feelings that can exist inside one experience," said Sims. "Watching audiences connect with Maxine without needing the film to tell them what to think has been incredibly rewarding. And because so many women were instrumental in bringing this story to life, it feels particularly special to continue sharing it at Catalina and the LA Women in Film Festival."

The road to the screen was brutal. January 2025 Los Angeles wildfires halted production mid-shoot, forcing Sims to regroup her team, raise additional funds, and finish post-production - all while preparing for motherhood. She gave birth to her son on June 1, 2026, just three weeks before the world premiere.

Sims is currently in active development on the feature adaptation, which expands on the short's themes of generational cycles, personal belief systems, and the courage to forge your own path.

Screener access, high-resolution stills, and press materials available upon request.

ABOUT WRITER-DIRECTOR GRACE SIMS

Grace Sims is a New York–raised, Los Angeles–based writer and director who crafts intimate, character-driven stories on the human experience. Diagnosed with childhood epilepsy, she developed an outsider's perspective that deepened as she lived globally - from Hawaii to South Africa - and worked as a missionary, film student, and visual researcher at BOND.

Sims is currently developing the feature adaptation, centering on generational cycles, resilience, and identity.

WEST PALM BEACH, Fla., Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Award-winning singer-songwriter Natasha Owens' tribute single "We Miss You, Charlie," featuring Benjy Gaither, is projected to appear on Billboard's charts for a second consecutive week, capping a remarkable run for an independent release that climbed to #3 on the iTunes Pop Songs Chart and #13 on the iTunes All Genres Songs Chart, with the official music video surpassing 250,000 views.

Released September 4, 2026, through Real America's Music — a sister company of Real America's Voice — the single arrived just days before the one-year anniversary of Charlie Kirk's passing on September 10. Rather than dwell solely on loss, the song looks ahead to those Charlie inspired and to the generation now challenged to carry his legacy forward.

"This isn't just about looking back and mourning someone we lost. It's about asking what we do with what Charlie left us," said Owens. "His voice inspired an entire generation to stand up for what they believe. Now that generation has a responsibility to carry that torch forward."

One hundred percent of net profits from the project will be donated to TPUSA and TP Action, supporting the next generation of student leaders and grassroots organizing. Vinyl editions are available now through the Real America's Voice Shop.

"We Miss You, Charlie" also reflects the continued growth of Real America's Music, which earlier this year saw Steve Gruber and the Freedom Project's "One Nation" debut at #6 on Billboard's digital song sales chart.

"As Real America's Music continues to grow, our mission is to give a platform to artists and songs that carry that same courage, conviction, and love of country forward."

HAMILTON, Bermuda, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BACARDÍ® Rum, The World's Most Awarded Rum, returns for a fourth consecutive year as the Official Spirits Partner of the 2026 MTV VIDEO MUSIC AWARDS ("VMAs"), hosted by Snoop Dogg on Sunday, September 27 in Los Angeles and airing on CBS Television Network. As part of the next chapter of its global Do What Moves You campaign, BACARDÍ is expanding its partnership with the "VMAs" by helping bring back the Best Dance category for the first time in seven years.

Returning for the first time since 2019, the Best Dance category recognizes the artists whose work inspires audiences to move, connect, and share unforgettable moments. Building on their longstanding partnership and shared passion for music and culture, BACARDÍ and the "VMAs" believe dance is the most participatory expression of music - transforming songs into shared experiences that transcend language, background, and generations. Together, the duo is shining a spotlight on the artists, creators and fans who continue to shape the future of dance music and its influence on culture.

"Music has always had the power to bring people together, and dance is one of the most universal expressions of that connection," said Lisa Pfenning, Vice President of BACARDÍ in North America. "When we learned the Best Dance category hadn't been awarded in seven years, we knew it was time to bring it back for the fans. Dance has always been at the heart of music, and today, it's driving culture in more ways than ever, from viral trends to packed dance floors. We're proud to partner with Paramount to celebrate the artists and creators leading that movement."

To celebrate the category's return, BACARDÍ has partnered with Paramount Media Labs, Paramount Advertising's full-service branded content studio, to debut "It All Starts With a Beat," an original content campaign inspired by the rhythm that transforms music into movement. Featuring acclaimed producer Caleb Calloway alongside celebrated dancers and choreographers Dexter Carr, Gabi Barra and Dario Boatner, the campaign follows the creative process behind an original Latin-inspired remix and choreography built around iconic Best Dance-winning tracks, including "Livin' La Vida Loca" by Ricky Martin and "Waiting For Tonight" by Jennifer Lopez and "Free Your Mind" by En Vogue. Created and produced by Paramount Media Labs, the exclusive custom content will air during the "VMAs."

BACARDÍ will serve the official cocktail lineup on "VMAs" night, including the beloved Moonwalk Mojito, BACARDÍ Agua Fresca, BACARDÍ Coco Colada Spritz and BACARDÍ 808, inviting guests to raise a glass to the year's biggest celebration of music.

"Dance music is experiencing a powerful resurgence, making this the perfect year to reintroduce Best Dance Video to the 'VMAs'. Together with BACARDÍ's vision and Paramount's deep music, talent and cultural expertise, we created an authentic campaign and unforgettable experience that captures the energy fueling the genre's momentum and unites the brand, show, artists and fans in a meaningful way," said Matt Newcomb, Senior Vice President of Marketing Activation, Paramount Media Labs.

The 2026 MTV VIDEO MUSIC AWARDS ("VMAs") returns to the West Coast for the first time since 2017, broadcasting live on Sunday, Sept. 27 (7:30-9:30 PM, ET/ 4:30-6:30 PM, PT) on the CBS Television Network, simulcast on MTV and streaming live on Paramount+ (Premium) in the U.S. The show will also be available globally the next day on Paramount+ and MTV.

The "VMAs" are produced by Gunpowder & Sky. Van Toffler serves as producer. Jesse Ignjatovic of Den of Thieves, Barb Bialkowski and Bruce Gillmer serve as executive producers alongside Barry Barclay and Floris Bauer. Melanie Block serves as co-executive producer and Gary Lanvy as co-producer. Snoop Dogg is executive producer alongside producers Sara Ramaker and Jasmin Ratansi. Jen Proctor is executive talent producer. 

For more information, follow @bacardi, @MTV, @VMAs and @CBS on all social channels to stay in the loop for all things #VMAs.

releases.body:
CHICAGO, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Cook County Treasurer will commemorate Mexico's Independence on Wednesday with a noontime reception honoring the cultural contributions of Mexican Americans to Cook County.

The reception will take place in the Treasurer's Office at 118 N. Clark Street, Room 112, on the first floor of the County Building. The public is invited. The event will feature Morton High School's Mariachi Band and will celebrate the vibrant culture and enduring traditions of Cook County's Mexican diaspora through music and song.

"Mexican Independence Day is an opportunity to celebrate the history, culture and achievements of Mexican Americans who've enriched Cook County through their hard work, entrepreneurship, civic engagement and commitment to family and community," said the Treasurer. "Our county is strengthened by the diversity of its residents, and we're proud to recognize the more than one million people of Mexican heritage who call Chicagoland home by celebrating their contributions to the social, cultural and economic life of Cook County."

Observed annually on September 16, Mexico's Independence Day commemorates the beginning of country's struggle to free itself from Spanish colonial rule in 1810. The event known as the Grito de Dolores or the Cry of Dolores is named for the town where that first revolutionary spark ignited 116 years ago. That first "Cry" resulted in 11 more years of struggle before the Spanish were ultimately defeated in September of 1821. The observance honors Mexico's enduring commitment to freedom, democracy and national pride while celebrating the traditions and accomplishments of Mexicans both at home and abroad.

The reception will provide an opportunity to honor local community leaders by presenting them with Certificates of Excellence. 

Honorees: Andres Cervantes, Morton High School music director; Kevin Vesper, Morton High School fine arts and social director; Nazario Perez, La Cremeria la Ordena president; Mario Contreras, Medieval Times horse director and trainer; Adriana Rodriguez, vice president Necalli Cultural Movement; Gabriela Flores, co-founder, Necalli Cultural Movement; Amelia Gradilla, co-founder, Necalli Cultural Movement; Adriana Rangel, co-founder, Necalli Cultural Movement; Jacqueline Villanueva, co-founder, Necalli Cultural Movement

releases.title: Schmear We Go Again, as New York BagelFest Rolls Out Its 2026 Judges, Industry Talks and Entertainment
releases.body:
Acclaimed judges, bagel industry icons, world-class magic and live art join an international lineup of leading bagel makers at Citi Field on November 15th

NEW YORK, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The dough is rising, and so is demand for New York BagelFest, Presented by King Arthur Baking Company. The ultimate celebration of bagel culture returns to Citi Field on Sunday, November 15, 2026, bringing together more than 25 acclaimed bagel makers, culinary personalities, industry leaders and thousands of hungry fans for a day of unlimited tastings, friendly-but-fierce competition, conversation and entertainment.

"The global bagel industry is growing at a rapidly accelerating rate. The 7th Annual New York BagelFest will be the most magical one yet - quite literally, with a magician and mentalist joining this year's entertainment lineup - for our foodies, industry professionals, and competitors," says BagelFest founder Sam Silverman.

Bagel lovers don't want to miss a bite. Early Bird tickets sold out in just three hours, and one-third of all available tickets were sold within the first 24 hours. Tickets are now on sale, as anticipation builds for one of the festival's most ambitious editions yet. This fall, New York BagelFest will welcome bagel shops representing ten states and five countries, with bakers traveling from Ireland, Spain, Canada and India to compete alongside legendary New York institutions and leading bagel makers from across the United States. Getting a spot at BagelFest is no schmear feat. Fewer than 9% of applicants were selected to compete in 2026, following a highly curated selection process evaluating bakeries on quality, originality, reputation and the passionate communities they've built.

Now, BagelFest is rolling out the next batch of news: the experts who will determine which bagels rise above the rest, an Industry Talks series bringing together influential voices in the business, and world-class entertainment spanning magic, mentalism, live fine art, and family programming.

But first, a hole lot of responsibility comes with judging. Choosing among some of the world's best bagels is a tough job, but somebody has to do it. The judging lineup brings together acclaimed voices from food journalism, restaurants, culinary culture and digital media, including Joan Nathan, the James Beard Award-winning author of twelve cookbooks known as the "matriarch of Jewish cooking." Jake Cohen the New York Times bestselling author of Jew-ish and I Could Nosh the host of "Jake Makes it Easy" on A+E and Hulu. Ethan Zohn, a former professional soccer player, author, TV host, and champion of CBS's Survivor: Africa. Chef Einat Admony, the three-time James Beard Award-nominated chef, restaurateur and cookbook author behind New York City's Balaboosta and Moondog HiFi. Darra Goldstein, the founding editor of Gastronomica and editor in chief of the Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Food Studies, who has won numerous prizes for her work in food, including James Beard and IACP awards.

Gabriella Gershenson, a James Beard Award-winning food journalist, author and editor at the New York Times Wirecutter. Joining her is Leah Koenig, the IACP Award-winning author of eight cookbooks, including new title The Dessert Table: 100 Joyful Jewish Sweets. Jeremy Jacobowitz brings the perspective of a food and travel creator whose audience of more than 950,000 follows his culinary adventures around the world. Before building his digital presence, Jacobowitz worked in food television as an assistant to Bobby Flay and as a producer.

Jewish Food thought leaders such as Liz Alpern and Jeffrey Yoskowitz, co-founders of The Gefilteria, co-authors of The Gefilte Manifesto, and co-hosts of the Meet Me at the Deli podcast, and Shannon Sarna, the Founding Editor of The Nosher and author of Modern Jewish Baker and Modern Jewish Comfort Food.

Judges with deep production experience include Tim Von Hollweg, Director of Operations at Russ & Daughters, native New Yorker, and hospitality veteran; and Reva Castillenti, an award-winning baker turned bakery consultant and educator.

Joining are prolific bagel eaters and reviewers, like Mike Varley, the creator of EverythingIsEverything.NYC, a catalogue of over 200 New York City bagel reviews from across all five boroughs. The project has been featured in The New York Times, NPR, The Washington Post, and The Today Show. Justin Shukat, co-founder of Bagel Tawk, with over 100 bagel reviews under his belt. Sean Keeley, the creator and writer of It's a Shanda, a newsletter dedicated to bagels in Seattle and beyond. Joanna O'Leary, culinary consultant, food historian, and scientific writer, with bagel reviews from all around the world. And Morgan Carter, the Food and Drink Editor at Time Out New York.

Chairing the "Best Sandwich" Judge committee is Ben Gollan, founder of A Man and His Sandwich Tours, New York's sandwich-dedicated walking tour. Gollan has made a career out of debating what does, and doesn't, count as a sandwich, including in Forbes and on national television.

Rounding out the Expert Judge lineup are returning judges who demonstrate a deep passion and expertise: Dara Pollack, writer, food photographer, comedian, and bagel enthusiast; Tara Cox, Editor & Writer; Chrissy Traore, CEO of See and Be Kitchen, and Ryan Garson, NYC real estate agent and content creator with a focus on bagels.

"The BagelFest judges hold a critical responsibility. Winning a top BagelFest award has elevated neighborhood shops into the national culinary spotlight. PopUp Bagels went on to a $300 million valuation, and Starship Bagel became a James Beard Award finalist for Outstanding Bakery. It's permanently altered the trajectories of countless businesses, and the lives of the employees and families behind them," says Sam Silverman.

The coveted Best Bagel title will be determined through a blind taste test by the judges. Each unsliced plain bagel will receive a score from 1–10 across flavor, texture, appearance and aroma. The highest average score takes the crown, with flavor serving as the tiebreaker. The same judging criteria will determine honors for Best Bagel – New York Style, Best Bagel – Sourdough and Best Bagel – Montreal Style.

Expert judges will also select Schmear of the Year, based on flavor, texture and consistency, and originality; Most Creative, evaluating original concept, execution, presentation and story; Best Showmanship, honoring booth presentation, team energy and brand representation; and Best Bialy, judged on flavor, texture, appearance and creativity while honoring tradition. But the experts don't get all the fun. Festivalgoers will have their say through public voting for People's Choice, Best of the Boroughs, Best Beyond the Boroughs, Best International and Rising Star. For competitors who prefer speed to schmear, the Bagel Rolling Championship returns to the main stage, challenging participants to see who can roll the most bagels in just one minute.

BagelFest isn't just about who makes the best bagel; it's also about the people, ideas and businesses shaping where bagel culture rolls next. The festival's Industry Talks will bring bakers, operators and industry leaders together throughout the day for conversations about craft, growth, tradition and the future of the business.

"No matter your level of experience or knowledge, the industry panels at BagelFest offer a valuable opportunity to learn from professionals across the business. Panelists bring expertise in areas ranging from bagel making and business operations to brand marketing and beyond. There is no better place to connect with and learn from the industry's leading experts, all in one location," says Jeff Yankellow, Director of Bakery and Food Services Sales at King Arthur Baking Company.

The program kicks off at 10:15 a.m. with "The Key to the Perfect Bagel," featuring Jeff Yankellow (King Arthur Baking Company), Joe Savelli (Malt Products Corporation) and Chris Sarkesian (All Bake Technologies) moderated by journalist Annie Hollon. At 11:30 a.m., "From Toasted to Thriving" will feature Chris Pugliese (Tompkins Square Bagels), and Emily Winston (Boichik Bagels), moderated by Karen Bornarth (Bread Bakers Guild of America). At 1:15 p.m., "Icons of Jewish New York" brings together Jake Dell (Katz's Delicatessen), Josh Russ Tupper (Russ & Daughters), and David Zabar (Zabar's) for a conversation featuring names closely connected to New York food culture, moderated by Sean Keeley (It's a Shanda). The Industry Talks continue at 2:30 p.m. with a conversation between Christian Petroni and Scott Spellman of Utopia Bagels. Together, the conversations give guests a chance to go behind the counter and hear directly from the people helping turn a centuries-old food tradition into a thriving, evolving industry.

The bagels may be the stars, but they won't be the only thing making jaws drop. Leading this year's entertainment lineup is New York-based magician and mentalist Daniel Nicholas, who has performed at more than 1,000 events over 15 years, nationwide and around the globe. His performances blend sleight of hand with sleight of mind: magic that happens in guests' own hands and mind reading that unfolds inside their heads. At New York BagelFest, Nicholas will bring both up close and to the stage, moving from encounters just inches away to moments designed to hold an entire audience. His magic happens to guests rather than simply in front of them: a signed card can disappear and turn up somewhere impossible; a borrowed object takes an unexpected journey; an unspoken thought is revealed. No boxes. No doves. No assistants. Just plenty of "How did he do that?" to chew on between bagels.

BagelFest is also turning the art of the bagel into actual art. New York City-based fine artist Melissa Mae Kors will set up her easel directly inside the festival and construct a fully realized, gallery-ready masterpiece from scratch…transforming the iconic culinary staple into a centerpiece of high-detail, whimsical art. The immersive performance bridges the gap between culinary celebration and fine art, leaving attendees with an unforgettable window into the creation of contemporary surrealism. After all, when more than two dozen of the world's leading bagel makers are treating dough as their canvas, it only seems fitting to have an artist return the favor.

The entertainment doesn't stop with magic and live art. Families can also explore a dedicated Kids' Zone, featuring chef hat and apron decorating and interactive entertainment designed for the next generation of carb connoisseurs. The Kids' Zone will also welcome Allyson Fisher, author of Bagel Finds His Center, for readings and book signing, with copies available for purchase at the festival. The charming picture book follows Bagel, a nervous newcomer searching for what makes him special, using playful rhymes and food-themed humor to explore self-worth, individuality, friendship and belonging.

The day culminates with the BagelFest Awards Ceremony, where the day's winners will be crowned and the competitors who rise to the occasion will take home BagelFest bragging rights. BagelFest will also present its Lifetime Achievement Award, recognizing lasting impact on bagel culture. L.A. Film School alumni were credited across 41 nominated productions, with 44 individual alumni credits spanning 218 Emmy nominations. Other Emmy-winning productions featuring L.A. Film School alumni included The Muppet Show, where Raul Perez worked as a loader; Margo's Got Money Troubles, where Márk Faragó worked as a finishing artist; and Fallout, where Brice Bradley worked as a gaffer on the show's volume stage.

On Hacks, alumni Jamiel VanOver and Yermin "Randy" Garcia worked in the camera and electrical departments, while Stephanie Goldstein worked as an assistant editor. Ira Parker serves as showrunner and executive producer of A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms and was individually nominated for Outstanding Drama Series.

Alumni contributions also extended to a variety of other Emmy-recognized productions. Damian Drago contributed as a digital artist on Stranger Things, while Neiko Nagy worked as a compositor on The Diplomat's visual effects team.

Beyond the winning productions, L.A. Film School alumni contributed to a number of Emmy-nominated productions, including Nobody Wants This, Only Murders in the Building, Euphoria, and more.

This year's alumni credits reflect the many paths available to entertainment professionals and the range of disciplines that come together to bring stories to audiences. releases.title: Sonilo Takes AI Music to the World Stage at the Venice Film Festival
releases.body:
The Silicon Valley company showcases its music and sound-effects models in a completed cinematic soundtrack, marking a milestone in its expansion into professional filmmaking.

SILICON VALLEY, Calif., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sonilo, a U.S. company developing multimodal audio AI, brought its AI music and sound effects to the 2026 Venice International Film Festival. The company's technology contributed to the soundtrack of the PRIMORDIA trailer, which premiered during the opening program of an industry forum organized by TapNow at Venice Production Bridge. The presentation placed Sonilo's audio technology in front of an international film-industry audience through a finished cinematic work.

For Sonilo, the showcase represents a significant step into professional cinema. Its technology contributed to the musical identities, emotional progression and physical world of a production presented at Venice, demonstrating how AI-powered music and sound effects can move beyond standalone generation into the demands of cinematic storytelling.

The significance extends beyond visibility. A completed soundtrack gives filmmakers and production partners a tangible basis for evaluating the technology: how it works with the picture, supports the narrative and contributes to the experience audiences ultimately see and hear.

"Bringing Sonilo's AI-powered music to Venice is a milestone in our push into professional filmmaking," said Trista Hong, Chief Marketing Officer of Sonilo. "Cinema demands more than an impressive track or a realistic sound. It demands emotion, timing and a world the audience can believe in. We are building audio technology powerful enough to support ambitious productions and intelligent enough to serve the story."

Technology That Understands What the Story Needs

Sonilo is developing its Sound World Model, a multimodal AI system designed to connect video understanding, audio generation and temporal alignment. Rather than treating music and sound effects as isolated assets, the company is building technology that understands visual stories and generates audio in relation to the action, environment and narrative.

The production presented at Venice illustrated that approach across both music and sound effects.

For the score, Sonilo helped the production team explore contrasting instrumental textures within a character-driven musical framework. The finished soundtrack progressed from restrained elements beneath dialogue to deeper bass and additional layers as conflict approached. Rhythm and intensity increased with the action, culminating in a combination of synthesizers, orchestral elements and percussion. The result demonstrated how generated material can be developed into music with narrative structure, rather than simply placed beneath a sequence of images.

For sound effects, Sonilo analyzed scene content, movement, materials and narrative context before generating audio. Sound creators then reviewed and refined the results, corrected mismatches and added further creative direction. This scene-aware approach connects generation to a central requirement of filmmaking: sounds must belong to the world on screen, not merely sound convincing on their own.

"Film music is not everywhere in the film," said Shawn Song, CEO of Sonilo. "The model has to know when to start, when to stop, and when to leave room for the dialogue."

That is the technical ambition behind Sonilo's approach: audio generation that responds to what a scene means, not only what it contains.

Turning Generation Speed Into Creative Capability

The production also demonstrated how Sonilo's performance can expand creative exploration. According to the workflow presented at Venice, Sonilo reduced one initial music-exploration stage from approximately 10 hours to around 20 seconds. The comparison applies to that specific exploration stage, not to completion of the entire soundtrack.

The team used Sonilo to generate multiple musical and sound-effect directions, evaluate their emotional and narrative fit, and develop the strongest material through selection, combination, editing and professional post-production. This gave the project's composer and creative team a broader range of material to work with while preserving the decisions that shaped the final soundtrack.

For Sonilo, the opportunity is larger than making an existing task faster. The company aims to put more creative possibilities within reach: more musical directions to test, more sound palettes to explore and more opportunities to discover an approach that strengthens the film. Generation speed becomes valuable when it expands what a production can attempt and accomplish.

Building a Lasting Place for AI-Powered Music in Cinema

Sonilo's approach pairs technical ambition with respect for intellectual property and creative labor. "We respect knowledge, we respect IP, we respect effort. It should be common sense," Song said during the forum.

The company sees responsible development and professional collaboration as essential to building a lasting place in the film industry. Its goal is to advance audio technology that fits the realities of production, supports demanding creative work and develops alongside the filmmakers, composers and sound professionals who use it.

The Venice presentation offers a concrete example of that direction: Sonilo's generation capabilities working within a production process that combined composition, sound design and post-production to deliver a finished soundtrack.

For Sonilo, this is a foundation for a broader ambition: to make AI music and sound effects a meaningful part of professional filmmaking, with the capability to support increasingly ambitious stories. Its presence at Venice marks a step toward that future, demonstrated through the work itself.

About Sonilo

Sonilo is a Silicon Valley-based U.S. company developing multimodal audio AI for visual storytelling. The company is building the Sound World Model, designed to connect video understanding, music and sound-effects generation, and temporal alignment. Its technology supports filmmakers, creators and creative platforms across film, video, gaming and generative media.

About 10000 Parallel Universes

10000 Parallel Universes is TapNow's long-term international AI-native IP incubation initiative, designed to connect emerging creators with creative development, production support, international collaboration and distribution opportunities.

The initiative aims to explore how technology can amplify culturally diverse voices, expand access to filmmaking and help meaningful stories reach international audiences.
